BARRIER LAW.1: Creates a black, insubstantial wall up to 20'x20'x1" that light cannot pass into or through (i.e., it does not hinder movement, but it blocks vision). Note that this provides Full Soft Cover (see RMCL, Section 9.6). This will not block Darkvision, which does not require light to function.
BARRIER LAW.2: Creates a wall of dense churning air up to 10'x10'x3'. This wall requires 1 AP to cross, the pace of anyone moving through it at more than a Walk comes out with his pace reduced by one (e.g, a Run going in would be a Jog coming out), and attacks through the wall suffer a -50 penalty.
BARRIER LAW.3: As Shadow Wall I, except for duration.
BARRIER LAW.4: Creates a wall of water up to 10'x10'x1'. This wall requires 2 AP to cross, the pace of anyone moving through it at more than a Walk comes out with his pace reduced by two (e.g, a Run going in would be a Walk pace coming out) to a minimum of a Walk, and attacks through the wall suffer a -80 penalty.
BARRIER LAW.5: Creates a wall of wood up to 10'x20'x2". It can be burned through or chopped through or toppled if one end is not against a wall.
BARRIER LAW.6: Target lock becomes harder to pick or to force, giving a -20 penalty to any attempt to do so. Note that this will give a lock an RR against Heaven’s Key.
BARRIER LAW.7: Creates a wall of packed earth up to 10'x10'x (3' at base, 1' at top); it can be dug through only (20 man-rounds at top).
BARRIER LAW.8: Creates a wall of ice up to 10'x10'x (2' at base, 1' at top); it can be melted through or chipped through or toppled if not against a wall.
BARRIER LAW.9: Creates a sanctified entryway that will attempt to prevent “unholy” things from passing through the gate. The gate is defined by a closed loop that is either freestanding or at an entrance/exit point. A pair of pillars does not define a gate, because the top is open. Putting a crosspiece that connects that pair of pillars would close the loop and allow that to become a Sacred Gate. The gate does not need to have straight sides; a cave mouth could become a Sacred Gate. There is no size limit; the Gateway Arch in St. Louis could be made into a Sacred Gate. When an unholy being tries to pass through the Sacred Gate, it must make an RR. If it fails, then it takes an A Holy critical and is unable to pass through. If it succeeds, it passes through the gateway and the Sacred Gate spell is dispelled. If the Sacred Gate ever ceases to be a closed loop (e.g., the crosspiece falls off the pillars, leaving the top unconnected), the spell ends. It may also be canceled or dispelled normally.
BARRIER LAW.10: Opens a pit (up to 500 cubic feet in stone; 1000 cubic feet in earth or ice). The entire pit must be within 50' of caster and the pit can only be opened on a horizontal surface with an incline of less than 45°.
BARRIER LAW.11: As Airwall, except has a set duration of 1 min/level and does not require concentration.
BARRIER LAW.12: Creates a wall of non-precious stone up to 10'x10'x1'; it can be chipped through or toppled if not against a wall.
BARRIER LAW.13: As Waterwall, except caster need not concentrate and the duration is 1 minute per level.
BARRIER LAW.14: As Sacred Gate I, except for duration and it does a B Holy critical.
BARRIER LAW.15: As Woodwall, except duration is permanent.
BARRIER LAW.16: Unlocks one lock without triggering any associated traps. There is no chance of failure (other than normal spell failure), unless the lock has an RR.
BARRIER LAW.17: As Earthwall, except duration is permanent.
BARRIER LAW.18: As Icewall I, except size is up to 20'x20'x(4' at base, 2' at top).
BARRIER LAW.19: As Sacred Gate I, except for duration and it does a C Holy critical.
BARRIER LAW.20: As Stonewall, except duration is permanent and dimensions may be up to 20'x20'x1'.
BARRIER LAW.25: Fuses touching walls (seam can be up to 20' long) or fuses a section of stone blocks (up to 100 cubic feet).
BARRIER LAW.30: As any one of the lower level “wall” Spells on this list, except the wall can be curved up to a semicircle.
BARRIER LAW.35: As Sacred Gate I, except for duration and it does a D Holy critical.
BARRIER LAW.40: As Sacred Gate I, except for duration and it does an E Holy critical.
BARRIER LAW.50: Creates a transparent wall of “force” that is absolutely impassable by anyone or anything. It is up to 10'x20'x1".

CONCUSSION'S WAY.1: Any foreign matter causing an irritation (e.g., itching powder, poison ivy chemical, a splinter, allergen, or the like) is removed from the skin and exposed minor wounds of the target.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.3: An injury from burns, chemical burns, scalding, or frostbite incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, and the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.5: Target is relieved of 1 round of accumulated stun effects.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.6: As Light Exposure Relief, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.7: Reduces target’s concussion hit damage by 2 hits every round as long as caster concentrates; if caster is unconscious, this spell will operate on the caster without concentration.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.9: As Light Exposure Relief, except an injury incurring any penalty.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.12: As Regeneration I, except 4 hits per round.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.13: As Light Exposure Relief, except the recovery time is reduced from days to hours.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.16: As Medium Exposure Relief, except the recovery time is reduced from days to hours.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.17: As Stun Relief, except the range is 200'.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.18: As Regeneration I, except 6 hits per round.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.19: As Severe Exposure Relief, except the recovery time is reduced from days to hours.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.25: As Regeneration I, except 10 hits per round.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.30: Target is healed of all concussion hit damage.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.35: Up to one target per caster level is relieved of 1 round of stun effects.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.40: As Severe Exposure Relief, except the recovery time is reduced from days to rounds.
CONCUSSION'S WAY.50: Allows caster to heal all concussion hits in a number of targets equal to the level of the caster.

DETECTION MASTERY.1: Detects any active spell or active magical item from the Channeling realm; caster can concentrate on a different 5'R area each round.
DETECTION MASTERY.2: As Detect Channeling, except realm is Essence.
DETECTION MASTERY.3: As Detect Channeling, except realm is Mentalism.
DETECTION MASTERY.4: As Detect Channeling, except detects magic of any realm.
DETECTION MASTERY.5: As Detect Channeling, except detects living beings.
DETECTION MASTERY.6: As Detect Channeling, except detects curses on people or things.
DETECTION MASTERY.7: As Detect Channeling, except detects the presence of Undead.
DETECTION MASTERY.8: Analyzes one living being, giving race, age, and current state of health.
DETECTION MASTERY.9: As Detect Channeling, except detects invisible things; all attacks against something so detected are at -50.
DETECTION MASTERY.10: Gives the power (level) of the person or item or spell examined; caster can concentrate on a different target each round.
DETECTION MASTERY.11: Caster may analyze a poison to determine the exact effects and what antidotes are necessary. Poison may be on an item or in a being.
DETECTION MASTERY.12: As Detect Channeling, except it detects mechanical traps (but not unintentional hazards of any kind or magical protections).
DETECTION MASTERY.13: Detects any active magic on a target person or item. It also analyzes general spell type (in item or cast) and what profession cast or created it; in case of a person, it gives an exact profession.
DETECTION MASTERY.14: As Detect Channeling, except detects any holy or unholy creature/item, any items (including sacred texts) of religious significance, hallowed ground, and exceptionally pious individuals.
DETECTION MASTERY.15: As Detect Magic, except detects any spell that has been cast in the area examined going back 1 day/level of caster. Caster learns approximate time (within an hour) that a detected spell was cast.
DETECTION MASTERY.16: Identifies any woman or animal that is with child, at any stage of pregnancy. Caster learns the developmental stage, number, and sex(es) of the preborn. Caster can scan a different area each round.
DETECTION MASTERY.17: As Perceive Power, except range is 500' and everyone/everything in a five foot radius can be “perceived” at once, with a different area targeted each round.
DETECTION MASTERY.18: Gives the direction and distance to any specific object or place that the caster is familiar with or has had described in detail. The caster must have the dimensions of the object exact within 10% of actual size and know at least two other attributes that make the item unique (e.g., color, texture, weight, etc.) within range of the spell. Note that sometimes the caster must know more than two other attributes to make the item unique.
DETECTION MASTERY.19: As Detect Undead, except caster learns exact numbers, types, and levels of Undead, as well as whether or not each Undead is functioning independently or is currently controlled (including “mastered”) by another.
DETECTION MASTERY.20: As Detect Curse, except any curse may be analyzed for approximate level, effect, and required cure.
DETECTION MASTERY.25: As Life Typing, except also gives exact profession, degree of religious feeling, religious affiliation, experience level, and other pertinent details.
DETECTION MASTERY.30: Detects as any one of the lower level Detect spells. Thing detected and area of effect can both be changed each round.
DETECTION MASTERY.35: As Perceive Power, except every single item, spell, or individual within 500' of the caster that has “power” (a level) is “perceived” in an instant.
DETECTION MASTERY.40: As Life Analysis, except applies to 1 target/level within a range of 100'.
DETECTION MASTERY.50: As Location III, except range is 1 mile/ level.

LIGHT'S WAY.1: Beam of light (like a flashlight) springs from the caster’s palm; it has a 50' effective range. If the caster’s hand is closed into a fist, the light will “turn off”. If the caster’s fist is reopened before the end of the duration, the light will turn on again.
LIGHT'S WAY.2: Lights a 10'R area about the point touched. This spell may be cast onto a target as explained in Section 10.17.
LIGHT'S WAY.3: Causes a bright aura about the target, providing a more powerful appearance and subtracting 10 from all attacks on the target.
LIGHT'S WAY.4: As Light I, except 1 or 2 areas can be created with a total radius of 20' (e.g., one area of 20'R or two areas of 10’R) and the location(s) for the light(s) need not be touched.
LIGHT'S WAY.5: Causes a 10'R burst of intense light, all within are stunned (-50) for 1 round per 10 failure.
LIGHT'S WAY.6: As Aura, except it produces an extremely powerful appearance and subtracts 15 from all attacks.
LIGHT'S WAY.7: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT'S WAY.8: As Lights II, except up to three areas can be created with a total radius of 30'.
LIGHT'S WAY.9: Nullifies all magically created darkness in a 10'R, and lights that area as full daylight.
LIGHT'S WAY.10: As Light I, except caster can delay the spell up to 24 hours; it can be triggered by one of the following (decided by caster): elapsed time, specific movements, specific sounds, touch, etc.
LIGHT'S WAY.11: A ball of light one foot in diameter is shot from the palm of the caster: it will travel to the limit of Long range, explode (as a flare), burn with a bright light (as a flare), drift slowly to earth, and go out. An area equal to the range is lit if the flare can rise to its full range; drops 10'/round. It can be fired at a target as a Small Fire Bolt.
LIGHT'S WAY.12: As Lights II, except duration is one hour per level.
LIGHT'S WAY.13: As Lights II, except up to five areas can be created with a total radius of 50'.
LIGHT'S WAY.14: As Utterlight I, except up to three areas can be created with a total radius of 30'
LIGHT'S WAY.15: As Lights II, except up to ten areas can be created with a total radius of 100'.
LIGHT'S WAY.16: As Lights III, except duration is one hour per level.
LIGHT'S WAY.17: As Utterlight I, except up to five areas can be created with a total radius of 50'
LIGHT'S WAY.18: As Lights II, except total radius is 10' per level and this may be split between a number of areas equal to the caster’s level.
LIGHT'S WAY.19: As Lights V, except duration is one hour per level.
LIGHT'S WAY.20: As Aura, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
LIGHT'S WAY.25: Caster extends a finger and a 1" globe of blue-white light shoots out to the target location, then erupts in arcs of electricity in a 40' sphere. Attack is resolved on the Lightning Ball table as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT'S WAY.30: As Aura, except target seems like a minor god and the subtraction is 25.
LIGHT'S WAY.35: As True Aura, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
LIGHT'S WAY.40: As Mass Lights, except duration is one hour per level.
LIGHT'S WAY.50: As Utterlight I, except total radius is 10' per level and this may be split between a number of areas equal to the caster’s level.

LOFTY MOVEMENTS.1: Target gains a bonus of +30 for any Endurance rolls due to movement.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.2: Target can walk along narrow edges (down to 2" wide) that can support his weight. Maneuver rolls are not normally required.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.3: Target can walk along slick and/or wet surfaces as if on dry, secure footing.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.4: Target can walk along tree limbs as if on level ground.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.5: Target can walk on stone surfaces angled up to 60° as if on level ground.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.6: Target can walk on water as if on level dry ground. Water need not be perfectly still, but must be fairly calm.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.7: Target can merge into any organic material (alive or dead). While merged, target cannot move, perceive, or cast spells. When the target emerges from the material, it is possible to emerge from any side or face of the material, although this is limited to moving “through” no more than the target’s own body size plus two feet worth of material. The target can exit at any time up to the end of spell duration (at which time the target automatically emerges at the entrance point).
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.8: Caster “stores” a location for use with spells later on this list. While casting this spell, the caster must meditate for one hour in the location that will be stored. The caster can only have one sanctuary stored at a time. As long as this location remains “stored”, it will detect as a magical (i.e., “holy”) place.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.9: As Limbwalking, except target can move at up to a running pace (three times walking speed), without it being any more fatiguing than walking.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.10: Target can walk or run on stone surfaces angled up to 60° as if on level ground.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.11: As Waterwalking, except target can move at up to a running pace (three times walking speed), without it being any more fatiguing than walking.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.12: Target can walk on calm air. This spell only allows for horizontal movement. Vertical movement must be achieved by other means.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.13: Caster may return (as a teleport) to the caster’s stored sanctuary (from Store Sanctuary) so long as the sanctuary is no more than 1 mile away.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.14: Target can walk or run along slick and/or wet surfaces as if on dry, secure footing.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.15: As Merging Organic, except target can turn within the material and can perceive the outside world if within 6" of the surface.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.16: As Returning I, except the sanctuary can be up to 5 miles away.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.17: As Airwalking, except target can walk when winds do not exceed twice the caster’s level in miles per hour (i.e., when cast by a 20th level character, the target can walk in winds up to 40 mph). Wind does affect the target’s movement.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.18: As Airwalking, except target can run.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.19: As Returning I, except the sanctuary can be up to 10 miles away.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.20: As Great Merging Organic, except target may use self-targeted spells while merged.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.25: As Airrunning, except target can run up to thrice the normal speed (Running pace) on calm air without expending energy. This pace may be retained without any danger of Endurance checks related to movement during the duration.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.30: As Returning, except spell is instantaneous and the sanctuary can be up to 10 miles per level away.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.35: As Skywalking, except target can move at up to a running pace (three times walking speed), without it being any more fatiguing than walking.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.40: As Returning, except there is no distance limit.
LOFTY MOVEMENTS.50: Caster may return to the caster’s stored sanctuary (from Store Sanctuary) , stay up to 1 round per level, and then return to the point where he cast his spell (thus making it a round trip). Distance limit is 10 miles per level.

NATURE'S LAW.1: Caster learns nature, value, and history of one animal.
NATURE'S LAW.2: Caster learns nature, value, and history of one plant (that is not a magical herb).
NATURE'S LAW.3: Caster can understand the nature, origin, value, and use of any magical herb. If the plant is not a magical herb, no information will be related.
NATURE'S LAW.4: Caster learns nature, value, and history of one fungus.
NATURE'S LAW.5: Caster learns the nature, history, and origin of any one stone.
NATURE'S LAW.6: Caster can increase speed of growth for any one species of plant within a 10' radius by ten times normal growth rate.
NATURE'S LAW.7: Allows caster to understand and “speak” the language of any one animal species.
NATURE'S LAW.8: Caster learns the nature, value, origin, and eventual destination or outflow of one body of fresh water.
NATURE'S LAW.9: Allows caster to control the actions of any 1 animal.
NATURE'S LAW.10: Allows caster to monitor animate activity in the area (e.g., the caster will be aware of movements, subtle and overt). Caster cannot move while concentrating. Caster does not receive a picture of what is moving, just an awareness of the movement. This will allow distinguishing general size and shape of a moving object. Someone staying still, but breathing, will be detected, but only a very general idea of size would be determinable.
NATURE'S LAW.11: Allows caster to understand and “speak” the language of one plant species.
NATURE'S LAW.12: As Animal Mastery I, except caster can control up to three animals.
NATURE'S LAW.13: Caster can understand and/or visualize the thoughts and emotions of any one animal.
NATURE'S LAW.14: Caster can control the automatic and/ or mental processes of any one plant. Caster can also control the plant’s movements; this does not allow movement beyond normal allowances. If cast daily, this can be used to direct a plant’s growth into specific unusual shapes, so long as these would be naturally possible.
NATURE'S LAW.15: Caster can communicate with any one stone if it possesses any mental qualities (e.g., caster could speak to a holy stone which possesses some sort of intelligence).
NATURE'S LAW.16: Caster can grow an herb to sudden maturity by planting the proper seed; the herb is sterile and the growth takes 1-10 rnds.
NATURE'S LAW.17: Allows caster to understand and “speak” the language of one species of fungus.
NATURE'S LAW.18: As Animal Mastery I, except caster can control up to five animals.
NATURE'S LAW.19: As Plant Control I, except caster can control any three plants.
NATURE'S LAW.20: As Nature’s Awareness I, except that the radius is 500'.
NATURE'S LAW.25: Caster can understand and/or visualize the thoughts and emotions of any one animal, plant, fungus, stone, or dead organic object. The caster can change target each round.
NATURE'S LAW.30: As Animal Mastery I, except caster can control all animals of a given species within 10'R per level.
NATURE'S LAW.35: Caster can control the actions of up to five fungal life forms.
NATURE'S LAW.40: Caster is made aware of the ecological health of the area and anything that is causing significant ecological impact on the area (e.g., the water from the magic spring makes everything here grow fast, poison is leaching out from the pile of mine tailings, or the unicorns prevent disease from spreading through the wildlife).
NATURE'S LAW.50: As Animal Mastery I, except duration is permanent and concentration is not required. At a given time, the total number of levels of animals controlled by caster through use of this spell cannot exceed the caster’s own level.

PURIFICATIONS.1: This spell neutralizes abnormal diseases, poison, and other similar substances in one day’s worth of food and/or water. It will not neutralize a poison or similar substance that is a natural part of the food (e.g., it will not neutralize the natural poison in poisonous mushrooms).
PURIFICATIONS.2: Stops infection and/or spread of a non-magical disease in one target that has acquired the disease. Infected areas may continue to worsen. Thus, no further damage will occur in uninfected areas of the body, and healing may begin.
PURIFICATIONS.3: This spell perfectly preserves one day’s worth of food (by the caster’s dietary requirements) for one week, after which it will spoil normally.
PURIFICATIONS.4: Neutralizes any one non-magical poison in the system of one target. Damage already sustained is not cured.
PURIFICATIONS.5: Target gets an additional RR against any disease(s).
PURIFICATIONS.6: Target gets an additional RR against any poison(s).
PURIFICATIONS.7: As Food Preservation, except preserves one day’s worth of food per level of the caster.
PURIFICATIONS.8: As Disease Resistance I, except target gets 2 additional RRs.
PURIFICATIONS.9: As Poison Resistance I, except target gets 2 additional RRs.
PURIFICATIONS.10: Target is cured of one mental illness or malady. This will require a 1-10 day recovery period to take effect.
PURIFICATIONS.11: As Disease Resistance I, except target gets 3 additional RRs.
PURIFICATIONS.12: As Poison Resistance I, except target gets 3 additional RRs.
PURIFICATIONS.13: As Food Preservation, except preserves one day’s worth of food for one month.
PURIFICATIONS.14: Caster can remove any one disease from a target.
PURIFICATIONS.15: Caster can remove any one poison from a target.
PURIFICATIONS.16: As Mind Disease Cures, except cures one mental illness or malady in a number of targets up to the caster’s level.
PURIFICATIONS.17: As Food Preservation, except preserves one day’s worth of food for a year.
PURIFICATIONS.18: Caster can remove any one disease from a number of targets up to the caster’s level (e.g., an 18th level caster could remove leprosy from 18 targets).
PURIFICATIONS.19: Caster can remove any one poison from the systems of a number of targets up to the caster’s level.
PURIFICATIONS.20: Target is instantly cured of one mental illness or malady.
PURIFICATIONS.25: Any disease in the area is eliminated.
PURIFICATIONS.30: Any poison in the area is neutralized.
PURIFICATIONS.35: As Food Preservation, except preserves one day’s worth of food per level of the caster for a period of one year/level.
PURIFICATIONS.40: As Mind Disease Cures True, except cures one mental illness or malady in a number of targets up to the caster’s level.
PURIFICATIONS.50: Eliminates all poisons and/or diseases in the area.

SOUND'S WAY.1: Target is able to communicate basic ideas in a specific language (e.g., hungry, thirsty, bathroom, peace, etc.); equivalent to skill rank 2.
SOUND'S WAY.2: Creates a 1'R area into and out of which sound cannot travel. As discussed in Section 10.17, this spell can be cast on an individual target, which the spell will then follow; this target gains +25 to Stalking attempts, but likewise automatically fails any Perception attempts based on hearing alone and suffers a -50 to Perception rolls where hearing is a factor (e.g., to detect someone Stalking the target). Note that this does not interfere with spell-casting (the target can still speak, even yell, the sound is simply unable to leave the radius of the Quiet - certain spells like Ultrasonics may have their range limited to the interior of the Quiet radius, however).
SOUND'S WAY.3: Caster is able to communicate basic ideas in a specific language (e.g., hungry, thirsty, bathroom, peace, etc.); equivalent to skill rank 2.
SOUND'S WAY.4: Caster learns the origin and significance of any one sound that the caster has heard in the last minute.
SOUND'S WAY.5: Creates a plane (up to 20'x20') through which sound will not pass.
SOUND'S WAY.6: As Speech I, except target can communicate more complex concepts, although there is a good chance of misinterpretations; equivalent to skill rank 4.
SOUND'S WAY.7: As Quiet I, except radius is 10'.
SOUND'S WAY.8: As Quiet I, except 3 targets can be affected.
SOUND'S WAY.9: As Tongues I, except caster can communicate more complex concepts, although there is a good chance of misinterpretations; equivalent to skill rank 4.
SOUND'S WAY.10: As Soundwall I, except six such walls are created; each Soundwall must be connected to at least one other Soundwall.
SOUND'S WAY.11: As Quiet I, except 5 targets may be affected.
SOUND'S WAY.12: Creates a wordless sound (may resemble a human voice, it just cannot transmit words) that can be heard only by members of the caster’s faith. Sound will not have any direct effects, but may serve as a signal and as the spell name implies, it is often used as a signal to assemble for religious services.
SOUND'S WAY.13: As Sphere of Silence I, except radius is 50'.
SOUND'S WAY.14: Caster’s voice is made more pleasant and suitable for whatever task it is put to. The caster gains a +20 bonus to any vocal tasks (singing, oratory, etc.).
SOUND'S WAY.15: As Speech I, except target is reasonably fluent in the language. Target’s accent is imperfect, but there is only a slight chance of misinterpretation; equivalent to skill rank 6.
SOUND'S WAY.16: Caster can speak a language he already knows in any regional or subcultural dialect, accent, and/or slang as if that form was his normal way of speaking.
SOUND'S WAY.17: Target’s voice carries five times as far as normal.
SOUND'S WAY.18: Anyone speaking within the area of effect has his words scrabbled into nonsense; anyone hearing speech within the area of effect hears the words as nonsense. The only way two individuals within the area of effect can communicate through speech is if they both make their RRs.
SOUND'S WAY.19: As Tongues I, except caster is reasonably fluent in the language. Caster’s accent is imperfect, but there is only a slight chance of misinterpretation; equivalent to skill rank 6.
SOUND'S WAY.20: As Sphere of Silence I, except radius is 100'.
SOUND'S WAY.25: As Soundwall V, except as many Soundwalls as the caster’s level can be created.
SOUND'S WAY.30: As Quiet I, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
SOUND'S WAY.35: As Speech III, except target speaks the specified language like a native and the caster does not need to concentrate (duration is 1 min/level). Skill is equivalent to skill rank 8.
SOUND'S WAY.40: No sound can exist within the area of effect. It may be targeted on one being as its center, and if that being fails an RR, the radius of effect will travel with that being.
SOUND'S WAY.50: As Tongues I, except caster speaks the specified language like a native (equivalent to skill rank 8) and the duration is 10 minutes/level.

SPELL DEFENSE.1: Target gains a bonus of +5 to RRs against spells and a bonus of +5 to DB against elemental attacks.
SPELL DEFENSE.2: When the caster is a target of a spell from the Realm of Channeling, the “incoming” spell must first make an RR before the caster makes an RR. If the “incoming” spell passes the RR, it may target the caster of this spell normally; otherwise the incoming spell has no effect on this target. Being a “willing target” does not eliminate this effect, but the caster’s own spells do not need to make an RR. Note that the caster is considered to be a target of any spell which includes him in its area of effect or would “detect” him.
SPELL DEFENSE.3: As Protection I, except all beings within 10'R of target (sphere moves with target) get the benefits.
SPELL DEFENSE.4: As Cancel Channeling, except affects spells from the realm of Essence.
SPELL DEFENSE.5: As Protection I , except bonuses are +10.
SPELL DEFENSE.6: As Cancel Channeling, except affects spells from the realm of Mentalism.
SPELL DEFENSE.7: As Protection Sphere I, except bonuses are +10.
SPELL DEFENSE.8: Any active spell from the realm of Channeling that is on the target must make an RR. If the spell fails its RR, it is dispelled.
SPELL DEFENSE.9: Creates a shimmering shield in front of the caster: it provides a bonus to the caster’s RR or DB of +10 against all frontal Channeling spell attacks on the caster (force and elemental). If the caster takes an instantaneous action to do so, he can “deflect” one spell attack. This results in adding the caster’s ranks in this list to his RR or, for spells that use an attack table, to his DB (in addition to the basic bonus of 10 for having the Shield). Multiple deflections can be done in a single round, but each is a separate instantaneous action (costing 1 AP for every instantaneous action after the first).
SPELL DEFENSE.10: As Protection I, except bonuses are +15.
SPELL DEFENSE.11: As Channeling Shield, except it is effective only against Essence spells.
SPELL DEFENSE.12: As Dispel Channeling I, except it affects spells of the realm of Essence.
SPELL DEFENSE.13: As Channeling Shield, except it is effective only against Mentalism spells.
SPELL DEFENSE.14: As Protection I, except bonuses are +20.
SPELL DEFENSE.15: As Channeling Shield, except it is effective against any two of the three realms.
SPELL DEFENSE.16: As Dispel Channeling I, except it affects spells of the realm of Mentalism.
SPELL DEFENSE.17: As Protection I, except bonuses are +25.
SPELL DEFENSE.18: Dispels a curse if the curse fails an RR. The curse’s level is the level of the caster of the curse. If the curse is not dispelled, the caster cannot try again until he has gone up another level of experience.
SPELL DEFENSE.19: As Channeling Shield, except it is effective against all three realms.
SPELL DEFENSE.20: Target gets +50 to all RRs against Channeling spells.
SPELL DEFENSE.25: Target gets +50 to all RRs against Essence spells.
SPELL DEFENSE.30: Target gets +50 to all RRs against Mentalism spells.
SPELL DEFENSE.35: As Channeling Resistance, except for duration.
SPELL DEFENSE.40: As Channeling Resistance, except is effective against spells from two realms of the caster’s choice.
SPELL DEFENSE.50: As Channeling Resistance, except is effective against all three realms.

WEATHER WAYS.1: Caster may determine air temperature, humidity, barometric pressure, and wind speed. One round of concentration is required per piece of information.
WEATHER WAYS.2: Gives caster a 95% chance of predicting the time and type of rain (or other precipitation) by ±15 minutes over the next 24 hours.
WEATHER WAYS.3: Gives caster a 95% chance of predicting the high and low temperatures over the next 24 hours.
WEATHER WAYS.4: Caster has a 95% chance of correctly predicting time, type, and severity of weather over the next 24 hr period.
WEATHER WAYS.5: No rain, snow, sleet, hail, or fog will come closer than an inch from the caster or what the caster is wearing, allowing the caster to pass through a downpour and come out completely dry.
WEATHER WAYS.6: Caster causes a breeze to come forth which will drive out any gaseous matter (clouds, fog, poison gasses, etc.) and subtracts from all missile attacks (-10). Once set, the direction of the breeze will not change.
WEATHER WAYS.7: Caster causes fog to arise that obscures nearly all vision in and through the radius; treat as a heavy fog as described in RMCL, Section 15.7.
WEATHER WAYS.8: Disperses fog within the area of effect. If not all of a fog is dispersed (i.e., the fog covers a greater area than the area of effect for this spell), fog will refill the area of effect, reducing the cleared radius by 10' every 1-5 minutes (depending on the heaviness of the fog and ambient humidity).
WEATHER WAYS.9: All water within a 100'R is calmed; waves are cut by 20' in the center and less towards the perimeter. This will negate the effects of currents in the area of effect.
WEATHER WAYS.10: As Weather Prediction I, except that caster has a 95% chance of predicting weather over a 3-day period.
WEATHER WAYS.11: Caster causes rain or snow to fall (depending on temperature). The precipitation obscures vision into the radius (-25 to Perception) and modifies all missile attacks passing through part of the radius by -25.
WEATHER WAYS.12: Alerts the caster any time that the weather within the area of effect is altered by supernatural means.
WEATHER WAYS.13: As Weather Prediction I, except that caster has a 95% chance of predicting weather over a 5-day period.
WEATHER WAYS.14: Caster can adjust the temperature up or down by 18°F (10°C). Once the duration of the spell is over, the temperature will slowly adjust back to the ambient temperature (over the course of an hour).
WEATHER WAYS.15: Caster can control the speed and direction of the wind. Caster can increase or decrease wind speed by 1 mph per caster level (e.g., if the wind speed is normally 20 mph, a 15th level caster could alter the wind speed to between 5 and 35 mph). By directing the wind against missile attacks the caster can cause a -1 modification for each mph of wind speed. Note that caster can also control the direction of the flow of gases and/or clouds.
WEATHER WAYS.16: Caster can summon a dew (or frost, should the temperature be below freezing) the following morning.
WEATHER WAYS.17: Caster can control water movement. Caster can create magical barriers blocking water flow, but intangible to all else, within the limits of the spell. Caster can also control the flow of surface currents on a large body of water, providing up to 1 mph per caster level of current, which can carry boats or ships along.
WEATHER WAYS.18: Caster can make the skies clear of haze, precipitation, clouds, etc. This spell will not affect the wind.
WEATHER WAYS.19: As Weather Prediction I, except that caster has a 95% chance of predicting weather over a 30-day period.
WEATHER WAYS.20: Caster can summon rain of moderate intensity; the rain will obscure short-range vision (-25 to Perception and missile attack out to 100', -75 beyond 100').
WEATHER WAYS.25: Caster may use any of the lower level spells on this list, but with the effects covering a one mile radius.
WEATHER WAYS.30: Caster may call forth a storm of any type with maximum wind speeds equal to twice caster’s level in miles per hour, and intensity according to the caster’s desires. Effects will vary according to circumstance (and the GM’s discretion). For example, a 30th level caster could summon a lightning storm with intense rain and constant wind speeds of up to 60 mph: the GM may wish to have random rolls to determine possible lightning strikes vs. exposed targets.
WEATHER WAYS.35: Caster can cause lightning bolts to strike a region within range, with anyone in the area subject to a 25% chance of being targeted by a lightning bolt during any given round. The results are determined on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table, with the OB equal to the caster’s ranks in this list. This spell requires that there already be clouds in the sky. Any fumbles are resolved based on the clouds launching the lightning, not the caster.
WEATHER WAYS.40: Caster creates a tornado. This spell requires a cloudy sky and at least 20 mph winds. The tornado will be 15' in radius and will move 100' randomly each round that the caster does not concentrate. If the caster concentrates, he can control the movement of the tornado (up to 100' per round). The tornado is resolved on living things and structures as a Large Ram Attack with an OB equal to the caster’s ranks in this list, with an additional Grapple critical. If the tornado ever gets a 100% “grapple” on someone, it will pick him up and drop him from a height of 1-100'. The tornado will pick up and toss around small objects, raise dust and water, and the GM should call for breakage checks on any items he thinks may be threatened. Note that range is for initial formation only; tornado may travel any distance from caster once formed.
WEATHER WAYS.50: Caster may dictate the weather conditions in the area, modifying wind speeds by ±1 mph x level, and setting the level of precipitation, fog, cloud cover etc. Caster may call for shifts in the patterns as he concentrates, but the change will take at least 1 minute.

BLOOD LAW.1: Reduces target’s blood loss by up to 1 hit per round. Until the injury is actually treated by some means (e.g., Medicine maneuver or a Flesh Relief spell), the target cannot move or be moved without the bleeding resuming. Multiple Staunch Wound, Flowstop, Clotting, or Cut Repair spells may not be cast upon the same wound.
BLOOD LAW.2: As Staunch Wound I, except the caster may choose one option: reduce the bleeding by an additional 2 hits/round, or cause the wound to clot so that it is only at risk of reopening during the first hour and only if the target engages in activity more vigorous than walking.
BLOOD LAW.3: One poison or disease afflicting the target is reduced by one level of severity (e.g. from Extreme to Severe, or from Mild to cured), and, in the case of disease, anyone subsequently infected by the target gains a bonus of +20 on their RR.
BLOOD LAW.4: A flesh wound or skin/tissue injury that incurs a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, and the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll.
BLOOD LAW.5: Prevents the deterioration of 1 limb (even while severed); also requires the use of Limb Preservation from the Bone, Muscle, and Nerve spell lists.
BLOOD LAW.6: As Staunch Wound II, except two options may be chosen, including multiple reductions in the amount of bleeding. If the clotting option is selected twice, bleeding is instantly stopped with no danger of reopening. In addition, one option may be spent to split the effect of the spell between multiple bleeding injuries (e.g., if the reduction will be 3 hits per round, it may be applied to reduce bleeding of one wound by 1 hit per round and another by 2 hits per round).
BLOOD LAW.7: Target receives an additional RR vs either poison or disease, as specified by the caster at the time of casting.
BLOOD LAW.8: As Light Flesh Relief, except a wound incurring a penalty up to -40.
BLOOD LAW.9: As Staunch Wound III, except three options may be chosen.
BLOOD LAW.10: As Medium Flesh Relief, except a wound incurring any penalty.
BLOOD LAW.11: A flesh wound or skin/tissue injury that incurs a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll, and the recovery period is reduced to hours rather than days.
BLOOD LAW.12: Caster may reattach one severed limb. The Joining spells from the Bone, Muscle, and Nerve spell lists must be cast for the limb to be functional. The recovery time is 1-10 days.
BLOOD LAW.13: As Staunch Wound III, except four options may be chosen.
BLOOD LAW.14: As Light Flesh Healing, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
BLOOD LAW.15: As Staunch Wound III, except five options may be chosen.
BLOOD LAW.16: Removes any one disease from the target.
BLOOD LAW.17: As Light Flesh Healing, except an injury incurring any penalty.
BLOOD LAW.18: Removes any one poison from the target.
BLOOD LAW.19: As Staunch Wound III, except seven options may be chosen.
BLOOD LAW.20: Removes all disease from one target/ level.
BLOOD LAW.25: As Joining, except recovery is instantaneous.
BLOOD LAW.30: As Light Flesh Healing, except the recovery period is reduced to rounds.
BLOOD LAW.35: Removes all poison from one target/ level.
BLOOD LAW.40: As Medium Flesh Healing, except the recovery period is reduced to rounds.
BLOOD LAW.50: As Severe Flesh Healing, except the recovery period is reduced to rounds.

BONE LAW.1: An injury to cartilage incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, and the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll.
BONE LAW.2: Caster acquires complete understanding of any bone damage, including the tools and methods required for healing. Caster does not receive the skill or power necessary to perform the cure, but this diagnostic does provide a +20 bonus to treatment if supervised by the caster. Alternatively, this spell can be used to identify bones, including the approximate age, species, sex, and in some cases cause of death.
BONE LAW.3: As Light Cartilage Relief, except a bone injury.
BONE LAW.4: Target’s bones become flexible, granting +50 to escape maneuvers.
BONE LAW.5: Allows caster to prevent deterioration of one limb (even while severed); requires use of the Blood, Muscle, and Nerve Limb Preservation spells as well.
BONE LAW.6: As Light Cartilage Relief, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
BONE LAW.7: As Medium Cartilage Relief, except a bone injury.
BONE LAW.8: Target’s bones are strengthened, and the injury penalty incurred by any bone injury sustained within the duration is halved. Injuries suffered before the spell was cast are not affected.
BONE LAW.9: As Medium Cartilage Relief, except an injury incurring any penalty.
BONE LAW.10: As Medium Cartilage Relief, except a bone injury incurring any penalty.
BONE LAW.11: A bone injury is temporarily braced and immobilized such that the injury penalty from that injury is halved for the duration.
BONE LAW.12: Caster may reattach one severed limb. The Joining spell from the Blood, Muscle, and Nerve spell lists must be cast for the limb to be functional. The recovery time is 1-10 days.
BONE LAW.13: An injury to cartilage incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll and the recovery period is reduced to hours rather than days.
BONE LAW.14: As Light Cartilage Healing, except for a bone injury.
BONE LAW.15: As Light Cartilage Healing, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
BONE LAW.16: As Medium Cartilage Healing, except for a bone injury.
BONE LAW.17: As Strong Bones I, except the duration is 10 minutes per level.
BONE LAW.18: As Light Cartilage Healing, except an injury incurring any penalty.
BONE LAW.19: As Severe Cartilage Healing, except for a bone injury.
BONE LAW.20: Target’s bones are greatly strengthened, granting a physical RR to prevent any new injury penalties incurred from bone injuries.
BONE LAW.25: As Joining, except recovery is instantaneous.
BONE LAW.30: As Medium Cartilage Healing, except the recovery time is reduced to rounds.
BONE LAW.35: As Medium Bone Healing, except the recovery time is reduced to rounds.
BONE LAW.40: Any new bone injury suffered by the target will not result in any injury penalty. Other effects of the attack (hits, stun, etc.) are not prevented by this spell.
BONE LAW.50: Caster can use any lower level spell (on this list) once per round.

CALM SPIRITS.1: Caster is placed in a state of calm. This provides a +25 RR bonus against Fear or any spells that provoke an emotional response, a +10 bonus to any maneuvers that benefit from calm (including the use of missile weapons), while giving a -15 penalty to any activity to which calm is detrimental (e.g., most moving maneuvers above a walking pace, melee combat, thrown weapons)
CALM SPIRITS.2: Target will take no aggressive/offensive action and will fight only if attacked.
CALM SPIRITS.3: Target will not be able to rise as undead or house any animating spirit or otherwise be made to occupy a state other than peaceful death or true resurrection that returns the body to life and rehouses the soul.
CALM SPIRITS.4: As Calm I, except 2 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.5: Humanoid target has its Action Points per round reduced by 3 (i.e., normally, the target will have 1 AP each round).
CALM SPIRITS.6: As Calm I, except 3 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.7: As Restful Spirit I, except for duration.
CALM SPIRITS.8: As Calm I, except 4 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.9: As Calm l, except 5 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.10: Caster can calm (as Calm I) a number of animals equal to the caster’s level.
CALM SPIRITS.11: Any target has its Action Points per round reduced by 3 (i.e., normally, the target will have 1 AP each round).
CALM SPIRITS.12: As Calm I, except that 10 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.13: As Hold Kind I, except 3 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.14: The caster enters a deep relaxing meditation from which he cannot be woken until a specified time has passed (up to the duration of the spell). While meditating the caster regains Hits and PP at twice the normal rate and receives +50 to any Meditation maneuvers.
CALM SPIRITS.15: All targets in radius must resist or they are calmed (as Calm I).
CALM SPIRITS.16: As True Hold I, except 2 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.17: As Restful Spirit I, except for duration.
CALM SPIRITS.18: [RR Mod.: -20] As Mass Animal Calm I, except RRs are modified by -20 and the range is 10'/lvl.
CALM SPIRITS.19: As Hold Kind I, except 5 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.20: [RR Mod.: -20] As Calm I, except that 20 targets may be affected.
CALM SPIRITS.25: [RR Mod.: -20] As Calm I, except that calmness lasts for 1 day/level.
CALM SPIRITS.30: [RR Mod.: -20] As Calm I, except that caster can calm a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
CALM SPIRITS.35: As Hold Kind I, except that caster can affect a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
CALM SPIRITS.40: As True Hold I, except that caster can affect a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
CALM SPIRITS.50: As Calm I, except that calmness is permanent.

CREATIONS.1: Creates (out of thin air) a cloth up to 3'x6' in area, the cloth is made of typical local textile materials (of an inexpensive kind), suitable for use as either a blanket or as a simple garment.
CREATIONS.2: Allows caster to go without food or water and not suffer damage (i.e., provides nutrition and water for 1 day).
CREATIONS.3: Caster can produce sufficient water in any available receptacle to supply a being for one day.
CREATIONS.4: Caster can produce sufficient food from the surrounding area to feed one hearty appetite for one day.
CREATIONS.5: Allows caster to set a fire of 1'R; fire will then last as long as there is fuel. A target in the 1'R will take an A Heat critical. Caster may only target a specific location, not an individual, with this spell.
CREATIONS.6: Caster can produce a loaf of blessed bread that weighs half a pound and will support one being for one day; the loaf will lose potency in one month.
CREATIONS.7: As Water Production I, except caster can produce three days of water.
CREATIONS.8: As Food Production I, except caster can produce sufficient food to feed three beings for one day.
CREATIONS.9: Allows caster to enhance the efficacy of any one herb (growing or dead) with healing or durational effects. For healing herbs, recovery rolls receive an extra +25 bonus. For herbs with a durational effect, the duration is doubled. This spell may be employed only once per herb.
CREATIONS.10: As Water Production I, except caster can produce five days supply of water.
CREATIONS.11: As Food Production I, except caster can produce sufficient food to feed five beings for one day.
CREATIONS.12: As Nutrient Conjure I, except caster can produce three loaves of blessed bread.
CREATIONS.13: Caster can double the potency of any one herb (growing or dead). This has the effect of halving the quantity of herb needed for a full dose, i.e. if a normal dose requires one full leaf to be effective, following this spell, only half a leaf would be required. This spell may be employed only once/herb, and may not be combined with Herb Enhancement.
CREATIONS.14: Caster creates a plain tent, capable of sheltering up to four persons comfortably (or six uncomfortably) against local weather conditions. At the end of this spell, the tent simply disappears.
CREATIONS.15: Caster can produce a plant up to 10' in height and/or width; plant must be representative of the region.
CREATIONS.16: As Water Production I, except caster can create one day of water per level (e.g., a 17th level Cleric could create 17 days of water).
CREATIONS.17: As Food Production I, except caster can produce sufficient food to feed a number of beings equal to the caster’s level.
CREATIONS.18: As Herb Mastery, except caster may enhance one herb per level. Herbs must all be of the same type.
CREATIONS.19: As Tent of the Gods, except creates a log cabin suitable for 12 persons in comfort or 20 persons uncomfortably.
CREATIONS.20: Caster can create an animal representative of the surrounding region and weighing no more than 10 lbs; animal will be friendly to caster.
CREATIONS.25: As Nutrient Conjure I, except caster can produce a number of loaves of blessed bread equal to the caster’s level.
CREATIONS.30: As Lesser Plant Production, except that caster can create one plant with a height and/or width of one foot per caster level (e.g., a 30th level could produce a 30' high tree with a 30' maximum width); plant must be representative of the local area.
CREATIONS.35: As Tent of the Gods, except creates a stone tower suitable for 16 persons in comfort or 30 uncomfortably. This is a defensive structure, with a barred door and whatever standard structural design the caster’s culture would use for a fortified stone tower.
CREATIONS.40: As Greater Plant Production, except plant need not be native to the local area.
CREATIONS.50: As Lesser Animal Production, except that caster can produce an animal with a maximum weight of one pound per caster level. The animal must be a native of the area.

LOCATING WAYS.1: Caster knows which way is up and where the cardinal directions (north, east, south, and west) lie.
LOCATING WAYS.2: When faced with a choice about which the caster has little or no information (e.g., which corridor leads to the wine cellar), the caster may cast this spell and the Gamemaster will determine which choice the caster actually makes, biasing the choice favorably by 25% (e.g., if there are two choices, roll 1-100: correct on 26-100, incorrect on 01-25). The caster must have a limited number of options (i.e., finite and countable). After the spell is cast, the caster may not cast another Guess for the same information until his experience level has increased.
LOCATING WAYS.3: Caster learns the location(s) of any “path(s)” within 100'; gives the nearest point on each path, but not the path’s course.
LOCATING WAYS.4: Caster is subtly directed (by hints and clues) towards a specific destination (within 100'/lvl) by guidance from the caster’s deity. The exact form of the guidance may vary from deity to deity (e.g., a deity of water might leave hints in the rocks of a stream, etc.). For the duration of this spell, the caster must concentrate on following the guidance to perceive the clues.
LOCATING WAYS.5: Gives the direction and distance to any specific object or place with which the caster is familiar or has had described in detail. The caster must have the dimensions of the object exact within 10% of actual size and know at least two other attributes that make the item unique (e.g., color, texture, weight, etc.) within range of the spell. Note that sometimes the caster must know more than two other attributes to make the item unique, although the Tag spells allow one to shortcut this process.
LOCATING WAYS.6: As Pathfinding I, except range is 300'.
LOCATING WAYS.7: Caster places a distinctive “tag” on the aura of a person or item, which will qualify as a unique descriptive marker for purposes of Location (e.g., the caster could cast Tag I on a common coin and Location would be able to pick it out amongst all the various similar coins).
LOCATING WAYS.8: As Location I, except range is 300'.
LOCATING WAYS.9: As Pathfinding I, except range is 500'.
LOCATING WAYS.10: As Location I, except range is 500'.
LOCATING WAYS.11: Caster can remember an exact route that the caster has previously traveled regardless of whether or not the original journey was made with the caster’s normal sensory abilities active (e.g., a 12th level caster could remember the course of 12 hours of a trip even if blindfolded during that time). To be effective, this spell must be cast within one month of the journey.
LOCATING WAYS.12: As Pathfinding I, except range is 1 mile.
LOCATING WAYS.13: As Guidance, except the form of the guidance is that of an animal companion sent by the deity. The caster can follow the animal to a specific destination.
LOCATING WAYS.14: As Tag I, except for duration.
LOCATING WAYS.15: Caster can locate any 1 object the caster can describe, if indeed it exists and is in range (e.g., caster could describe a type of mace he had never seen or heard of). Description does not need to be unique. If item description is not unique, the spell locates the nearest item matching the description.
LOCATING WAYS.16: As Location I, except range is 1 mile.
LOCATING WAYS.17: As Pathfinding I, except range is 10 miles.
LOCATING WAYS.18: As Find Item I, except range is 300'.
LOCATING WAYS.19: As Tag I, except for duration.
LOCATING WAYS.20: As Location I, except range is 20 miles.
LOCATING WAYS.25: As Pathfinding I, except range is 1 mile/level and exact routes within the range are ascertained.
LOCATING WAYS.30: As Location I, except range is 1 mile/level.
LOCATING WAYS.35: As Tag I, except for duration.
LOCATING WAYS.40: As Location True, except it locates a person. Caster must still be able to provide a unique description.
LOCATING WAYS.50: As Find Item I, except range is 100'/level.

LORE.1: Allows caster virtually total recall of any conversation or writing encountered within a period of days equal to caster’s level.
LORE.2: Detects any evil being or any item created by evil or long used by a very evil person; caster can concentrate on a different 5'R area each round.
LORE.3: As Detect Evil, except detects curses on people or things.
LORE.4: As Detect Evil, except caster can detect the emotion of hatred, in the living mind or in an object forged with great malice. Any object or being “Of Slaying” will show as being filled with hate.
LORE.5: Caster can ascertain the origin point and nature of any one “holy item” that is not “of darkness” or “of evil”. This will not give specific capabilities.
LORE.6: Caster may analyze a poison to determine the exact effects and what antidotes are necessary. Poison may be on an item or in a being.
LORE.7: Caster can detect any extreme emotion (e.g., hatred, love, sadness, fear, etc.). In addition, the caster learns which emotion(s) the target is feeling. If there are no extremes of emotion (i.e., only normal feelings), nothing is detected. Caster may change the spell’s target each round.
LORE.8: Caster can determine the nature and type of any one living target. This will not ascertain the target’s personal traits or capabilities, but the caster will know the normal abilities associated with the target’s species.
LORE.9: Caster can recall appropriate quotations (from the caster’s own memory) which will both help make the caster’s point and be relevant to the target audience. This adds +15 to any maneuver involving persuasive speaking or writing and +10 to any maneuver involving artistic speaking or writing, but only applies if the caster has at least one rank in a Lore skill relevant to the audience.
LORE.10: Caster can determine nature and origin of any one curse, including the name of the one who bequeathed it.
LORE.11: As Light Lore I, except caster can ascertain the origin point and nature of any one item “of darkness” or “of evil.”
LORE.12: As Light Lore I, except that caster can ascertain the origin point and nature of any two “holy items” or caster can determine the nature, origin point, and the exact significance of any one “holy item.”
LORE.13: Caster can determine the nature and origin of active hatred found within any 1 target (inanimate or animate); the degree and other details of such hatred can also be acquired. Any objects or beings “Of Slaying” will show as hating their target type.
LORE.14: As Light Lore I, except caster can ascertain the origin point and nature of any one item that is neither holy nor unholy in nature.
LORE.15: As Hate Analysis, except caster can determine the nature and origin of any extreme emotion(s) in the target.
LORE.16: Caster can read any text (as if possessing eight ranks in the appropriate written language), although this spell does not assist in understanding cultural context, cultural references, implications, etc.
LORE.17: As Light Lore I, except that caster can ascertain the origin point and nature of any three “holy items” or caster can determine the age, origin point, name of the creator, and nature of any one “holy item.” Caster also learns item’s specific capabilities.
LORE.18: As Light Lore II, except that it can only be used on items “of darkness” or “of evil.”
LORE.19: Caster can ascertain exact nature, origin, purpose, history, and specific capabilities of any one “holy item”; this allows caster to visualize all who have possessed the item.
LORE.20: As Light Lore III, except that it can be used only on items “of evil” or “of darkness.”
LORE.25: As Life Lore, except caster can determine personal traits and capabilities of any one target.
LORE.30: As White Lore, except it can only be used on an item “of darkness” or “of evil.”
LORE.35: As Light Lore III, except it can only be used on items that are neither holy nor unholy in nature.
LORE.40: As Life Lore True, except caster determines the personal traits and capabilities of one target per caster level.
LORE.50: As White Lore, except caster can acquire the information on all “holy items” within 100'.

MOUNTED WAYS.1: Creates a bond between the caster and an animal, making the animal the caster’s “mount” for the purposes of other spells on this list. It is only possible to have one “mount” at a time. The target of this spell must be a typical mount of the caster’s culture (usually a horse or camel).
MOUNTED WAYS.2: Caster telepathically summons his mount, which will come to him as quickly as possible.
MOUNTED WAYS.3: Caster gains a +5 bonus to his Riding skill.
MOUNTED WAYS.4: The next maneuver by the mount receives a +20 bonus.
MOUNTED WAYS.5: Caster and mount make RRs using the higher of their two levels and the higher of their RR bonuses (e.g., if the mount has the higher level and the caster has the better RR bonus, they get the benefit of both).
MOUNTED WAYS.6: As Riding I, except bonus is +10.
MOUNTED WAYS.7: Mount gains the benefits of AT 4, but without any encumbrance or armor penalties since no armor is actually worn. This provides full suit coverage (i.e., treat the mount as having limb armor and a helm).
MOUNTED WAYS.8: As Select Mount, except that the target may be any rideable animal or other creature that the GM considers a suitable mount (e.g., the GM may wish to allow use of this list with a hippogriff mount).
MOUNTED WAYS.9: As Riding I, except bonus is +15.
MOUNTED WAYS.10: As Call Mount, except for range.
MOUNTED WAYS.11: As Augment Mount I, except bonus is +40.
MOUNTED WAYS.12: As Riding I, except bonus is +20.
MOUNTED WAYS.13: Restores all lost hits and treats any Light injuries (penalties up to -20) suffered by the mount. Recovery time for injuries takes normal time as described in RMCL Chapter 13.
MOUNTED WAYS.14: As Armor Mount I, except AT is 7.
MOUNTED WAYS.15: As One Spirit, except it also has the effect that any spells the caster casts during the duration of this spell that are “self” spells also affect the mount.
MOUNTED WAYS.16: As Riding I, except bonus is +25.
MOUNTED WAYS.17: As Augment Mount I, except bonus is +60.
MOUNTED WAYS.18: As Heal Mount I, except treats Medium injuries (penalties up to -40) as well. Recovery time is as described in RMCL, but convert days to hours.
MOUNTED WAYS.19: As Armor Mount I, except AT is 10.
MOUNTED WAYS.20: As Riding I, except bonus is +30.
MOUNTED WAYS.25: As One Soul, except it also has the effect that any Utility spells cast on the caster of this spell also affect the mount.
MOUNTED WAYS.30: As Augment Mount I, except bonus is +100.
MOUNTED WAYS.35: As Heal Mount I, except treats all injury short of death (will heal fatal damage so long as mount is still alive). Recovery time is as described in RMCL, but convert days to minutes.
MOUNTED WAYS.40: Caster and mount move as one, giving them both a +25 OB to all physical attacks (i.e., not spell) and +10 DB to attacks of which they are aware. This bonus does not apply if one of the duo is no longer fully aware and active (e.g., when one of them is stunned).
MOUNTED WAYS.50: During the duration of this spell, the mount needs no rest, sleep, food, or water. Its hunger and thirst do not grow, nor can it experience fatigue (i.e., it automatically makes any Endurance rolls). Hunger, thirst, and tiredness will begin to increase normally after the end of this spell.

MUSCLE LAW.1: Target receives a +10 bonus to all Jumping and Climbing maneuvers.
MUSCLE LAW.2: An injury to muscle or tendons incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, and the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll.
MUSCLE LAW.3: Target is not fatigued by moving at a walk or jog pace.
MUSCLE LAW.4: As Light Muscle Relief, except injuries incurring a penalty up to -40.
MUSCLE LAW.5: Allows caster to prevent deterioration of one limb (even while severed); requires use of the Blood, Bone, and Nerve Limb Preservation spells as well.
MUSCLE LAW.6: Target gains a +5 Strength bonus, granting +5 to most skills involving strength (+10 melee OB).
MUSCLE LAW.7: As Light Muscle Relief, except injuries incurring any penalty.
MUSCLE LAW.8: Target is not fatigued by moving on the ground or in water up to a run pace.
MUSCLE LAW.9: An injury to muscle or tendons incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll and the recovery period is reduced to hours rather than days.
MUSCLE LAW.10: Target drops anything currently held and takes a -20 to any maneuver attempted this round.
MUSCLE LAW.11: As Severe Muscle relief, except it treats every muscle and tendon injury in the target.
MUSCLE LAW.12: Caster may reattach one severed limb. The Joining spell from the Bone, Blood, and Nerve spell lists must be cast for the limb to be functional. The recovery time is 1-10 days.
MUSCLE LAW.13: A random limb is in intense pain and the joint locks, rendering the limb unusable. A moving bipedal target afflicted with a leg lock will fall down; a target with an arm lock will drop anything in that hand.
MUSCLE LAW.14: As Light Muscle Healing, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
MUSCLE LAW.15: Target regenerates any one tendon. The recovery time is 1-10 hours.
MUSCLE LAW.16: Target will not accumulate any additional fatigue penalties for the duration.
MUSCLE LAW.17: As Light Muscle Healing, except an injury incurring any penalty.
MUSCLE LAW.18: Target regenerates any one muscle (other than the heart). The recovery time is 1-10 hours.
MUSCLE LAW.19: As Strength I, except the bonus is +15 (resulting in +30 for melee OB).
MUSCLE LAW.20: As Light Muscle Healing, except the recovery period is reduced to rounds.
MUSCLE LAW.25: As Joining, except recovery is instantaneous.
MUSCLE LAW.30: As Strength I, except the bonus is +20 (resulting in +40 for melee OB).
MUSCLE LAW.35: As Light Muscle Healing True, except an injury incurring any penalty.
MUSCLE LAW.40: Target regenerates all tendons and muscles in his body (other than the heart). The recovery time is 1-10 hours.
MUSCLE LAW.50: All injuries to muscle or tendons are cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll and the recovery period is reduced to rounds rather than days.

NERVE & ORGAN LAW.1: Diagnoses target’s wounds, injuries, and diseases allowing a +20 bonus to all Medicine maneuvers made by the caster to treat the target’s diagnosed condition(s). Caster can take a round to advise someone else on treating the target, providing a +10 bonus to treat the target.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.2: Target becomes completely infertile for the spell’s duration.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.3: An injury to an organ (e.g. eye, ear, liver but not the brain or nerves) incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, and the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.4: Target is at -30 for all actions.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.5: Allows caster to prevent deterioration of one limb (even while severed); requires use of the Blood, Bone, and Muscle Limb Preservation spells as well.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.6: As Light Organ Relief, but an injury incurring a penalty up to -40. This can be used to cure most causes of infertility (if the requisite organs are still present).
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.7: One of target’s natural senses (e.g. vision, hearing, touch) is honed and perfected for the duration. Perception maneuvers based exclusively on that sense gain a +20 bonus, while Perception that involves that sense and others gain a +10 bonus.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.8: Target’s heart will start beating after having stopped. This does not repair any heart disease or damage that caused the initial stoppage.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.9: An injury to the brain or nerves incurring a penalty up to -20 is cleaned, protected, and bound as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, and the target receives a +50 bonus on their recovery roll.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.10: Target can see twice as far through fog, mist, water, or other semi-transparent substances that would otherwise reduce their range of vision.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.11: As Light Organ Relief, but an injury incurring any penalty.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.12: Caster may reattach one severed limb. The Joining spell from the Bone, Blood, and Muscle spell lists must be cast for the limb to be functional. The recovery time is 1-10 days.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.13: An injury to an organ incurring a penalty up to -20 is treated as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, the target receives +50 bonus on their recovery roll, and recovery time is reduced to hours rather than days.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.14: Target comes out of a coma or unconsciousness caused by injury, disease, poison, spell, or spell failure. Process takes 1-10 hours and target is at -50 to Endurance rolls for 1-10 days.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.15: As Light Organ Healing, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.16: An injury to the brain or nerves incurring a penalty up to -20 is treated as effectively as if a successful Medicine maneuver was performed, the target receives +50 bonus on their recovery roll, and recovery time is reduced to hours rather than days.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.17: Target regains function in one sensory organ, so long as that sensory organ has not been completely destroyed (in which case Organ Regeneration is required). Recovery time is instantaneous.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.18: As Severe Organ Relief, except the recovery time is reduced to hours rather than days.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.19: Caster can cure any paralysis problem. The recovery time is 1-10 days. Treat as -100 injury for progress of recovery.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.20: As Light Nerve Healing, except an injury incurring a penalty up to -40.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.25: As Joining, except recovery is instantaneous.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.30: As Light Nerve Healing, except an injury incurring any penalty.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.35: Target will regenerate any one organ (external or internal) other than the brain or nerves. The recovery time is 1-10 hours.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.40: As Paralysis Cures, except recovery is instantaneous.
NERVE & ORGAN LAW.50: Target will regenerate his brain. Spell must be cast before target dies. Target will be in a “healing coma” while brain grows back, and memories may be lost depending on the severity of the damage. Recovery time is 1-10 days.

SYMBOLIC WAYS.1: Caster learns what spell is emplaced within one Symbol within 50'. The Symbol will not be triggered (unless specifically created to be triggered by an Analyze Symbol spell).
SYMBOLIC WAYS.2: This spell “primes” the next spell cast by the caster – that spell is treated as if it were instantaneous. The PP cost of this spell is equal to the highest level that the caster wants to have primed. For example, if the caster wants any fourth (or lower) level spell to be treated as instantaneous, this spell will cost 4 PP. In addition, when casting this spell, the caster must pray for one minute per PP spent (e.g., if the caster spends 4 PP on this spell, he must pray for 4 minutes before the spell is completed.) The effects of this spell end when the caster casts his next spell (even if the next spell does not benefit from this spell due to being of too high a level or already an instantaneous spell).
SYMBOLIC WAYS.3: Caster can remove one Symbol I (an emplaced 1st level spell). The Symbol’s RR is based on the level of the spell in the Symbol spell (the target level) and the level of the Unsymbol spell (the attack level).
SYMBOLIC WAYS.4: Caster can emplace one 1st level spell on an inanimate, non-mobile slab of stone (block, piece, etc.) weighing at least 2,000 pounds. Only one Symbol may be placed on each continuous slab. The stone may not be moved appreciably without destroying the Symbol. Within one minute, the spell to be emplaced must also be cast (within 10'). A Symbol can be triggered (once per day) by one of the following (decided by caster): time period, specified movements, specified sounds, touch, reading, violent actions in the area, etc. The triggering range is normally the range of the emplaced spell or 10' (whichever is greater). The effective level of the embedded spell (for the purposes of RRs, Duration, etc.) is the level of the highest level spell the Symbol can hold. For example, a first level spell placed in a Symbol using Symbol I is cast at 1st level (regardless of the level of the original caster), while a first level spell place using Symbol VII is cast at 7th level. If the spell is an elemental attack, the OB is normally +0. However, the attack can be focused on a location (as opposed to simply the person who triggers the symbol); in this case, the OB is +50. The Symbol is usually visible, but is only required to be visible if reading is the trigger.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.5: This spell must be cast on a Symbol that has already been triggered this day. Once this spell is cast on the Symbol, the Symbol is recharged and can be triggered again. A given caster cannot recharge the same Symbol more than once per day, but one caster may recharge any number of Symbols and a Symbol may be recharged by multiple casters.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.6: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-II may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.7: As Symbol I, except a 1st-2nd level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.8: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-V may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.9: As Symbol I, except a 1st-3rd level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.10: As Analyze Symbol, except caster learns what spells are emplaced in all Symbols within a 50'R.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.11: As Symbol I, except a 1st-5th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.12: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-VI may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.13: As Symbol I, except a 1st-6th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.14: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-VII may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.15: As Symbol I, except a 1st-7th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.16: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-VIII may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.17: As Symbol I, except a 1st-8th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.18: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-X may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.19: As Symbol I, except a 1st-9th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.20: As Symbol I, except a 1st-10th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.25: This spell allows for the creation of random magic items. See Treasure Law, Section 4.4.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.30: As Unsymbol I, except a Symbol I-X or a Lord Symbol may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.35: As Symbol I, except a 1st-20th level spell may be emplaced.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.40: As Unsymbol I, except any Symbol may be removed.
SYMBOLIC WAYS.50: As Symbol I, except a spell with a level up to half that of the caster (e.g., a 50th level caster can emplace a 25th level spell) may be emplaced.

CHANNELS.1: When this spell is cast, up to four fluid ounces of clean, clear water are transformed into holy water. This spell takes one hour to cast. If the water is not placed into a clean receptacle, its holy nature is ruined.
CHANNELS.2: Caster points his arm (elbow locked and fist clenched) at the target and channels raw power from his power source (usually a deity). The target of the spell may take no aggressive/offensive action, and will only fight if attacked.
CHANNELS.3: When this spell is cast, the 1st level spell that the caster begins to cast (or prepare) the next round will be “channeled” to another spell user of the Channeling realm. The “channeled” spell is transmitted to the other spell user when it would normally take effect, and must be used by the receiving spell user immediately or delayed as described in Section 4.8 (treating the receiving spell user as the caster of the spell). All normal restrictions on the transmitted spell apply. The caster of the Channels spell must be able to see the receiver or know exactly where the receiver is (direction and distance or specific place). The receiver must know exactly when the spell is coming (but need not know what the spell sent is). For example, if a Cleric was at a certain altar at a certain time (midnight of full moon) ready to receive a spell; then another spell user (or deity) who knew this could use Channels I to send a spell to that Cleric. Because the spell is passed through the aura of the receiving character, the spell is cast at the level of the receiving character (including any level-based parameters).
CHANNELS.4: As Channels I, except instead of sending a spell, the caster may send up to 1 PP/level to the other spell user (who need not use them right away). If the PP sent put the receiver over his normal PP maximum, excess PP are lost and the receiving individual suffers one hit of damage per PP in excess of his maximum.
CHANNELS.5: As Calming, except target is stunned (-50).
CHANNELS.6: As Channels I, except a 1st-3rd level spell may be transmitted.
CHANNELS.7: As Channels I, except the caster can send up to 2 PP/level.
CHANNELS.8: As Stunning, except target falls into a deep sleep. The spell duration of this sleep is magical (and the target cannot be awakened in any normal fashion). After this magical sleep, the target may be awakened normally, but if undisturbed, the target will sleep for a normal length sleep period (eight hours for humans).
CHANNELS.9: As Create Holy Water, except that the holy water is simply created without the need for clean water to transform.
CHANNELS.10: As Channels I, except a 1st-5th level spell may be transmitted.
CHANNELS.11: As Stunning, except target is blinded for 1 minute per 5 failure.
CHANNELS.12: [RR Mod: -20] Target takes a B Holy critical.
CHANNELS.13: As Channels I, except a 1st-8th level spell may be transmitted.
CHANNELS.14: [RR Mod: -20] Target’s “soul” is torn from the target’s body (or other physical location if the soul is otherwise housed); it remains in whatever place “souls” go for 1 week/10 failure. The soul can be returned early only through Lifegiving or Reuniting. Target is unconscious until soul is restored; even subconscious activity (i.e., healing, etc.) suffers a -75 penalty.
CHANNELS.15: All beings not of the caster’s own “alignment” (religious persuasion) are affected. All targets failing to resist by 1-40 are stunned (-50) 1 rnd/10 failure; those failing by more than 40 are unconscious for 1 rnd/5 failure.
CHANNELS.16: Target item (weighing no more than 10 pounds) will return to a designated location. This spell has two possible durations (determined at the time of casting). The caster may send (i.e., teleport) the target item to a designated location at the time of casting (with an instantaneous duration), or the caster can designate that the target item will return to the caster when the possessor of the item has completed a specific task (specified at the time of casting).
CHANNELS.17: As Channels I, except a 1st-10th level spell may be transmitted.
CHANNELS.18: Caster is returned to a predefined place (this is a type of teleportation). Caster must have lived in the place for 30 days (meditating 16 hours each day) to define it as the caster’s “sanctuary”. Only one such place may be defined at any one time; to change it, the new place must be defined as above.
CHANNELS.19: As Item Returning, except object will stay at the designated location (set at the time of casting) for up to 1 round per level. At the end of this time, the object will go back to where it “returned” from.
CHANNELS.20: [RR Mod: -20] As Absolution, except the “soul” can only be brought back through Lifegiving or Reuniting.
CHANNELS.25: For up to 1 round/level after having used Sanctuary, the caster may cast this spell and be returned to within 20' of the point at which the Sanctuary spell was cast.
CHANNELS.30: As Channels I, except a 1st-20th level spell may be transmitted.
CHANNELS.35: [RR Mod: -20] Target takes an E Holy critical.
CHANNELS.40: As Channels I, except there is no limit on the level of spell that may be transmitted.
CHANNELS.50: Opens a direct channel to the caster’s deity; results depend on the deity’s personality, motives, and powers. Any spell the deity can cast may be transmitted through the gate.

COMMUNAL WAYS.1: When faced with a choice about which the caster has little or no information (e.g., which corridor leads to the wine cellar), the caster may cast this spell and the Gamemaster will determine which choice the caster actually makes, biasing the choice favorably by 25% (e.g., if there are two choices, roll 1-100: correct on 26-100, incorrect on 01-25). The caster must have a limited number of options (i.e., finite and countable). After the spell is cast, the caster may not cast another Guess for the same information until his experience level has increased.
COMMUNAL WAYS.2: Caster can speak and understand the language( s) of any supernatural entities favorable to his religion with the same fluency as he has in his native language.
COMMUNAL WAYS.3: Caster gains a vision of what will probably happen in the next minute if the caster takes a specified action.
