CONCEALMENT MASTERY.19: As See Invisible, except the duration is 10 minutes per level.
CONCEALMENT MASTERY.20: As Conceal III, except choose nineteen options.
CONCEALMENT MASTERY.25: As Unseen III, except up to 1 object per level.
CONCEALMENT MASTERY.30: As Invisibility I, except as many targets as the caster’s level may be the centers of constant 1' radii of invisibility.
CONCEALMENT MASTERY.35: As Displacement I, except chance of missing is 50%.
CONCEALMENT MASTERY.40: As Conceal III, except choose one option per caster level.
CONCEALMENT MASTERY.50: As Invisibility I, except the caster can vary the radius of invisibility up to 1' and if the caster attacks he is only visible for the 5 seconds immediately following the attack. Likewise, he may cast a type E or F spell and become visible for the following 5 seconds. Violent blows do not affect this spell.

INFLUENCES.1: [RR Mod.: -30] Target that is already at least napping falls into a very deep sleep, taking a -50 penalty to Perception rolls to wake up.
INFLUENCES.2: Target animal(s) will believe the caster is a good friend.
INFLUENCES.3: Caster gains a +10 bonus to all Social Awareness skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.4: Anyone making a Social Awareness maneuver with respect to the caster becomes a target of this spell. If affected, the target will suffer a -25 penalty to all such Social Awareness maneuvers while the spell lasts.
INFLUENCES.5: Caster gains a +10 bonus to all Influence skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.6: Caster can read the surface thoughts of the target.
INFLUENCES.7: Caster gains a +20 bonus to all Social Awareness skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.8: One humanoid target for every five levels (or fraction thereof) of the caster will believe the caster is a very good friend.
INFLUENCES.9: Caster becomes highly fluent (equivalent of rank 10) in any spoken or signed language in which he has at least one rank.
INFLUENCES.10: Caster gains a +30 bonus to all Social Awareness skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.11: Humanoid targets (up to one for every five levels, or fraction thereof, of the caster) will perform a single suggested act that is not self-destructive or diametrically opposed to a target’s personality (e.g., no suicide suggestions, no self-mutilation suggestions, no suggestions that a priest pray to an enemy god, etc.). Suggestion must be the same for all targets.
INFLUENCES.12: Caster gains a +20 bonus to all Influence skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.13: Humanoid targets have their Action Points per round reduced by 3 (i.e., normally, the targets will have 1 AP each round). Up to one target for every five levels (or fraction thereof) of the caster may be affected.
INFLUENCES.14: Caster has a +25 bonus to any Performance Art skill maneuver using his voice.
INFLUENCES.15: As Mind Reading I, except for range.
INFLUENCES.16: Caster gains a +40 bonus to all Social Awareness skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.17: Caster gains a +30 bonus to all Influence skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.18: As Group Suggestion, except group will obey throughout duration and different commands can be issued to different members of the group.
INFLUENCES.19: The caster must record in writing a single suggested act that is not self-destructive or diametrically opposed to the ultimate target’s personality (e.g., no suicide suggestions, no blinding himself suggestions, no suggestions that a priest pray to an enemy god, etc.). This creates a minor magic item, and at this time no RR is made. When the text is read by the intended recipient (caster may specify an individual, a specific type, or simply aim for the first reader), the spell is triggered and if the triggering reader fails his RR, he will act as suggested. Once triggered, the text loses its enchantment.
INFLUENCES.20: Caster gains a +50 bonus to all Social Awareness skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.25: As Mind Reading I, except for range.
INFLUENCES.30: [RR: -25] The caster presents any paper or badgelike item or whatever item is roughly similar in type to the proper identification, credential, pass, or other document granting permission and/or authority that is being claimed by the caster. If the spell succeeds, the targets perceive the object presented as the genuine article. Caster must initially touch the item, but then the item may be taken for inspection and even handed from one individual to another out of sight of the caster without interruption of the effect.
INFLUENCES.35: Caster gains a +50 bonus to all Influence skill maneuvers.
INFLUENCES.40: [RR Mod.: -10] Humanoid targets (up to one per level of the caster) will perform a single suggested act that is not self-destructive or diametrically opposed to a target’s personality (e.g., no suicide suggestions, no self-mutilation suggestions, no suggestions that a priest pray to an enemy god, etc.). Suggestion must be the same for all targets.
INFLUENCES.50: Targets are given one task; failure results in a penalty determined by the Gamemaster (task must be within capabilities of the targets). If a target ignores the quest, or fails to cooperate with the other targets towards the success of the quest, this incurs the same effects as for failure.

MOVEMENT MASTERY.1: Caster may move at two times normal walking pace (i.e., Jog pace) as easily as walking. Fatigue and difficulty of maneuvers are as if at Walk pace; spells requiring a “walking pace” may be used (e.g. Shadow Steps), but not those requiring slower than walking pace (e.g., Spider’s Step). Once the caster stops moving, the spell is canceled.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.2: Caster may jump (from any pace) up to 10' plus 5' per level of the caster horizontally or 5' plus 2' per level of the caster vertically. This spell will allow the caster to always land safely from jumps of this distance or less. The jump itself is a 1 AP action or it may be incorporated into movement at no cost if the caster is moving at a Jog (x2) or greater pace.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.3: This spell may be cast when the caster begins to fall, taking effect immediately, allowing the caster to land safely in a fall up to 20' per level of the caster and to take that distance off the severity of any longer fall. This landing will also be noiseless.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.4: Allows the caster to cloak all of his movements in complete silence, so long as he moves no faster than a walking pace. This provides a +25 bonus to Stalking maneuvers and negates any penalties for especially noisy surfaces.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.5: Caster can take action underwater as if on land.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.6: Adds +50 to any rolls for any moving maneuvers performed at a walking pace or less (e.g., walking a 3" beam).
MOVEMENT MASTERY.7: Caster can move (at Creep pace) along any solid surface angled up to 90° so long as at least three point contact (e.g., two feet and a hand) is maintained with the surface.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.8: Caster can safely dive through the air up to 50' per level so long as there is deep enough water present at the end of the dive (at least 1' of water per 25' of dive).
MOVEMENT MASTERY.9: Caster can move at a walking pace without leaving tracks or other visible signs of his passing.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.10: As Spider’s Step, except caster can move along any surface (including ceilings).
MOVEMENT MASTERY.11: Caster can float upon the air. While floating, the caster is at the mercy of the prevailing winds and cannot control any aspect of his flight without access to some other motive force (i.e., pulling along a rope or wall, being towed, etc.).
MOVEMENT MASTERY.12: As Spider’s Step, except caster may move at a normal walking pace and he needs only to maintain a 2-point contact with the wall.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.13: As Jog, except pace is three times walking pace.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.14: As Soft Landing, except caster can land safely from any fall 99% of the time, and still takes the normal 20'/level off any fall for the 1% of the time that safety is not complete. While falling, the caster gets his full Stalking bonus and adds +25 to that if not in direct sunlight.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.15: Caster can “glide” through the air. The product of caster’s altitude and horizontal speed cannot exceed 100 (with altitude in feet and speed in feet per round). For example, a caster can glide along at a rate of 5' per round if he were 20' off the ground, or he could glide at the rate of 50' per round if he were 2' off the ground. Note that the product must equal 100 (i.e., the caster cannot choose to have a result less than or more than 100). Elevation may be increased up to 5' or decreased up to 10' each round, with the highest elevation being used to calculate the horizontal speed. There is a minimum elevation of 2'.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.16: Caster can walk on calm air. This spell only allows for horizontal movement. Vertical movement must be achieved by other means.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.17: Caster can move at any pace or using any means (e.g., swimming, which would normally be less stealthy due to splashing water) without penalty to any Stalking rolls.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.18: As Jog, except pace is four times walking pace.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.19: As Glide I, except product is 200.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.20: As Spider’s Walk, except caster can move along any surface (including ceilings).
MOVEMENT MASTERY.25: As Glide I, except product is 300.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.35: As Jog, except pace is five times walking pace.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.40: As Glide I, except product is 500.
MOVEMENT MASTERY.50: Caster may use any lower level spell from this list once per round.

SENSES.1: Caster gains an extremely acute sense of hearing. This results in +50 to Perception rolls involving only hearing, +25 to Perception involving hearing and other senses.
SENSES.2: Caster can see up to 100' as if it were daylight, so long as there is some light.
SENSES.3: Caster gains an extremely acute sense of smell. This results in +50 to Perception rolls involving only smell, +25 to Perception involving smell and other senses.
SENSES.4: One location is “marked” so that the caster can find it again later with a Far Sense spell. The marker is automatically located when the caster casts a Far Sense spell if the marker is within range of the Far Sense spell. A marker can be placed on any inanimate object. The caster can only have as many markers as he has ranks in this list; a Sensory Marker spell can be cancelled even if the caster is no longer within range of the marker.
SENSES.5: Caster may designate any one of his senses to be used at any “marked” location within range (see Sensory Marker). The caster can use any perception abilities he has at the time (e.g., if he is currently under the effects of Nightvision, he will have Nightvision at the marked location). The remote sensory point may be rotated to face any direction. While he is sensing at the marked location, the caster must remain immobile and concentrate (and does not have that sense available at his own location).
SENSES.6: Caster has a 300° field of vision. The flank bonus for attacks against the caster is lowered to +5 and the rear bonus is lowered to +15.
SENSES.7: Caster gains extreme tactile sensitivity. This provides a bonus to any action requiring a sense of touch. For example, caster might receive +25 to picking locks, disarming traps, opening secret doors, etc. and +50 to Perception involving only touch, +25 to Perception involving touch and other senses).
SENSES.8: Caster can see 100' in any water (including murky water) as if through air in daylight.
SENSES.9: As Nightvision, except any darkness can be seen through. No light at all is needed for this spell to work.
SENSES.10: As Far Sense I, except caster may designate up to two senses for use at the marked location.
SENSES.11: Caster can see through wood (up to 1" per level).
SENSES.12: Caster can see in any brightness of light (including that which would be blinding or glaring). This spell does not work in the absence of light.
SENSES.13: Caster can see through any woven organic substance (up to 1" per level).
SENSES.14: As Far Sense I, except caster can move while the spell is active (though he must maintain concentration).
SENSES.15: As Far Sense I, except for range.
SENSES.16: Caster can see through stone (up to 1" per level).
SENSES.17: Caster knows the location (distance and direction) of one chosen Sensory Marker relative to the caster’s current location.
SENSES.18: As Far Sense II, except caster can move while the spell is active (though he must maintain concentration).
SENSES.19: Caster can see through metal (up to 1" per level).
SENSES.20: As Far Sense II, except for range.
SENSES.25: As all Vision spells on this list operating at the same time.
SENSES.30: Caster has the effects of Sly Ears, Scent, Touch, and all Vision spells simultaneously.
SENSES.35: Caster has a warning of any impending danger. This will give the caster a second chance to notice any trap he has missed before actually triggering it, prevent any attacker from gaining the bonus for Surprise or succeeding in using Ambush skill against the caster, and should provide similar protection against other sudden danger (GM’s discretion).
SENSES.40: As Greater Far Sense I, except caster can use all senses and the range is improved.
SENSES.50: Caster may use any lower level spell on this list once per round.

SMOKE AND MIRRORS.1: Makes one surface of an inanimate object up to 10'x10' perfectly reflective in the orientation desired by the caster, e.g. to permit viewing around a corner.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.2: Creates a cloud of obscuring smoke (caster’s choice of color) which obscures as heavy fog (-50 Perception, visibility reduced to 50').
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.3: Creates any simple, immobile visual image/scene in an area of up to 10'R, or creates a set of immobile sounds in an area of up to 10'R.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.4: Caster gains a +25 Perception bonus to notice that which is hidden by any means (including noticing illusions).
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.5: Creates a simple, immobile image or scene up to an area of 10'R. Two of the following options may also be chosen: a) an extra sense can be added (not the tactile or Presence senses), b) the duration can be doubled, c) the range can be doubled, d) the radius of the area of effect can be doubled, or e) the illusion can cast light. All parts of the area of effect must be in the caster’s field of vision at the time of casting.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.6: Creates an area of darkness up to 2'R/lvl about the point touched. The darkness is equal to the darkest night. (See RMCL Section 15.7) If the point is on a mobile object or being, it will move with the object/being (but any target gets an RR to avoid having it “stick” to them).
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.7: Creates the image of one object or being that will move however the caster wants (as long as the caster concentrates). When the caster stops concentrating, the image remains but stops moving. The caster may resume concentration again later, and make the image move again (presuming that the duration has not expired). The image can be of any size that would fit in a 10'R. One of the following options may also be chosen: a) an extra sense can be added (not the tactile or Presence senses), b) the duration can be doubled, c) the range can be doubled, d) the radius of the area of effect can be doubled, e) another image can be created and moved independently of the first (all separate images must be within the caster’s field of vision and within range of the spell), f) the phantasm can cast light, or g) limited repetitious sounds, movements, etc., can be added that do not require concentration of the caster (the proper senses involved must also be included within the illusion).
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.8: Instantly extinguishes a fire up to the size of a campfire.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.9: The next spell cast from this list (must be within 1 minute) will have its effect delayed up to 24 hours. At the time of casting, the caster must decide upon the trigger for the spell. The caster can choose one of the following: a) time period, b) specified movements, or c) specified sounds.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.10: Instantly ignites any one thing intended to burn, e.g. it will light a lantern, torch, firewood, but not other items such as furniture or clothing.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.11: As Subtle Eye I, except bonus is +50.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.12: As Illusion II, except four options can be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.13: As Phantasms II, except two options may be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.14: As Extinguish Minor, except fires up to 10' in diameter.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.15: As Extinguish Minor, except all minor fires in the area of effect.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.16: As Illusion II, except seven options can be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.17: As Smoke Cloud, but area of effect is 10'R/lvl.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.18: As Phantasms II, except three options can be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.19: Immediately extinguishes all fire within 5’/lvl radius.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.20: As Ignite Fuel, except it will ignite all suitable things of the specified type (or all suitable types) within the radius.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.25: As Phantasms II, except four options can be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.30: As Illusion II, except nine options can be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.35: As Subtle Eye I, except bonus is +100.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.40: As Illusion II, except 14 options can be chosen.
SMOKE AND MIRRORS.50: As Phantasms II, except nine options can be chosen.

TRADE MASTERY.1: Caster receives basic idea of item’s purpose, and receives +20 to its use if it is intended to be operated using any Craft or Technical skill.
TRADE MASTERY.2: When this spell is cast upon a machine, the machine’s efficiency will return to its original level. For example, if cast upon a rusty lock, the lock would return to its original non-rusty operational level.
TRADE MASTERY.3: This spell allows the caster to perform one maneuver using a Craft or Technical skill as if the caster had a complete set of the appropriate tools with a bonus of +10.
TRADE MASTERY.4: Target mechanism (trap, lock, door, machine, etc) is jammed, and has only a 7% chance of operating when used/triggered normally. It remains jammed until repaired.
TRADE MASTERY.5: Caster can assess the value of jewels and metals within 10% of actual value. This spell allows the caster to calculate different values for all of the cultures with which the caster is familiar. This spell evaluates materials only, not craftsmanship or magical properties.
TRADE MASTERY.6: This spell will operate any non-magical machine in its normal capacity for the duration. After the duration, the machine will operate normally. For example, if this spell were used to turn a wheel, the wheel would spin for the duration of the spell, then slowly spin to a stop. This merely provides basic motive power; any additional controls (directional controls, frequency settings, etc.) must be handled separately.
TRADE MASTERY.7: As Jewel/Metal Assessment, except this spell will determine the value of an item, taking into account the craftsmanship of the item.
TRADE MASTERY.8: As Phantom Tools I, except the bonus is +30.
TRADE MASTERY.9: Caster will be aware of any machine activity or stored power for a machine (e.g. capacitors, battery, springs, weights) within the radius of effect. The caster will not know what the machine is or exactly where, though successful Perception may give an idea of the number of machines, vague location, and overall energy involved. A Very Hard Perception maneuver while moving at a walking pace or slower with this spell active will give the caster enough warning that he is starting to trigger a mechanism for the caster to pull back, avoiding a tripwire or pressure plate activation.
TRADE MASTERY.10: Caster receives a +25 bonus to Trading skill and to any Social or Lore skill used to locate a buyer or seller.
TRADE MASTERY.11: Caster gains a general idea of an item’s abilities (e.g., it provides a bonus to Stealth [but not the amount], it allows casting a spell twice daily [but not which spell], or it does an additional critical in combat [but not what kind or information on the severity of the critical]).
TRADE MASTERY.12: As Operate I, except concentration is not required and the duration is 1 minute per level.
TRADE MASTERY.13: As Jam I, but the mechanism has only a 4% chance of operating when used/triggered.
TRADE MASTERY.14: Caster can detect any item in the radius which has cultural or historical significance (e.g. a sacred relic, a item formerly possessed by a great hero), and its magnitude (mild significance, great fame, etc), but not the details. Caster can move the area of effect 5' each round by concentrating.
TRADE MASTERY.15: As Operate II, except duration is 1 hr/level.
TRADE MASTERY.16: As Phantom Tools I, except the bonus is +50.
TRADE MASTERY.17: As Acumen I, except the bonus is +50.
TRADE MASTERY.18: The caster learns the area of origin of the item, the race of the being who made it, and when it was made (within 100 years).
TRADE MASTERY.19: As Operate II, except the duration is 1 day per level.
TRADE MASTERY.20: As Jam II, except affects all mechanisms in the area of effect.
TRADE MASTERY.25: Caster gets a vision of a significant event in the item’s past.
TRADE MASTERY.30: Allows caster to operate and control one machine. This not only provides basic motive power (as an Operate spell), but allows full control of an entire machine by the caster alone. Treat as if as many individuals as needed for normal operations (up to a maximum equal to the caster’s level) were working under the perfect command of the caster. Treat the skill of this crew as either +0 or the caster’s own bonus in the appropriate skill.
TRADE MASTERY.35: As Acumen I, except the bonus is +100.
TRADE MASTERY.40: As Operate II, except affects all machines in the area of effect.
TRADE MASTERY.50: As Operate II, except the duration is permanent.

GUISES.1: Causes target to appear blurred to attackers, granting a +10 to the target’s DB.
GUISES.2: Target and objects on the target’s person appear to be in shadow and thus are almost invisible in dark areas (in many situations this could be handled with a Stalking bonus of between +25 and +75).
GUISES.3: Target has a limited illusion on himself that allows him to look like any humanoid race within 20% of his own size. The illusion moves as the target moves.
GUISES.4: [RR Mod: -50] Caster can communicate simple ideas to the target through sign language (yes, no, hungry, good-bye, etc.); to the target it will seem as if the caster were using the gestures appropriate to the target’s culture.
GUISES.5: Target’s apparent location is offset from the actual location; all attacks have no effect 10% of the time. Each time a foe misses due to this effect, the chance of that foe missing again goes down 5%.
GUISES.6: As Facade I, except one of the other senses can be added.
GUISES.7: As Facade I, except that a specific person can be impersonated with regards to looks. The person must have been observed for at least 1 minute of concentration.
GUISES.8: As Facade I, except two of the other senses can be added.
GUISES.9: As Impersonation Facade I, except that one other aspect (or trait) of the person is impersonated. Additionally, the caster must study the target for at least two minutes of concentration. For example, the target’s voice can be impersonated.
GUISES.10: As Displacement I, except chance of missing is 20%.
GUISES.11: Creates a duplicate of the caster, which the caster may concentrate to control and otherwise does exactly what the caster does. The image includes visual and audio components, but no other senses.
GUISES.12: As Impersonation Facade I, except that two other aspects (or traits) of the person are impersonated. Additionally, the caster must study the target for at least three minutes of concentration. For example, the target’s voice and scent can be impersonated.
GUISES.13: As Blur, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
GUISES.14: As Facade I, except all of the other senses may be added.
GUISES.15: As Displacement I, except chance of missing is 30%.
GUISES.16: As Impersonation Facade I, except that three other aspects (or traits) of the person are impersonated. Additionally, the caster must study the target for at least four minutes of concentration. For example, the target’s voice, scent, and subtle mannerisms can be impersonated.
GUISES.17: The caster may cast this spell and instantly know everything necessary for Impersonation Facade spells (i.e., this spell replaces time spent studying the subject to be impersonated).
GUISES.18: As Shadow, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
GUISES.19: As Impersonation Facade I, except that all aspects of the person are impersonated. Additionally, the caster must study the target for at least five minutes of concentration. With this spell, even the closest friends and relatives of the individual impersonated will have difficulty noticing the facade.
GUISES.20: As Displacement III, except chance of missing is 40%.
GUISES.25: As Facade II, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
GUISES.30: As Displacement I, except chance of missing is 50%.
GUISES.35: As Displacement II, except caster can protect one target per level.
GUISES.40: As Displacement I, except chance of missing is 60%.
GUISES.50: As Facade V, except the caster can change the facade to a different facade each round.

ILLUSION MASTERY.1: Creates a simple, immobile image or scene within the area of effect. One of the following options may also be chosen: a) an extra sense can be added (the corresponding Mirage spell must be known); b) the duration can be doubled; c) the range can be doubled, d) the radius of the area of effect can be doubled, or e) the illusion can cast light. All parts of the area of effect must be in the caster’s field of vision at the time of casting.
ILLUSION MASTERY.2: Creates the image of one object or being that will move however the caster wants (as long as the caster concentrates). When the caster stops concentrating, the image remains but stops moving. The caster may resume concentration again later and make the image move again (presuming that the duration has not expired). The image can be of any size that would fit within the area of effect.
ILLUSION MASTERY.3: As Illusion II, except any two of the options may be chosen. See notes above for guidelines on how to combine the options.
ILLUSION MASTERY.4: As Illusion II, except it can be delayed by up to 24 hours. At the time of casting, the caster chooses the trigger for the spell. The caster can choose one of the following: a) time period, b) specified movements, c) specified sounds, d) specified smells, e) specified tastes, f) specified touch, or g) a Presence spell cast in the area of effect. If a sense is used to trigger the spell, that sense must be included in the illusion.
ILLUSION MASTERY.5: As Phantasms I, except one of the following options may also be chosen: a) an extra sense can be added (the corresponding Mirage spell must be known); b) the duration can be doubled; c) the range can be doubled; d) the radius of the area of effect can be doubled; e) another image can be created and moved independently of the first (all separate images must be within the caster’s field of vision and within area of effect of the spell); f) the phantasm can cast light; or g) limited repetitious sounds, movements, etc., can be added that do not require concentration of the caster (the proper senses involved must also be included within the illusion). See notes for guidelines on how to combine the options.
ILLUSION MASTERY.6: As Illusion II, except any four of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.7: As Phantasms II, except it can be delayed as in Waiting Illusion II. The Phantasm will move and act if given a simple command (e.g., attack, run, etc.) or it can deliver a short speech if sound was one of the senses.
ILLUSION MASTERY.8: As Waiting Illusion II, except any two of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.9: As Phantasms II, except any two of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.10: As Illusion II, except any six of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.11: As Waiting Phantasm II, except any two of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.12: As Phantasms II, except any three of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.13: As Waiting Illusion II, except any four of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.14: As Phantasms II, except any four of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.15: As Illusion II, except any nine of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.16: As Waiting Phantasm II, except any four of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.17: As Phantasms II, except any six of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.18: As Waiting Illusion II, except any six of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.19: All of the terrain in the area of effect will appear differently than it actually is (the corresponding Terrain spell for each sense incorporated must be known). The caster may designate in what way the terrain is different. For example, a clearing in the woods could be disguised as a heavily wooded area of the woods.
ILLUSION MASTERY.20: As Phantasms II, except any nine of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.25: As Waiting Illusion II, except any nine of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.30: As Illusion X, except its duration is permanent (until dispelled).
ILLUSION MASTERY.35: As Illusion II, except any nineteen of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.40: As Phantasms II, except any nineteen of the options may be chosen.
ILLUSION MASTERY.50: As Phantasms X, except its duration is permanent (until dispelled); Phantasm can move only if caster concentrates, except for simple programmed repetitions, if that option is chosen.

LIGHT MOLDING.1: Creates any simple immobile image or scene up to an area of 10'R. The visual aspects of the scene are really created (no RR) and detecting that it is an illusion can normally be accomplished only through spells or the use of a sense other than sight.
LIGHT MOLDING.2: Beam of light (like a flashlight) springs from the caster’s palm; it has a 50' effective range. If the caster’s hand is closed into a fist, the light will “turn off”. If the caster’s fist is reopened before the end of the duration, the light will turn on again.
LIGHT MOLDING.3: Caster can control the intensity of light within the area of effect; the intensity can vary from daylight to darkness (natural), and it can be different in different parts of the radius.
LIGHT MOLDING.4: Causes a 10'R burst of intense light, all within are stunned (-50) for 1 round per 10 failure.
LIGHT MOLDING.5: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT MOLDING.6: One object (up to 10 pounds per level) has its visual appearance altered for the duration of the spell. Note that no other aspect of the object changes. This spell cannot make an object cast light (although it may alter the appearance of light given off, whether naturally or from another spell).
LIGHT MOLDING.7: Lights a 50'R area about the point touched.
LIGHT MOLDING.8: Reduces illumination to a dark night in a 50'R area about the point touched.
LIGHT MOLDING.9: Creates an area of darkness about the target’s head that blinds him unless dispelled or canceled by Utterlight.
LIGHT MOLDING.10: As Light Control I, except area affected is 50'R.
LIGHT MOLDING.11: Nullifies all magically created darkness in a 100'R and lights that area as full daylight.
LIGHT MOLDING.12: All of the terrain in the area of effect will look differently than it actually is. The caster may designate in what way the terrain appears different. For example, a group of small trees could be made into a group of tall trees. Note that only the visual aspect of the terrain changes.
LIGHT MOLDING.13: A ray of light (any color) springs from caster’s palm; it can be up to 1 mile long.
LIGHT MOLDING.14: Darkens a 100'R area, no light (except Utterlight) can exist within this radius.
LIGHT MOLDING.15: As Light Control I, except area affected is 100'R.
LIGHT MOLDING.16: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT MOLDING.17: As Light Glamour, except that it affects up to one item per caster level, with the duration and range listed.
LIGHT MOLDING.18: As Beacon I, except the ray of light can be up to 5 miles long.
LIGHT MOLDING.19: As Light Control I, except area affected is 200'R.
LIGHT MOLDING.20: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack.
LIGHT MOLDING.25: As Light Control I, except area affected is 500'R.
LIGHT MOLDING.30: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack.
LIGHT MOLDING.35: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack.
LIGHT MOLDING.40: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster every each round the spell remains in effect.; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT MOLDING.50: As Light Control I, except area affected is 100'R/level.

MIND SENSE MOLDING.1: Caster can check one object or place (up to a 5'R) and tell if it is an illusion or has an illusion on it.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.2: Detects any invisible objects or beings; one 5'R area can be checked each round. All attacks against detected targets are modified by -50.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.3: For the purposes of mental or magical detections, target appears to be of any race with which the caster is familiar.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.4: As Misfeel Kind, except target’s level may be misrepresented by 1 level (up or down).
MIND SENSE MOLDING.5: Creates a false “presence” of a being for the purposes of magical detection.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.6: As Misfeel Kind, except target’s profession may be misrepresented.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.7: As Misfeel Power I, except target’s level may be misrepresented by up to 3 levels.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.8: Caster becomes undetectable by Presence spells or related abilities.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.9: Conceals an item’s magical power. Any attempt to detect its magical power (an appropriate Detect spell while it is active, an Attunement attempt, or other means) is hindered. If the item has a single power, then if the detection attempt fails an RR against this spell, it does not register the item’s magic. In the case of multiple powers, a magical detection attempt gains a +5 to its RR for each power beyond the first, while someone attempting Attunement (and failing the RR) will be unable to discover one ability (chosen at the time this spell is cast), but may discover and use the remaining powers normally.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.10: As Misfeel Power I, except target’s level may be misrepresented by up to 5 levels.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.11: While this spell is in effect, one illusion within the caster’s range ceases to exist for the caster only. The caster must specify the illusion to be negated (unless caster knows something is an illusion, this spell would be gambling PP).
MIND SENSE MOLDING.12: As Detect Illusion, except caster can concentrate on one object or place per round.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.13: As Misfeel Power I, except target’s level can be misrepresented by up to 10 levels.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.14: As Disillusion I, except up to three illusions within the area of effect cease to exist for the caster.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.15: Applies all the lower level Misfeels to a target at once (only one Misfeel Power can be applied).
MIND SENSE MOLDING.16: Target becomes undetectable by Presence spells or related abilities.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.17: As Disillusion I, except up to five illusions within the area of effect cease to exist for the caster.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.18: As Reduce Power Emanations, except affects up to some combination of five powers/targets, i.e. the caster could use this to conceal up to five powers of a single item, three powers of one item and two powers of another item, one power each of five items, etc.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.19: As Disillusion I, except all illusions within the area of effect cease to exist for the caster.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.20: As Unpresence I, except affects up to five targets.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.25: As Misfeel Multiple, except duration is 1 hour/level.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.30: As Unpresence, except 20 targets may be affected.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.35: As Misfeel Power I, except target’s level may be misrepresented by any number of levels.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.40: Creates one false “presence” of a being for the purposes of magical detection for each level of the caster and these will be located as the caster desires within the area of effect. Caster may move these presence mirages by concentrating at a rate of 10'/round each.
MIND SENSE MOLDING.50: As Misfeel Multiple, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.

SENSE MOLDING.1: Fills the area of effect with a set of immobile smells. The smells are real (no RR) and detecting that it is an illusion can normally only be accomplished through spells or the use of a sense other than smell.
SENSE MOLDING.2: Target is struck with the equivalent of a (Medium-sized) bare fist (Strikes attack table). The attack is invisible unless combined with the visual sense in an Illusion or Phantasms. Directed Spells: Illusionary Attacks skill may be developed for this attack.
SENSE MOLDING.3: As Smell Mirage, except a set of tastes can be created in a 10'R.
SENSE MOLDING.4: Creates a 10'R cloud of noxious gas that will stun anyone failing to resist (all targets must make RRs each round they are in the cloud). Cloud drifts with the wind. Targets are stunned (-50) 1 round per 10 failure.
SENSE MOLDING.5: As Smell Mirage, except all the objects and surfaces in a 10'R can be made to feel differently than they really are. Striking an object or surface will cancel the spell for that object or surface only.
SENSE MOLDING.6: One object (up to 10 pounds per level) has either its taste, its smell, or the way its surface feels altered for the duration of the spell. Note that the visual aspects of the object do not change.
SENSE MOLDING.7: Target is struck with the equivalent of a (Medium-sized) bare fist (Strikes attack table). The attack is invisible unless combined with the visual sense in an Illusion or Phantasms. Directed Spells: Illusionary Attacks skill may be developed for this attack.
SENSE MOLDING.8: Creates a dulling of tactile sensations in the target, especially the hands. Fumble ranges of weapons are increased by 2, applied after any reduction for number of ranks, and all tasks requiring tactile feedback (e.g., picking a lock, dancing with a partner, playing the piano) are at -25, while Perception rolls for the sense of touch are at -50.
SENSE MOLDING.9: As Tear Cloud I, except radius is 20'.
SENSE MOLDING.10: As Feel Mirage I, except objects with a feel mirage on them must be struck three times before the feeling is cancelled.
SENSE MOLDING.11: Target is struck with the equivalent of a (Medium-sized) bare fist (Strikes attack table). The attack is invisible unless combined with the visual sense in an Illusion or Phantasms. Directed Spells: Illusionary Attacks skill may be developed for this attack.
SENSE MOLDING.12: All of the terrain in the area of effect will feel differently than it normally would. The caster may designate in what way the terrain feels differently. For example, flat ground could be made to feel rocky or rocky ground could be made to feel flat.
SENSE MOLDING.13: As many objects as the caster’s level can be given individual smells and tastes.
SENSE MOLDING.14: As Tear Cloud I, except radius is 50'.
SENSE MOLDING.15: As Feel Mirage I, except objects with a feel mirage on them must be struck five times before the feeling is cancelled.
SENSE MOLDING.16: As many objects as the caster’s level can be given individual feelings to the touch. Striking an object or surface will cancel the spell for that object only.
SENSE MOLDING.17: One Target each round is struck with the equivalent of a (Medium-sized) bare fist (Strikes attack table). Target may be changed from one round to another. The attack is invisible unless combined with the visual sense in an Illusion or Phantasms. Directed Spells: Illusionary Attacks skill may be developed for this attack.
SENSE MOLDING.18: As Feel Mirage I, except objects with a feel mirage on them must be struck eight times before the feeling is cancelled.
SENSE MOLDING.19: As Tear Cloud I, except radius is 100'.
SENSE MOLDING.20: As Feel Mirage I, except objects with a feel mirage on them must be struck ten times before the feeling is cancelled.
SENSE MOLDING.25: Caster can give one object (up to 10 pounds per level) a permanent scent.
SENSE MOLDING.30: Caster can give one object (up to 10 pounds per level) a permanent taste.
SENSE MOLDING.35: As Tear Cloud I, except radius and range are as listed.
SENSE MOLDING.40: Caster can give one object (up to 10 pounds per level) a permanent feel to its surface.
SENSE MOLDING.50: As Smell Mirage, Taste Mirage, and Feel Mirage I, except all changes are permanent on every affected object and surface unless it is moved beyond the area of effect.

SOUND MOLDING.1: Creates a set of immobile sounds in an area of up to 10'R. The sounds are real (no RR) and detecting that it is an illusion can normally only be accomplished through spells or the use of a sense other than hearing.
SOUND MOLDING.2: Creates a 10'R area into and out of which sound cannot travel. As noted above, this spell can be cast on an individual target, which the spell will then follow; this target gains +25 to Stalking attempts, but likewise automatically fails any Perception attempts based on hearing alone and suffers a -50 to Perception rolls where hearing is a factor (e.g., to detect someone Stalking the target). Note that this does not interfere with spell-casting (the target can still speak, even yell, the sound is simply unable to leave the radius of the Sphere of Silence - certain spells like Ultrasonics may have their range limited to the interior of the Sphere of Silence radius, however).
SOUND MOLDING.3: Caster can control the intensity of sounds within the range; the intensity can vary from none to a very loud shout, and it can be different in different parts of the radius.
SOUND MOLDING.4: Causes a very loud, sudden sound next to the target’s ears; target is stunned (-50) for 1 round per 10 failure.
SOUND MOLDING.5: As Sound Control I, except radius is 50'.
SOUND MOLDING.6: One object (up to 10 pounds per level) has its sound altered for the duration of the spell. Note that no other aspect of the object changes.
SOUND MOLDING.7: Target cannot hear sounds occurring more than 6" from the target’s ears (or other organs of hearing), and the target’s own voice cannot be heard from more than 6" away from the target’s mouth (or other organ of speech).
SOUND MOLDING.8: As Sphere of Silence I, except radius is 50'.
SOUND MOLDING.9: All beings (except the caster) within range capable of hearing ultrasonic sounds are stunned (-50) 1 rnd/10 failure; an RR must be made once per round while in the radius. Even if they are not stunned, animals capable of hearing ultrasonics will have to make a second, non-magical RR against Fear (level of Fear is half the caster’s level).
SOUND MOLDING.10: As Sound Control I, except radius is 100'.
SOUND MOLDING.11: As Sudden Sound, except everyone in a 20'R is affected.
SOUND MOLDING.12: All of the terrain in the area of effect will have sounds that are different than the terrain’s normal sounds. The caster may designate in what way the terrain sounds different. For example, an open plain could be made to sound like a rustling forest. Note that only the audio aspect of the terrain changes. This can provide between a -30 to a +30 modification to all Stalking attempts within the terrain, depending on how “noisy” the illusionary environment is.
SOUND MOLDING.13: As Sphere of Silence I, except radius is 100'.
SOUND MOLDING.14: As Muffle, except everyone in a 10'R is affected.
SOUND MOLDING.15: As Sound Control I, except radius is 10'R/lvl.
SOUND MOLDING.16: As Sphere of Silence I, except range is 10' per level.
SOUND MOLDING.17: As Sound Contol I, except range is 10' per level.
SOUND MOLDING.18: As Sudden Sound, except for range.
SOUND MOLDING.19: As Muffle, except range is 10' per level.
SOUND MOLDING.20: As Muffle, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected.
SOUND MOLDING.25: As many targets as the caster’s level can have a 1'R silence on them. Except for the radius hugging closer to the body of the target, this functions as described in Sphere of Silence I.
SOUND MOLDING.30: As Sound Control I, except radius is 20'/lvl and the caster does not have to concentrate except to make changes.
SOUND MOLDING.35: As Sudden Sound Sphere II, except everyone in a 50'R is affected.
SOUND MOLDING.40: As Sudden Sound Sphere II, except everyone in a 100'R is affected and the range is 500'.
SOUND MOLDING.50: All beings (except the caster) within range capable of hearing ultrasonic sounds are stunned (-50) 1 rnd/10 failure; an RR must be made once per round while in the radius. Anyone failing to resist by 40-75 falls unconscious, while anyone failing the RR by more than 75 dies. Even if they are not stunned, animals capable of hearing ultrasonics will have to make a second, non-magical RR against Fear (level of Fear is equal to the caster’s level).

EARTH LAW.1: Caster transforms up to one cubic foot per level of clay into baked pottery. Firing clay in this manner will always be successful. This can also cook glazes onto earthenware. Quality of product depends on the skill of whomever shapes the clay.
EARTH LAW.2: Loosens 100 cubic feet of earth to the consistency of plowed ground.
EARTH LAW.3: Caster receives a +30 bonus on any maneuvers involving the working of stone.
EARTH LAW.4: Creates a wall of packed earth up to 10'x10'x (3' at base, 1' at top); it can be dug through only (20 man-rounds at top).
EARTH LAW.5: Any previous cracks or flaws in material up to 10'x10'x10' section will extend to their limit.
EARTH LAW.6: Caster may mend a single break in a small (up to 2 pounds) inorganic object or multiple breaks, rips, or cracks in a larger (up to 10 pounds) organic object. All component parts of the object must be within a 10' radius.
EARTH LAW.7: Creates a wall of non-precious stone up to 10'x10'x1'; it can be chipped through or toppled if not against a wall.
EARTH LAW.8: This spell causes the area of effect to bristle with hundreds of 6" to 12" sharp spikes and points. The exact composition of these spikes will depend on the material the ground is made of. The area of effect must be placed horizontally on a surface (i.e., it cannot be placed on walls). Most animals and creatures cannot be induced to walk through the area. Anyone moving through the area must make a maneuver roll (at least Extremely Hard difficulty) for every 5' moved through. Anyone who falls inside the area of effect receives an A Puncture critical strike.
EARTH LAW.9: Changes 100 cubic feet of stone to packed earth. This change is gradual, taking three rounds to complete.
EARTH LAW.10: As Earthwall, except duration is permanent.
EARTH LAW.11: As Stone/Earth, except changes earth to soft mud.
EARTH LAW.12: As Stone/Earth, except changes packed earth to solid stone and loose earth to gravel.
EARTH LAW.13: As Stonewall, except duration is permanent and dimensions may be up to 20'x20'x1'.
EARTH LAW.14: As Stone/Earth, except changes mud to packed earth.
EARTH LAW.16: Fuses two touching walls together (seam can be up to 20' long) or fuses a section of stone blocks (up to 100 cubic feet).
EARTH LAW.17: As Stone/Earth, except changes stone to mud.
EARTH LAW.18: As Stonewall True, except wall may be curved to a semicircle.
EARTH LAW.19: Removes a flaw from a single gem, mineral, or stone. This can greatly enhance the value of some jewels.
EARTH LAW.30: Causes a very minor earthquake which could cause shoddy construction to collapse (and can be very terrifying). This is approximately 5.5 on the Richter scale.
EARTH LAW.35: As Stonewall True, except wall may be curved as desired so long as total length does not exceed 10' per level and wall is two feet thick.
EARTH LAW.40: Transforms one stone into a stone golem (sophistication of shape depending on caster’s artistic skills) for the duration of the spell, during which it will obey the caster faithfully unless control is wrested by another (in which case the caster can always cancel the spell and return the golem to boulder form before duration runs out). Size of the golem is based on the stone’s weight (which may be modified up to 50% in order to achieve desired Size) and may be up to Large.
EARTH LAW.50: Caster can use one lower level spell (on this list) each round.

FIRE LAW.1: For each level of the caster, one cubic foot of liquid can be heated to boiling at a rate of 1 cubic foot per round. Once the caster ceases concentration, the liquid (if any remains) will cool normally.
FIRE LAW.2: Any solid, inanimate, non-metal material (up to 1 cubic foot per level) can be warmed to 100°F (38°C) at a rate of 1 cubic foot per round.
FIRE LAW.3: Causes any wood to ignite and burn. All wood ignited must be within 1' of caster’s palm.
FIRE LAW.4: Creates an opaque wall of fire (up to 10'x10'x6"). Anyone passing through it takes an A Heat critical (no RR).
FIRE LAW.5: As Warm Solid, except for duration and material can be heated to 500°F (260°C) at a rate of one cubic foot heated by 100°F (56°C) per round. The caster must concentrate to increase the temperature (without concentration, the material will retain its current temperature for the duration of the spell).
FIRE LAW.6: A bolt of fire is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Fire Bolt Table.
FIRE LAW.7: Creates a cube of flame (up to 10'x10'x10'); it takes 1 complete round for the cube to form and be effective. Anyone passing through (or caught within) the cube takes an A Heat critical each round spent in the cube.
FIRE LAW.8: A 1' diameter ball of fire is shot from the palm of the caster. Upon reaching the selected target/location, it expands to affect a 10'R area. Resolve attack on the Fire Ball Table.
FIRE LAW.9: The caster may designate a type of light source to ignite or extinguish (e.g., candles, torches, fireplaces, or lanterns). This spell will affect all of the light sources of the specified type(s) within the area of effect.
FIRE LAW.10: As Wall of Fire, except “wall” is 10' high and forms a 10'R circle (6" thick) with the caster at the center (it is non-mobile).
FIRE LAW.11: A bolt of fire is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Fire Bolt Table.
FIRE LAW.12: As Call Flame I, except cube is up to 20'x20'x20' in size and the range is 20'.
FIRE LAW.13: As Call Flame I, except the effect can be delayed for up to 24 hours. The effect can be triggered by one of the following (decided by the caster at time of casting): time period, certain movements, certain sounds, touch, violent actions in the area, or any other trigger so long as the caster would be able to sense it if the caster remained at the area of effect.
FIRE LAW.14: As Call Flame I, except small balls of flame rain down in a 10' cube causing a B Heat critical to all within or passing through the area of effect.
FIRE LAW.15: Causes a metal object to burst into flames, the object can be up to 1 lb/level in mass. If the object is on a being, it gets an RR, and if it fails, the being takes an automatic Heat critical of a severity to be determined by its location on the being’s body. If the object is touching exposed flesh, the being takes a C Heat critical; if the object is touching through cloth, the being takes a B Heat critical; any being within a 1'R takes an A Heat critical.
FIRE LAW.16: Three bolts of fire are shot from the palm of the caster. They can strike up to three different targets as long as they are all within 60° of each other and are within the caster’s field of vision. Caster may apply his Directed Spell skill by dividing it as he chooses among the three bolts (e.g., a +120 OB could be split evenly into three +40 bolts or one +120 bolt and two +0 bolts or one +60, one +40, and one +20 bolt).
FIRE LAW.17: A bolt of fire is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Fire Bolt Table.
FIRE LAW.18: As Waiting Flame, except a Firestorm can be delayed.
FIRE LAW.19: As Call Flame I, except the size is up to a 50' cube and the range is 50'.
FIRE LAW.20: As Fire Bolt III, except caster can make the bolt turn once by up to 90° before striking the target (the caster must know the target’s location). The caster’s OB is modified by -25 when using this spell. However, this spell can be used to bypass a positional modifier – any DB bonus gained through the use of cover (partial/half/full soft cover; partial/half/full hard cover) is reduced to zero if the turn circumvents the cover; a target that otherwise would be unable to be hit can be attacked using this spell.
FIRE LAW.25: A bolt of fire is shot from the palm of the caster; caster can make the bolt make as many turns as necessary, with an OB penalty of -25 per turn, and go through openings (must be larger than 6" radius) to strike the target. The caster’s OB is modified by -25 when using this spell. However, this spell can be used to bypass a positional modifier – any DB bonus gained through the use of cover (partial/half/full soft cover; partial/half/full hard cover) is reduced to zero if the turn circumvents the cover; a target that otherwise would be unable to be hit can be attacked using this spell.
FIRE LAW.30: A stone surface of up to 300 sq. ft. bursts into flames, and a C Heat critical is given each round to anything passing through (or spending the round in) the 3' flames.
FIRE LAW.35: A bolt of fire is shot from the palm of the caster; caster can make the bolt make as many turns as necessary and go through openings (must be larger than 6" radius) to strike the target. The caster’s OB is modified by -25 when using this spell. However, this spell can be used to bypass a positional modifier – any DB bonus gained through the use of cover (partial/half/full soft cover; partial/half/full hard cover) is reduced to zero if the turn circumvents the cover; a target that otherwise would be unable to be hit can be attacked using this spell.
FIRE LAW.40: A cone of fire resembling the breath weapon of a fire-breathing dragon shoots from the caster’s hand or face, with a diameter of 1' at its origin point at the caster increasing to a diameter of 50' at the termination of the cone 100' away. Results of this attack are determined using the Fire Ball table.
FIRE LAW.50: Caster can use any one lower level spell (on this list) each round.

ICE LAW.1: The caster may decrease the temperature of any inanimate body of liquid of up to 1 cubic foot per level by up to 100°F (56°C) per round. Once the liquid begins to freeze it will not continue to cool, and will begin to warm naturally if the caster stops concentrating. (Temp. cannot be lower then -20°F[-29°C]).
ICE LAW.2: Any solid, inanimate, non-metal material can be cooled to -20°F (-29°C), at a rate of 1 cubic foot per round (cooling spreads evenly from initial point of cooling unless caster concentrates to direct spread).
ICE LAW.3: Creates a wall of intense cold (up to 10'x10'x1'), normally visible as mist condenses out of the air. Anyone passing through takes an A Cold critical (no RR).
ICE LAW.4: While this spell lasts, the caster can walk through ice as if it were air. The caster will not drop through ice if he enters it in the middle of a tall ice formation, as under his feet, the ice will still be solid for him and provide good footing.
ICE LAW.5: As Cool Solid, except material can be cooled to -200°F (-129°C), at a rate of cooling one cubic foot of material by 100°F (56°C) each round. The caster must concentrate to decrease the temperature (without concentration, the material will retain its current temperature for the duration of the spell).
ICE LAW.6: A bolt of ice is shot from the palm of the caster. Results are resolved on the Ice Bolt Table.
ICE LAW.7: A 1' ball of cold is shot from the palm of the caster. Upon reaching the selected target/location, it expands to affect a 20'R area. Resolve attacks on the Cold Ball Table.
ICE LAW.8: Creates a wall of ice up to 10'x10'x (2' at base, 1' at top); it can be melted through or chipped through or toppled if not against a wall.
ICE LAW.9: Creates a cube of cold (up to 10'x10'x10') similar to a Wall of Cold; it takes 1 complete round for the cube to form and be effective. Anyone passing through (or caught within) the cube takes an A Cold critical each round spent in the cube.
ICE LAW.10: As Wall of Cold, except the “wall” is 10' high and forms a 20'R circle (6" thick) with the caster at the center. The wall will not move with the caster.
ICE LAW.11: A bolt of ice is shot from the palm of the caster. Results are resolved on the Ice Bolt Table.
ICE LAW.12: Changes 10 cubic feet per level of water to ice, instantly.
ICE LAW.13: Chills metal to the point that it becomes extremely brittle (1 object only), giving it a -50 penalty to its strength and the object will be subject to a breakage check if it strikes another object or is struck. Anyone in direct skin-to-metal contact with the chilled metal will take a B Cold Critical each round contact is maintained.
ICE LAW.14: As Call Cold I, except the size is up to a 20' cube and the range is 20'.
ICE LAW.15: A bolt of ice is shot from the palm of the caster. Results are resolved on the Ice Bolt Table.
ICE LAW.16: Three bolts of ice are shot from the palm of the caster. They can strike up to three different targets as long as they are all within 60° of each other and are within the caster’s field of vision. Caster may apply his Directed Spell skill by dividing it as he chooses among the three bolts (e.g., a +120 OB could be split evenly into three +40 bolts or one +120 bolt and two +0 bolts or one +60, one +40, and one +20 bolt).
ICE LAW.17: As Wall of Cold, except it lasts for 1 minute per level and does a D Cold Critical to anyone who passes through it.
ICE LAW.18: As Call Cold I, except size is up to a 50' cube and the range is 50'.
ICE LAW.19: A bolt of ice is shot from the palm of the caster. Results are resolved on the Ice Bolt Table.
ICE LAW.20: As Cold Ball II, except area of effect is 40'R and the range is 300'.
ICE LAW.25: For as long as it continues to rain, this spell changes all rain within 1 mile of the caster to snow; radius decreases 500' for every 10°F (5.5°C) the ambient air temperature is above freezing (32°F) (0°C).
ICE LAW.30: Causes the ambient temperature in the area of effect to drop 1°F (0.6°C) every ten minutes with a maximum reduction equal to the caster’s level in degrees Fahrenheit (within a 1000'/lvl R).
ICE LAW.35: As Call Cold I, except size is up to a 100' cube and the range is 100'.
ICE LAW.40: As Cold Ball II, except area of effect is 60'R and the range is 500'.
ICE LAW.50: Caster can use any one lower level spell (on this list) each round.

LIGHT LAW.1: Beam of light (like a flashlight) springs from the caster’s palm; it has a 50' effective range. If the caster’s hand is closed into a fist, the light will “turn off”. If the caster’s fist is reopened before the end of the duration, the light will turn on again.
LIGHT LAW.2: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT LAW.3: Lights a 10'R area about the point touched.
LIGHT LAW.4: All shadows and darkness within the area of effect deepen, giving all Perception maneuvers involving seeing anything hidden/hiding in the area a penalty of -20. Area is not mobile.
LIGHT LAW.5: Causes a 10'R burst of intense light, all within are stunned (-50) for 1 round per 10 failure.
LIGHT LAW.6: Reduces illumination to a dark night in a 10'R area about the point touched.
LIGHT LAW.7: As Light I, except radius can be up to 50' (can be changed by concentrating 1 round).
LIGHT LAW.8: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT LAW.9: As Darkness I, except radius is 50'.
LIGHT LAW.10: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack.
LIGHT LAW.11: In conjunction with any Light or Darkness spell (i.e., this spell is cast and then the Light/ Darkness spell is cast) it can delay the action of that spell up to 24 hours; it can be triggered by one selected trigger (decided by the caster): time period, certain movements, certain sounds, touch, violent actions in the area, or any other trigger so long as the caster would be able to sense it if the caster remained at the area of effect.
LIGHT LAW.12: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT LAW.13: Ray of light of any color springs from caster’s palm; it can be up to 5 miles long.
LIGHT LAW.14: As Light I, except radius is 30', duration is 1 hour per level, and spell must be cast upon a non-living organic object, like a wooden staff or leather cap.
LIGHT LAW.15: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack.
LIGHT LAW.16: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
LIGHT LAW.17: Nullifies all magically created darkness in a 100'R, and lights that area as full daylight.
LIGHT LAW.18: Darkens a 100'R area, no light (except Utterlight) can exist within this radius.
LIGHT LAW.19: As Beacon V, except beacon can be up to 10 miles long.
LIGHT LAW.20: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack.
LIGHT LAW.25: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack. The caster can make the bolt turn once by up to 90° before striking the target (the caster must know the target’s location). The caster’s OB is modified by -25 when using this spell. However, this spell can be used to bypass a positional modifier – any DB bonus gained through the use of cover (partial/half/full soft cover; partial/half/full hard cover) is reduced to zero; a target that otherwise would be unable to be hit can be attacked this spell.
LIGHT LAW.30: A bolt of lightning is shot from the caster’s palm; resolve attack on the Lightning Bolt Attack Table as a Medium-sized attack. The caster can make the bolt make as many turns as necessary, with an OB penalty of -25 per turn, and go through openings (must be larger than 6" radius) before striking the target (the caster must know the target’s location). However, this spell can be used to bypass a positional modifier – any DB bonus gained through the use of cover (partial/half/full soft cover; partial/half/full hard cover) is reduced to zero; a target that otherwise would be unable to be hit can be attacked this spell.
LIGHT LAW.35: Caster is surrounded by a blazing electrical aura. This illuminates a 30' radius, but more importantly, it also provides a defensive (or rather, counter-offensive) effect. Anyone attacking the caster in melee receives an electrical critical of the same severity as that suffered by the caster. This is not scaled by target size. If a massive troll does an E+A critical to a Magician surrounded by a Corona, the troll takes an E+A Electricity critical in return.
LIGHT LAW.40: As Utterlight, except that duration is 10 minutes per level and the radius illuminated is 10' per level.
LIGHT LAW.50: Caster can use one lower level spell (on this list) each round.

WATER LAW.1: Condenses 1 cubic foot of water from the surrounding air. Condensation can be channeled into any suitable receptacle, including caster’s cupped hands.
WATER LAW.2: Creates dense fog within the area of effect. Treat as a heavy fog as described in RMCL Section 15.7. Fog disperses naturally after creation (this can mean lingering for days in suitable environments).
WATER LAW.3: Creates a wall of water up to 10'x10'x1'. This wall requires 2 AP to cross, the pace of anyone moving through it at more than a Walk comes out with his pace reduced by two (e.g, a Run going in would be a Walk pace coming out) to a minimum of a Walk, and attacks through the wall suffer a -80 penalty.
WATER LAW.4: A bolt of water is shot from the caster’s palm; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table.
WATER LAW.5: Disperses fog within the area of effect. If not all of a fog is dispersed (i.e., the fog covers a greater area than the area of effect for this spell), the fog will refill the area of effect, reducing the cleared radius by 10' every 1-5 minutes (varying depending on the heaviness of the fog and ambient humidity).
WATER LAW.6: Target’s fluids are immediately replenished, eliminating any dehydration that the target may have been suffering. This spell also meets the target’s water needs for the next 24 hours, not including losses directly due to magic (i.e., it will not defend against a Dessication spell, but will cure its effects if cast after).
WATER LAW.7: A bolt of water is shot from the caster’s palm; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table, except that if the caster knows the Fire Law list to 7th level, this bolt becomes scalding hot, trailing thick tendrils of steam behind it. It uses the Water Bolt Table, but in addition to the normal results, it does an additional Steam critical one level of severity less than the usual critical.
WATER LAW.8: All water within a 100'R is calmed; waves are cut by 20' in the center and less towards the perimeter. This will negate the effects of currents in the area of effect.
WATER LAW.9: An area of water is made hostile to any air-breather who intrudes upon it. Powerful undertows will appear out of nowhere and sudden currents seem to grab at the victim. Swimming maneuvers are made at -100 within the area of effect.
WATER LAW.10: As Waterwall, except the caster need not concentrate and the duration is 1 min/level.
WATER LAW.11: A bolt of water is shot from the caster’s palm; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table.
WATER LAW.12: A region of water becomes slightly denser, making it easier to float. All Swimming maneuvers to avoid drowning or to move at or near the surface of the water gain a +30 bonus.
WATER LAW.13: If there are clouds in the sky, it rains outdoors for the duration of the spell.
WATER LAW.14: A bolt of water is shot from the caster’s palm; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table, except that if the caster knows the Fire Law list to 14th level, this bolt becomes scalding hot, trailing thick tendrils of steam behind it. It uses the Water Bolt Table, but in addition to the normal results, it does an additional Steam critical one level of severity less than the usual critical.
WATER LAW.15: A bolt of water is shot from the caster’s palm; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table.
WATER LAW.16: Three bolts of water are shot from the palm of the caster. They can strike up to three different targets as long as they are all within 60° of each other and are within the caster’s field of vision. Caster may apply his Directed Spell skill by dividing it as he chooses among the three bolts (e.g., a +120 OB could be split evenly into three +40 bolts or one +120 bolt and two +0 bolts or one +60, one +40, and one +20 bolt).
WATER LAW.17: The area of effect for this spell is the water immediately surrounding the boat that the caster is on (where “boat” should be interpreted loosely; a log is a “boat” for purposes of this spell if the caster is riding it on water). For as long as the caster concentrates, the speed of the boat can be increased by 25' per round (approximately 3 miles per hour).
WATER LAW.18: As Calm Water, except radius is 100'/ lvl and waves are cut by 50' in the center and caster need not concentrate.
WATER LAW.19: As Quench, except affects up to one target/ level and can target anyone within 100'.
WATER LAW.20: Creates a whirlpool with a 50 foot radius in any liquid body that will draw in any objects in the liquid up to 500' away. Objects capable of moving under their own power may make a Very Hard maneuver to resist the pull of the whirlpool.
WATER LAW.25: Caster can part water up to 100' deep and 100'/ lvl long and 10' wide at bottom (50' at top).
WATER LAW.30: Summons forces of nature in a fierce sea storm (must be created over a large body of water). This storm will include waves of 20-50', heavy rain, and winds of 25-60 mph. The storm can be delayed up to 1 hour/level after casting the spell. After the storm has been summoned, it will dissipate normally.
WATER LAW.35: As Command Current, except speed is increased by 50' per round.
WATER LAW.40: As Whirlpool, except caster need not concentrate as the Maelstrom lasts 10 minutes per level on its own and the maneuver to resist the pull is Extremely Hard.
WATER LAW.50: Caster can use one lower level spell (on this list) each round.

WIND LAW.1: Causes a light breeze as long as the caster concentrates. The breeze moves any gasses in the area as the caster directs, up to 20' per round.
WIND LAW.2: Creates a wall of dense churning air up to 10'x10'x3'. This wall requires 1 AP to cross, the pace of anyone moving through it at more than a Walk comes out with his pace reduced by one (e.g, a Run going in would be a Jog coming out), and attacks through the wall suffer a -50 penalty.
WIND LAW.3: By concentrating, the caster can remove most of the oxygen from the area of effect. After three rounds of concentration, all targets in the area of effect must make an RR each round in the area of effect or fall asleep (1 round per 10 failure). All fire spells in the area suffer a -20 penalty (or are 20% less effective in the case of non-attack spells).
WIND LAW.4: Creates a 5'R cloud of charged gas particles. The cloud takes one round to form, so anyone in the radius when it is cast may make a maneuver to move out of the radius without taking a critical; however, after that anyone within the radius at anytime in the round takes the critical indicated (a maximum of one per round). Following the initial formation round, the cloud delivers a C Electricity critical to all within the area of effect on the first and second rounds, a B critical on the third and fourth rounds, and an A critical on the fifth and sixth rounds, after which it dissipates. It drifts with the wind.
WIND LAW.5: Stops all generalized air movement up to winds of 30 mph and cuts higher winds by 30 mph in a 10' radius.
WIND LAW.6: As Stun Cloud I, except radius is 10'.
WIND LAW.7: Creates a 5' radius of near vacuum; all within the radius take a B Impact critical as the air leaves and rushes back in (if they fail an RR).
WIND LAW.8: As Air Stop I, except radius is 20'.
WIND LAW.9: As Slumber Mist, except for the duration and that it drifts with the wind.
WIND LAW.10: As Stun Cloud I, except radius is 20'.
WIND LAW.11: As Stun Cloud I, except delivers an E critical on rounds 1 and 2, a D on rounds 3 and 4, a C on rounds 5 and 6, a B on rounds 7 and 8, and an A on rounds 9 and 10, after which it dissipates.
WIND LAW.12: As Vacuum I, except radius is 10'.
WIND LAW.13: As Air Stop I, except radius is 100'.
WIND LAW.14: A 10'R whirlwind is created, taking one round to form. It delivers an A Impact critical to all inside (every round). It requires 2 AP to enter or exit the whirlwind, and pace is limited to a walk within it and all Movement maneuvers are Very Hard at a minimum. The caster can move the whirlwind 10' per round (does not require concentration, but caster must be able to see the whirlwind).
WIND LAW.15: As Death Cloud I, except radius is 10' and range is 40'.
WIND LAW.16: Creates an area of constantly shifting winds. Any missile passing through this region suffers a -100 penalty to its OB and elemental bolt attacks suffer this penalty as well, except for Shock and Lightning Bolts. Any sailing vessel caught in these crosswinds will be unable to make any significant progress.
WIND LAW.17: As Vacuum I, except radius is 20'.
WIND LAW.18: As Vacuum I, except delivers a D Impact critical.
WIND LAW.19: As Stun Cloud IV, except by concentrating the caster can move it 10'/round up to 100' away.
WIND LAW.20: Allows the caster to change the direction of the wind within the radius.
WIND LAW.25: A hard wind comes forth from caster’s outstretched arms, fanning out to reach a 100' wide span at a distance of 200'. All within the cone receive a B Unbalancing critical.
WIND LAW.30: As Vacuum I, except radius is 40'.
WIND LAW.35: Summons forces of nature in a fierce thunderstorm which includes heavy rain, 25-60 mph winds, lightning (random) and a blizzard (if correct climate). Can be delayed up to 1 hour/level after casting.
WIND LAW.40: As Death Cloud I, except radius is 25' and range is 100'.
WIND LAW.50: Caster can use one lower level spell (on this list) each round.

DARKNESS.1: Reduces illumination to a dark night in a 20'R area about the point touched.
DARKNESS.2: Target can see up to 100' as if it were daylight, so long as there is some light.
DARKNESS.3: Caster can vary the intensity of darkness in the area, but he cannot lighten the area past its natural state.
DARKNESS.4: As Darkness II, except radius is 50'.
DARKNESS.5: As Darkness II, except radius is 100'.
DARKNESS.6: As Nightvision, except any darkness can be seen through. No light at all is needed for this spell to work.
DARKNESS.7: As Dark Control II, except range and radius are 50'.
DARKNESS.8: Caster can create the visual illusion of either shadowy figures or actual shadows (as many as the caster’s level); they will move when he concentrates.
DARKNESS.9: As Darkness II, except radius is 300'.
DARKNESS.10: Darkens a 20'R area, no light (except Utterlight) can exist within this radius.
DARKNESS.11: As Dark Control II, except range and radius are 100'.
DARKNESS.12: As Darkvision, except the target can see as far as he would in normal daylight.
DARKNESS.13: As Lesser Utterdark, except radius is 100'.
DARKNESS.14: As Darkness II, except radius is 500'.
DARKNESS.15: Creates a “cloud” of darkness that has a 100'R and drifts with the wind. The darkness can vary in intensity from an overcast day to the dark of night.
DARKNESS.16: As Nightvision, except affects a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
DARKNESS.17: As Lesser Utterdark, except radius is 200'.
DARKNESS.18: As Darkvision, except affects a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
DARKNESS.19: As Clouds of Darkness I, except for area of effect.
DARKNESS.20: As Darkness II, except radius is 1,000'.
DARKNESS.25: As Lesser Utterdark, except radius is 300'.
DARKNESS.30: As Darkness II, except radius is 100' per level of the caster.
DARKNESS.35: As Darkvision True, except affects a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
DARKNESS.40: As Darkness V, except duration is permanent.
DARKNESS.50: As Clouds of Darkness I, except radius is 1 mile per level of the caster.

DARK SUMMONS.1: The caster can attune himself to a small creature of animal intelligence (i.e., with the Animalistic flaw) to serve as his familiar. The caster must obtain the creature (which can be no more than 10% of caster’s own mass) through normal means and cast the spell on the animal once each day for 1 week (associating with the animal for 2 hours each day). The caster can then control the familiar and view the world through its senses by concentrating on it (must be within 50' per caster level). If the animal is killed, the caster will have a -25 modification to all actions for 2 weeks.
DARK SUMMONS.2: Caster can instantly summon a first level non-intelligent (i.e., possessing the Animalistic or Mindless flaw) living creature, which appears somewhere with the spell’s range. The caster can specify the general type of creature, but exactly what the creature is should be determined randomly (e.g., the caster could specify “four-legged, hoofed” and could get a zebra, horse, camel, etc.). If the creature can understand the caster’s communication, the creature can be controlled by normal communication. Otherwise, control is maintained through concentration of the caster. If the creature summoned is used for a task that is not dangerous (in its own perception), the duration for this spell is 10 minutes per level. However, if the creature is ever put into a dangerous situation, the duration immediately drops to 1 round per level. At the end of the spell’s duration, the summoned creature will disappear back to whence it came.
DARK SUMMONS.3: This spell is cast upon the caster’s familiar. However, the familiar must be a type of animal that is usually associated with evil in the caster’s culture. This spell transfers part of the caster’s “life” into the familiar. This spell must be cast upon the familiar every day for a month (associating with the animal for 2 hours a day). The familiar retains all of its old abilities and it gains special abilities. The familiar will become a malformed version of the animal it once was (more grotesque). The caster can view the world through the senses of the creature at a range of 250' per level. The creatures AT changes to 3 (if not already higher), and it gains a +10 to its DB and OB. The caster can cast spells through the familiar as if the caster were actually where the familiar is (this includes casting “self” spells on the familiar): range for this ability is 50' per level. The creature will make all of its RRs at half the caster’s level or its own level, whichever is higher. The familiar can be sent on long-range missions, although it will be limited in its ability to interpret ambiguous instructions or adapt to unexpected events. It can always find its way back to the caster through their bond unless the caster is magically hidden. If the familiar dies, the caster will lose one quarter of his Power Points and Concussion Hits for 1-5 weeks (and these cannot be restored by any means until the time has passed).
DARK SUMMONS.4: As Summons I, except the caster chooses one of the following options: a) the level of the summoned creature is increased by one, b) an extra 1st level creature can be summoned, or c) the duration can be doubled. When applying options to the higher level Summons spells, option “a” can only be applied to one creature at a time (i.e., two 2nd level creatures takes three options: one for the second creature and one each to raise the creatures to 2nd level).
DARK SUMMONS.5: Caster can bind one creature (up to second level) with animal intelligence (i.e., with the Animalistic flaw). The bound creature must follow the commands of the caster (the caster does not have to concentrate). The caster can only have as many creatures bound as he has levels. If the creature is ever outside the range of the spell, the spell is dispelled.
DARK SUMMONS.6: As Summons II, except two options are chosen.
DARK SUMMONS.7: The target of this spell is any creature with animal intelligence (i.e., with the Animalistic flaw) that has been bound (with a Binding spell).
