GAS ALTERATION.4: Creates a near vacuum with a five foot radius; all within this radius take an A Impact critical (if they fail an RR), as air leaves and rushes back in.
GAS ALTERATION.5: Stops all generalized air movement up to winds of 30 mph and cuts higher winds by 30 mph in a 10' radius.
GAS ALTERATION.6: As Thick Fog II, except radius is 100'.
GAS ALTERATION.7: As Airwall, except has a set duration of 1 min/ level and does not require concentration.
GAS ALTERATION.8: A bolt of fire is shot from a fire source within 20' of the caster; results are determined on the Fire Bolt Table. Range modifier is based on the distance from the fire source to the bolt’s target.
GAS ALTERATION.9: As Vacuum A, except results in a B Impact critical.
GAS ALTERATION.10: As Air Stop I, except radius is 50'.
GAS ALTERATION.11: As Thick Fog II, except radius is 300'.
GAS ALTERATION.12: All gas within 10' of caster is converted to breathable air.
GAS ALTERATION.13: As Vacuum A, except results in a C Impact critical.
GAS ALTERATION.14: Enriches a 50' radius of air with extra oxygen; within this radius all animal life receives a +20 bonus to their OBs and fire attacks deliver double the normal number of hits.
GAS ALTERATION.15: Creates a whirlwind about caster; it moves with the caster and has a 10'R. No missile attacks can penetrate it and any movement (except for caster’s) into the whirlwind costs 2 AP and slows movement to a Walk pace, melee or elemental attacks on the caster through the whirlwind suffer a -50 penalty to OB.
GAS ALTERATION.16: As Bolt of Fire I, except range increment is 75'.
GAS ALTERATION.17: As Vacuum A, except causes a D Impact critical.
GAS ALTERATION.18: As Vacuum B, except radius is 10'.
GAS ALTERATION.19: Allows the caster to change the direction of the wind within the radius.
GAS ALTERATION.20: As Thick Fog II, except duration is 1 hour per level and the radius is 100' per level.
GAS ALTERATION.25: As Vacuum A, except causes an E Impact critical.
GAS ALTERATION.30: Caster has complete control of clouds within area of effect (includes fog); storm clouds can be gathered and made to rain (or snow or hail in suitable conditions), but they cannot be created.
GAS ALTERATION.35: As Vacuum E, except radius is 10'.
GAS ALTERATION.40: Creates a cloud of toxic gas. Any living thing coming within the cloud must make an RR versus poison each round or suffer a cumulative -10 penalty and take 2d10 damage from the effects of the gas. Treat the penalty as organ damage (lungs) for treatment/healing purposes and the final penalty as a single injury. Level of the poison is the level of the caster. The cloud takes one round to form, but the gas is barely visible (Very Hard Perception maneuver to notice by sight). Those in the cloud during the formation round will have their breathing irritated but suffer no damage if they leave the cloud before the next round.
GAS ALTERATION.50: May transmute 1,000 cubic feet of gas (no part can be more than 20' away) into another non-magical gas that the caster has a sample of. This transmutation requires eight hours of uninterrupted work.

HIDING.1: Causes caster to appear blurred to attackers, granting a +10 to the caster’s DB.
HIDING.2: A single object is made invisible (1 garment, 1 naked body, etc.); until 24 hrs pass or target is struck by a violent blow (being hit by a weapon, falling, etc.) or target makes a violent move (i.e., an attack) or target casts a spell of type E or F.
HIDING.3: Caster and objects on the caster’s person appear to be in shadow and thus are almost invisible in dark areas (in many situations this could be handled with a Stalking bonus of between +25 and +75).
HIDING.4: Creates a 1'R area into and out of which sound cannot travel. As explained in Section 10.17, this spell can be cast on an individual target, which the spell will then follow; this target gains +25 to Stalking attempts, but likewise automatically fails any Perception attempts based on hearing alone and suffers a -50 to Perception rolls where hearing is a factor (e.g., to detect someone Stalking the target). Note that this does not interfere with spell-casting (the target can still speak, even yell, the sound is simply unable to leave the radius of the Quiet - certain spells like Ultrasonics may have their range limited to the interior of the Quiet radius, however).
HIDING.5: As Unseen I, except everything within 1' of the target is invisible as long as it is within the 1'R and none of the Unseen I termination conditions occur. The first time an Unseen I termination condition occurs, the target will become visible for one round and then become invisible again. If an Unseen I condition happens again, the spell ends. A target rendered invisible by this spell therefore can make one violent move (an attack) or cast one spell of type E or F or be struck once by a violent blow without losing the invisibility.
HIDING.6: As Resilient Invisibility I, except the caster can vary the radius up to 1'. This makes the invisible target harder to see by reducing the “fringe effect”.
HIDING.7: Creates a 1,000 square foot screen on which the caster can place any static scene; this scene seems 3-dimensional and normal.
HIDING.8: Caster’s apparent location is offset from the actual location; all attacks have no effect 10% of the time. Each time a foe misses due to this effect, the chance of that foe missing again goes down 5%.
HIDING.9: As Resilient Invisibility I, except target is also undetectable by smell and sound.
HIDING.10: Creates a duplicate of the caster; if the caster concentrates, it will move as willed; otherwise, it does exactly as the caster does. The duplicate cannot move more than 100’ away from the caster. If the caster concentrates, he can “merge” the duplicate with himself and then split back apart again (making it difficult to discern which one is the “real” caster).
HIDING.11: As Resilient Invisibility I, except the constant radius is 10'. Note that anything that exits the radius will become visible again.
HIDING.12: As Displacement I, except base chance of missing is 20%.
HIDING.13: Caster is flattened until becoming virtually two-dimensional. This allows the caster to slide through cracks and makes the caster effectively invisible when viewed from the side.
HIDING.14: Caster can merge into any solid, inanimate material. While merged, the caster cannot move, perceive, or cast spells. When the caster emerges from the material, it is possible to emerge from any side or face of the material, although this is limited to moving “through” no more than the caster’s own body size plus two feet worth of material. The caster can exit at any time up to the end of spell duration (at which time the caster automatically emerges at the entrance point).
HIDING.15: As Resilient Invisibility II, except the invisibility can survive (level/5) termination actions. For example, if cast by a 15th level caster, the invisibility will survive three (15/5) termination events, e.g. a total of three violent moves, spell casting attempts or being struck violently, thus the caster could make an attack, be hit by an opponent, and cast a spell without losing the invisibility, but if the caster made another attack or cast another E or F spell or suffered another hit, the invisibility would end .
HIDING.16: As Displacement I, except base chance of missing is 30%.
HIDING.17: Caster may pass through any inanimate material up to 1 foot/ level. It takes 1 round to pass through 2 feet of material.
HIDING.18: Caster’s actions are extremely subtle for the duration of this spell. Any form of non-magical detection or observation regarding the Mystic and his activities suffers a -50 penalty. The caster also may hide spell-casting without the normal Subtlety penalty to his spell-casting roll (and the -50 is applied to attempts to detect this casting as well).
HIDING.19: As Merging, except caster can turn within the material and can perceive the outside world if within 6" of the surface.
HIDING.20: As Displacement I, except base chance of missing is 40%.
HIDING.25: Caster and objects on his person cannot be detected by any “Detect...” spells.
HIDING.30: As Displacement I, except base chance of missing is 50%.
HIDING.35: Caster disappears into a private world. This place is largely featureless, but by concentrating, the caster can view (and listen) from the point of departure. The caster may also create any material objects desired, although anything not consumed by the caster will disappear upon leaving the dimensional closet (so the caster may eat, drink, take an antidote to a poison, etc., but cannot arm himself or emerge with great wealth). The caster will reappear in the same place when the duration of the spell expires or when the caster chooses to cancel the spell. If the point of departure is now occupied, the caster will be teleported D10x100 feet in a random direction.
HIDING.40: As Displacement I, except base chance of missing is 60%.
HIDING.50: Caster can “Merge” into a material and may observe surrounding activity, and is affected by Unpresence, Nondetect, and Greater Resilient Invisibility all with this one spell.

LIQUID ALTERATION.1: The caster may alter the temperature of any inanimate body of liquid of up to 1 cubic foot per level by 50°F [28°C] per round of concentration. Once the liquid begins to boil or freeze, it will not continue to change temperature, but will begin to warm or cool naturally if the caster stops concentrating. Caster is immune to the heat/cold thus generated.
LIQUID ALTERATION.2: Removes all sediment and dissolved substances from a liquid.
LIQUID ALTERATION.3: All targeted liquid (up to a maximum of 1000 cubic feet per level) is evaporated (i.e., boiled away and turned into heated gas) at a rate of one hundred cubic feet of liquid per round of concentration.
LIQUID ALTERATION.4: Creates a wall of water up to 10'x10'x1'. This wall requires 2 AP to cross, the pace of anyone moving through it at more than a Walk comes out with his pace reduced by two (e.g, a Run going in would be a Walk pace coming out) to a minimum of a Walk, and attacks through the wall suffer a -80 penalty. See Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.
LIQUID ALTERATION.5: A bolt of water is shot from a water source within 20' of the caster; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table. Range modifier is based on the distance from the water source to the bolt’s target.
LIQUID ALTERATION.6: Creates a corridor through liquid up to 100' long, 3' wide, and 10' deep (must be open at the top).
LIQUID ALTERATION.7: If there are clouds in the sky, it rains outdoors for the duration of the spell.
LIQUID ALTERATION.8: All water within a 100'R is calmed; waves are cut by 20' in the center and less towards the perimeter. This will negate the effects of currents in the area of effect.
LIQUID ALTERATION.9: Creates a wave moving away from the caster; wave is 1' high per level in the center and 10' per level wide.
LIQUID ALTERATION.10: As Waterwall, except caster need not concentrate and the duration is 1 minute per level.
LIQUID ALTERATION.11: As Water Corridor I, except limit is 300'x4'x50' deep.
LIQUID ALTERATION.12: Changes any liquid into fresh water.
LIQUID ALTERATION.13: Creates a whirlpool with a 20 foot radius in any liquid body that will draw in any objects in the liquid up to 200' away. Objects capable of moving under their own power may make a Very Hard maneuver to resist the pull of the whirlpool.
LIQUID ALTERATION.14: Creates a tunnel through liquid that is 5' in diameter and 100' long.
LIQUID ALTERATION.15: As Calm Water, except radius is 100'/ lvl and waves are cut by 50' in the center and caster need not concentrate.
LIQUID ALTERATION.16: The area of effect for this spell is the water immediately surrounding the boat that the caster is on (where “boat” should be interpreted loosely; a log is a “boat” for purposes of this spell if the caster is riding it on water). For as long as the caster concentrates, the speed of the boat will be increased by 25' per round (approximately 3 miles per hour).
LIQUID ALTERATION.17: Creates a bubble of air (10'R) around the caster and others, which will carry them in up to 100' depth of water (air is replenished). Caster can direct the motion of the bubble at a rate of 30'/round (may be adjusted by the presence of (un) favorable water currents. If/when the caster stops concentrating, the bubble will rise to the surface at the same rate (30'/round). If the caster resumes concentrating before the bubble surfaces, the bubble may be controlled again. All objects inside the bubble will rise with it. After reaching the surface, the bubble will burst.
LIQUID ALTERATION.18: A bolt of water is shot from the caster’s palm; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table.
LIQUID ALTERATION.19: Caster can cause up to one cubic foot per level of liquid into a magical acid strong enough to corrode an equal volume of metal or cause an A Acid critical to someone splashed with the acid or a D Acid critical each round immersed in the acid (with a C, a B, and an A critical coming in that order during the three rounds after getting out).
LIQUID ALTERATION.20: As Water Corridor I, except limit is 100' per level long, 6' wide and 100' deep and the caster need not concentrate.
LIQUID ALTERATION.25: As Water Tunnel, except limit is 6' in diameter and 100' per level long and the caster need not concentrate.
LIQUID ALTERATION.30: Caster can divert a water source or part of a water source into a stream which can be up to 15'x6' and as long as the range of this spell.
LIQUID ALTERATION.35: As Water Bubble, except that caster need only concentrate on the desired route for one round and the bubble will “pilot” itself until the destination is reached and the radius of the bubble may be up to 20' in radius and the maximum speed of the bubble is 50'/round and there is no depth limit.
LIQUID ALTERATION.40: As Call Rain, except for area of effect and duration.
LIQUID ALTERATION.50: May transmute 1 cubic foot of liquid into another non-magical liquid that the caster has a sample of. This transmutation requires eight hours of uninterrupted work.

MYSTICAL CHANGE.1: Caster studies and memorizes the appearance and mannerisms of a being, for later use with higher level spells on this list. The caster must observe the target for five minutes after casting the spell in order to complete the study. The caster can only have as many forms studied as he has ranks in this list. Caster may choose to forget a studied form at any time to make room for replacements.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.2: Allows caster to alter the form of his face. He can take on the exact face of another being if he has used Study Individual on the being he wishes to copy.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.3: Caster can alter his own form to the form of any desired humanoid race within his own Size category. The form can be that of a particular individual that has been the target of Study Individual; this does not include mannerisms, but only appearance. Note that only the physical form is gained (i.e., a target that becomes a Dwarf would not receive a Dwarf’s ability to see in the dark). Non-magical clothing will refit itself to the new form, but other equipment will not change, with the exception of prosthetics added by means of the Lay Healer Base list Prosthetics.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.4: For the purposes of mental or magical detections, caster appears to be of any race with which the caster is familiar.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.5: [RR Mod.: -50] Caster fools a magic item into reacting to the caster as if the caster were of another race, sex, Profession, religion, etc. in order to make use (or better use) of the item. This does not allow the caster to use a PP multiplier or Spell Adder for a realm he does not actually use, although it will allow use of a PP multiplier that works for only one of his realms.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.6: As Minor Changing, except form need not be humanoid, but must be a living organic thing.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.7: As Misfeel Kind, except caster’s profession may be misrepresented.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.8: Caster can breathe water, air, or any gas at will.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.9: As Minor Changing, except form may be one Size category smaller than the caster’s.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.10: [RR Mod: -50] Caster can speak mentally with any sentient target, and to the target, it will seem as if the caster was speaking in the target’s primary language.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.11: As Misfeel Kind, except caster’s level may be misrepresented (to an upper limit of twice the caster’s actual level).
MYSTICAL CHANGE.12: As Major Changing, except a specific being who has been the target of Study Individual can be duplicated in both appearance and mannerisms.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.13: Caster becomes undetectable by Presence spells or related abilities.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.14: Allows caster to use all of the “Misfeel” spells at once.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.15: As Major Changing, except caster can alter forms at will, by concentrating for one round/change.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.16: As Minor Changing, except form may be one Size category larger than the caster’s.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.17: As Impersonation, except caster can alter forms at will, by concentrating for one round/change.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.18: As Major Changing, except for duration.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.20: As Unpresence Self, except caster does not have to concentrate.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.25: As Misfeel, except it has a ten minute/level duration and does not require concentration.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.30: As Misfeel, except caster can misrepresent his presence and power, so that he seems to be a minor deity. Even those viewing with normal senses will be given an impression of superhuman power and majesty.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.35: Caster can alter his own form to the form of any desired living thing. The form can be that of a particular individual that has been the target of Study Individual, in which case the caster may have the mannerisms of that individual as well. The caster gains all natural abilities of the form taken, but not magical abilities. Non-magical clothing will change form to fit the caster’s new body, or may join the rest of items worn or carried, which merge into the caster’s body for the duration of the spell. If the caster dies, the spell immediately ends.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.40: As Shapechanging, except caster can alter forms at will, by concentrating for one round/change.
MYSTICAL CHANGE.50: Caster develops an entire false persona and places his own persona deep in his subconscious. To all detection attempts (except, perhaps, Mind Probe), the caster seems to be the false persona. The caster has no control over his actions (except for having designed the persona now in control), until the spell ends. The false persona can be a specific individual if Study Individual has been cast once/day (for 30 days) on that individual. The caster must determine a set period after which the spell will end and may also specify one triggering event that can cancel the spell before that period expires. The caster will remember everything that happened while the false persona was in control.

SOLID ALTERATION.1: If the caster holds one end of a rope, he can cause the rope to move up to its length in any direction and to tie itself in knots (it cannot attack or tie up a living being).
SOLID ALTERATION.2: Warms 1 cubic foot of any solid, inanimate material per level up to 500°F (260°C) at a rate of 1 cubic foot heated by 100°F (56°C) per round of concentration (without concentration, the material will remain at its current temperature for the remainder of the duration). The caster is immune to this heat.
SOLID ALTERATION.3: Any solid, inanimate, non-metal material can be cooled to -20°F (-29°C), at a rate of 1 cubic foot per round (cooling spreads evenly from initial point of cooling unless caster concentrates to direct spread).
SOLID ALTERATION.4: Any previous cracks or flaws in material up to 10'x10'x10' section will extend to their limit.
SOLID ALTERATION.5: Can cause a door to expand or contract due to subtle temperature changes; door can be jammed or loosened (a special modification of +/- 50 to maneuvers to force the door can be granted).
SOLID ALTERATION.6: Causes any wood to ignite and burn. All wood ignited must be within 1' of caster’s palm.
SOLID ALTERATION.7: Causes any one object of up to 1 cubic foot per level of the caster to be much more resistant to damage. It will resist destructive spells as if the RR was being made by the caster and it will have a +50 bonus to any normal rolls against breakage.
SOLID ALTERATION.8: As Heat Solid I, except the range is 50'.
SOLID ALTERATION.9: Any solid, inanimate, non-metal material can be cooled to -200°F (-129°C), at a rate of (1 cubic foot and -100°F/56°C)/round. The caster must concentrate to decrease the temperature (without concentration, the material will retain its current temperature for the duration of the spell).
SOLID ALTERATION.10: Creates a wall of ice up to 10'x10'x (2' at base, 1' at top); it can be melted through or chipped through or toppled if not against a wall. Requires a source of water or ice within 10'. See Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.
SOLID ALTERATION.11: Creates a doorway through any solid, inanimate material; it can be up to 3'x6'x1'.
SOLID ALTERATION.12: Will turn 100 cubic feet of stone to packed earth, 100 cubic feet of earth to mud, 100 cubic feet of mud to earth, or 100 cubic feet of earth to stone. The transformation takes 3 rounds to complete.
SOLID ALTERATION.13: Causes a non-metal, inanimate object to shatter (up to 1 cubic foot in size). All within 5' radius take an A Impact critical; anyone holding the object takes a C Impact critical.
SOLID ALTERATION.14: As Solid Door I, except size is 4'x8'x5'
SOLID ALTERATION.15: Caster’s hands can mold up to one cubic foot of any solid, inanimate material as if it were putty or clay. The material hardens to normal consistency when the caster is finished. Quality of results depends on caster’s skill and time invested.
SOLID ALTERATION.16: One cubic foot of any solid, inanimate material becomes very brittle. This causes the object to break if struck (the GM may rule that certain objects get an RR to resist breakage).
SOLID ALTERATION.17: Disintegrates (i.e., destroys without a residue) a target of up to 100 cubic feet of stone.
SOLID ALTERATION.18: As Strengthen Material, except object can be up to 100 cubic feet per level in size.
SOLID ALTERATION.20: Creates a tunnel through solid, inanimate material that is 4' in diameter and 5'/level long.
SOLID ALTERATION.25: As Solid Door, except size is 6'x12'x10'.
SOLID ALTERATION.30: As Solid Tunnel, except that it is permanent and size is 3'x6'x (1'/level).
SOLID ALTERATION.35: As Mold Solid, but working on a larger scale, suitable for monuments, architectural components, etc.
SOLID ALTERATION.40: Caster becomes able to work non-magical metals with his bare hands, needing no other tools to give it the shape and qualities desired (gaining a +20 to any appropriate maneuvers rolled). This includes being able to create alloys if the necessary components are available. If this spell is used in conjunction with proper equipment, a +35 bonus may be gained to appropriate maneuvers.
SOLID ALTERATION.50: Transmutes up to 1 ounce of any solid material into another non-magical solid material that the caster has a sample of. This transmutation requires eight hours of uninterrupted work.

FLESH DESTRUCTION.1: A random part of a random limb is sprained. If it is part of a leg: movement is cut by 25%, combat is at -10. If it is part of an arm, combat is modified by -20.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.2: A random limb is in intense pain. If it is a leg, the target cannot walk (target may crawl at 10% of walking movement rate). If it is an arm, that arm cannot be used.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.3: The bones and tissues of the target’s body are disrupted as if the target had fallen a long distance. If the target’s RR fails by 1-10, the target takes an A Impact critical; increase the severity of the critical for each 10 by which the RR is failed (i.e. 11-20 = B, 21-30 = C, 31-40 = D, 41+ = E).
FLESH DESTRUCTION.4: One of the target’s joints locks. Target suffers as in Limb Pain, and in addition a moving target that is afflicted with leg lock will fall down; if a target with arm lock is carrying anything, it is dropped.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.5: A random limb is broken. A broken arm incurs a -40 penalty, while a broken leg results in -25 and movement is reduced by 50%.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.6: As Touch of Disruption, except range is 20'.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.7: Target’s skin will flake and peel (on entire body). There is no tactical penalty, but it ruins the appearance of the target, resulting in a -25 to -75 on social interactions, depending on the importance of appearance. Lasts until dispelled and 1 month passes (recovery time may be reduced through magical healing).
FLESH DESTRUCTION.8: As Touch of Disruption, except range is 50'.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.9: One of the target’s ears (randomly chosen) is disrupted. Hearing is at 50% of normal until cured (-25 to Perception involving hearing, -50 to Perception only involving hearing). If both ears go, the target will be rendered deaf.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.10: One of the target’s limbs (random) will wither and die. Target loses 5% of the use of the limb per day; when the total reaches 100%, the limb falls off. Can be cured through flesh and nerve repair spells suitable for the degree of lost use (e.g., at 25% loss, treat as a -25 injury penalty, thus requiring Medium Flesh Relief and Medium Nerve Relief) before reaching 80%, after which it must be regenerated. If the limb is a leg, movement is reduced by half the percentage lost (e.g., if a leg is 60% withered, movement is cut by 30%). If the limb is an arm, combat suffers a -1 penalty per 2% withered (e.g., if an arm is 80% withered, all combat with that arm will suffer a -40 penalty).
FLESH DESTRUCTION.11: As Ear Disruption, except an eye is affected and the penalties are to Perception involving sight.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.12: One of the target’s lungs collapses. This restricts the target to half of normal activity for all physical activity (treat as 2 AP per round and half normal BMR) until the lung is repaired.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.13: As Limb Death, except a random muscle is affected (not muscle organs, e.g., not the heart).
FLESH DESTRUCTION.14: As Limb Death, except a random bone (not part of spine or skull) gradually disintegrates.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.15: One of the Black Channel I spells may be used (see Section 10.7); the Gamemaster must decide which one(s) may be used on the basis of culture and world system.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.16: Target’s skin splits and begins to bleed. One bleeding wound opens for every 10 by which the target’s RR was failed, with each bleeding 1-5 hits per round (roll randomly for each wound).
FLESH DESTRUCTION.17: As one of Sprain Limb, Limb Pain, Lock Joint, Break Limb, Skin Death, or Ear Disruption, except with a range of 300'.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.18: Target must be dead; the spell causes a body to decompose almost instantaneously, including the bones or other hard parts, crumbling into a fertile dust.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.19: As any lower level spell other than Disruption or Black Channel spells, except that it may be cast upon as many targets as the caster has levels.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.20: The target’s bones will gradually petrify; a loss of activity (as in Limb Death) occurs due to loss of blood production. Treat the loss of use as a penalty to all physical maneuvers and all Endurance rolls. At 100%, this effect becomes fatal.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.25: As Touch of Disruption, except range is 100'.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.30: As Black Channel I, except one of the Black Channel II spells may be used.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.35: As Touch of Disruption, except range is 300' and delivers an E Impact critical if the target fails to resist.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.40: As Black Channel I, except that it may be cast upon as many targets as the caster has levels.
FLESH DESTRUCTION.50: As Black Channel I, except one of the Black Channel III spells may be used.

FLUID DESTRUCTION.3: Causes 1000 cubic feet of liquid to rapidly evaporate over the course of 1 hour.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.4: Instantly disintegrates 100 cubic feet of water.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.5: All water within a 100'R is calmed; waves are cut by 20' in the center and less towards the perimeter. This will negate the effects of currents in the area of effect.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.6: A bolt of water is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Water Bolt Table.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.7: No precipitation will occur in the area of effect for the duration of the spell.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.8: Removes all the liquid (usually water) from 1 cubic foot of inanimate material.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.9: As Evaporation I, except 10,000 cubic feet are affected.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.10: As Unwater I, except 1,000 cubic feet are affected.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.11: As Unrain, except affects a 500'/level radius for 1 day/level.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.12: As Dehydrate, except affects 10 cubic feet.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.13: As Evaporation I, except affects 100,000 cubic feet.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.14: As Unwater I, except affects 10,000 cubic feet.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.15: As Calm Water, except radius is 100'/lvl and waves are cut by 50' in the center and caster need not concentrate.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.16: A bolt of acid is shot from the palm of the caster; results determined on the Fire Bolt Table, but replacing Heat criticals with Acid criticals and also doing Impact criticals one severity level less than the primary critical.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.17: As any single spell on this list of no more than 10th level, but with a range of 300', or a 75' range increment in the case of Water Bolt.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.18: [RR Mod.: -25] This spell takes advantage of any bleeding wounds on a target to draw out and destroy additional blood. Target suffers the equivalent of ten rounds bleeding from his wounds as a result of this spell (e.g., if the target were bleeding at a rate of 3 hits per round, this spell would inflict 30 hits of damage).
FLUID DESTRUCTION.19: The target immediately begins to dehydrate and wither as if in a wind-blown sandy desert. Target is immediately at a -10 penalty to all actions and loses 1% of his total hits. For each round that the caster concentrates, the target takes another -5 penalty and 1% of total hits. If the caster maintains concentration for 10 consecutive rounds, animate targets will be reduced to dried out husks, dying. If the target gets out of range or the caster stops concentrating, there is no further damage, but the penalty and hits loss remain. The hits can heal normally, but the penalty recovers at a rate of 10 per day, assuming regular hydration. A Cure Disease spell can remove the penalty, once the hit loss is healed.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.20: For every minute that the caster concentrates, the humidity drops 1% of the original humidity (up to 50%). The humidity will gradually increase at a rate of 5% (of original humidity) per day until the original humidity is reached. Note that this change in humidity levels could affect an area’s climate (in turn affecting the area’s vegetation).
FLUID DESTRUCTION.25: As Evaporation I, except 1,000,000 cubic feet can be affected.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.30: As Calm Water True, except radius is 1000'R/level.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.35: A bolt of acid is shot from the palm of the caster; results determined on the Fire Bolt Table, but replacing Heat criticals with Acid criticals and also doing Impact criticals one severity level less than the primary critical.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.40: As Desiccation, except caster may affect up to one target/level.
FLUID DESTRUCTION.50: Every minute that the caster concentrates, the humidity drops 5% of the original humidity (up to 95%). The humidity later increases as per the Dehumidify spell. Note that this change in humidity levels could affect an area’s climate (in turn affecting the area’s vegetation).

GAS DESTRUCTION.1: Disperses all fog in a 10'/level radius and prevents new fog from forming within that radius for 10 minutes per level. If a fog-creating spell makes its RR against this spell, it can create fog within the area of effect.
GAS DESTRUCTION.2: Stops all generalized air movement up to winds of 30 mph and cuts higher winds by 30 mph in a 10' radius.
GAS DESTRUCTION.3: Creates a 5' radius of near vacuum; all within the radius take a B Impact critical as the air leaves and rushes back in (if they fail an RR).
GAS DESTRUCTION.4: Caster can remove the oxygen in a 10' radius at the rate of 2% of the original oxygen each round.
GAS DESTRUCTION.5: As Air Stop I, except affects a radius of 20'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.6: As Vacuum I, except affects a radius of 10'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.7: As Deoxygenation I, except affects a radius of 20'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.8: Changes any gas to normal, breathable air at a rate of 1 cubic foot per round as long as the caster concentrates.
GAS DESTRUCTION.9: As Air Stop I, except affects a radius of 100'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.10: As Vacuum I, except affects a radius of 20'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.11: As Vacuum I, except delivers a D Impact critical in a 5' radius.
GAS DESTRUCTION.12: As Deoxygenation I, except removal rate is 5% per round.
GAS DESTRUCTION.13: As Deoxygenation I, except affects a radius of 50'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.14: As Great Vacuum I, except affects a radius of 10'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.15: As Fast Deoxygenation I, except affects a radius of 20'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.16: As Air Stop I, except affects a radius of 10'/level.
GAS DESTRUCTION.17: As any single spell on this list of no more than 10th level, but with a range of 300'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.18: As Great Vacuum I, except affects a radius of 15'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.19: As Deoxygenation I, except affects a radius of 20' and removal rate is 10% per round.
GAS DESTRUCTION.20: [RR Mod.: -10] As Vacuum I, except delivers an E Impact critical in a 5' radius.
GAS DESTRUCTION.25: As Deoxygenation I, except affects a radius of 20' and removal rate is 20% per round.
GAS DESTRUCTION.30: [RR Mod.: -10] As Major Vacuum I, except affects a 10' radius.
GAS DESTRUCTION.35: As Vacuum I, except affects a radius of 50'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.40: [RR Mod.: -10] As Major Vacuum I, except affects a radius of 20'.
GAS DESTRUCTION.50: Destroys gases in a single enclosure (usually a building) up to a size of 100'x100'x100' (or 1,000,000 cubic feet). The building has a chance of collapsing (dependent on construction) and everyone inside takes an E Impact critical from falling debris. The implosion will make a very loud noise. If the building collapses everyone within a distance from the building equal to the building’s height takes a C Impact critical from flying debris.

MIND DESTRUCTION.1: Causes loss of 25% of target’s remaining concussion hits (i.e., those not already taken); these hits are healed when the duration is up, provided target has not died.
MIND DESTRUCTION.3: Target must subtract 25 from all Perception maneuvers and subtract 5 from initiative rolls.
MIND DESTRUCTION.4: Target must subtract 25 from all maneuvers involving movement and subtract 5 from initiative rolls.
MIND DESTRUCTION.5: Target must subtract 25 from all combat rolls and subtract 5 from initiative rolls.
MIND DESTRUCTION.7: As Minor Pain, except 50% of remaining hits are taken.
MIND DESTRUCTION.8: Target forgets a period (of up to one minute per level) of the past, as desired by the caster.
MIND DESTRUCTION.9: [RR Mod.: -10] As Major Pain, except hits must be cured or heal normally.
MIND DESTRUCTION.10: As As Disorientation, Unbalance, and Falter (all at once), except initiative penalty is 10.
MIND DESTRUCTION.11: Target mind blanks out for a period of 10 minutes each day at random. Target is incapable of activity or thought during this period.
MIND DESTRUCTION.13: Target’s mind is completely blank for the duration. The target cannot perceive events, time, or activity; when the target’s mind does come back, this produces one round of stun (-50) due to reorientation.
MIND DESTRUCTION.14: As Disorientation, except for range, duration, and that it affects a number of targets up to the caster’s level.
MIND DESTRUCTION.15: Target is a blathering idiot. The target can be led around, but can take no action.
MIND DESTRUCTION.16: As Unbalance, except affects a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
MIND DESTRUCTION.17: As any single spell on this list of no more than 10th level, but with a range of 300'.
MIND DESTRUCTION.18: As Falter, except affects a number of targets equal to the caster’s level.
MIND DESTRUCTION.19: [RR Mod: -20] Target hallucinates an attack by a creature drawn from the target’s worst fears. The target will be attacked each round by the creature (doing real damage with a +100 Martial Arts Strikes attack). Regardless of the damage done by the target (to the creature), the creature will only be defeated when the target either loses consciousness or makes an RR (one RR each 6 rounds).
MIND DESTRUCTION.20: Target loses 5% of collected experience (usually experience points).
MIND DESTRUCTION.25: As Minor Pain, except as many targets as the caster’s level are affected, the duration is until healed, and the range is 300'.
MIND DESTRUCTION.30: Target forgets completely about any one particular subject (e.g., the caster, the Fire Ruby of Romju, the Battle of Xon’s Crossing).
MIND DESTRUCTION.35: As Mind Shock, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected and the range is 300'.
MIND DESTRUCTION.40: As Major Pain, except as many targets as the caster’s level are affected, the duration is until healed, and the range is 300'.
MIND DESTRUCTION.50: As Unminding, except as many targets as the caster’s level can be affected and the range is 300'.

SOLID DESTRUCTION.1: Melts up to 10 cubic feet/level of ice.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.2: Loosens 100 cubic feet of earth to the consistency of plowed ground.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.3: Causes a 100 cubic feet/level section of inorganic material to erode and deteriorate at 1000 x normal rate.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.4: Any previous cracks or flaws in material up to 10'x10'x10' section will extend to their limit.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.5: Will vaporize a non-magical door up to 6" thick, 10' high, and 10' wide (if the door is thicker than 6" it will vaporize the closest 6 inches).
SOLID DESTRUCTION.6: Changes 100 cubic feet of stone to packed earth. This change is gradual, taking three rounds to complete.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.7: Causes one non-living wooden object to burst apart in a spray of splinters. All within a 5' radius take an A Puncture critical and holder takes a C Puncture critical.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.8: As Stone/Earth, except changes earth to soft mud.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.9: Loosens 43,560 cubic feet of earth (1 acre-foot) to the consistency of plowed ground.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.10: Creates a 3'x6' corridor that is up to 1'/level long; it can be cut through any non-metal, inorganic material. The corridor can be cut at a rate of 1' (length) per round as the caster concentrates.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.11: Causes a non-metal, inanimate object to shatter (up to 1 cubic foot in size). All within 5' radius take an A Impact critical; anyone holding the object takes a C Impact critical.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.14: As Undoor I, except any single door is vaporized.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.16: Disintegrates 1 cubic foot of any inanimate solid.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.17: As any single spell on this list of no more than 10th level, but with a range of 300'.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.18: As Corridor, except that it can cut through non-magical metal.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.19: Causes a large crack to open in the ground. The size of the crack will be up to 10' wide, up to 100' deep, and up to 200' long. The crack takes 2 rounds to open.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.20: Disintegrates 1 cubic foot per level of any inanimate solid.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.25: Causes a very minor earthquake which could cause shoddy construction to collapse (and can be very terrifying). This is approximately 5.5 on the Richter scale.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.30: Causes a large crevasse to open in the ground (up to 10' per level deep, 1' per level wide and 20' per level long). The crevasse takes 2 rounds to open. The caster can concentrate for 3 rounds to close the crevasse.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.35: As Shatter, but affects up to 1 target per level (each individual target restricted in size as per Shatter). If someone is within attack radius of more than one shattered object, multiple criticals are possible.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.40: As Metal Corridor, except that it can cut through even magical metal. Note that this is a Force spell so the magical metal will normally get an RR.
SOLID DESTRUCTION.50: Caster can cause an earthquake; with the caster’s location at the time of casting as the epicenter. The quake can be delayed up to 1 round/level. The severity of the quake on the Richter scale is determined by a roll: (01-20) = 5.5, (21-45) = 6, (46-65) = 6.5, (66-80) = 7.0, (81-90) = 7.5, (91-95) = 8.0, (96-98) = 8.5, (99-100) = 9.0.

SOUL DESTRUCTION.1: Target must answer a single concept question (presuming that the target can understand the question).
SOUL DESTRUCTION.2: Target is possessed by a Type I Demon; caster has no control over the target or Demon. The Demon will force the target to do random (not necessarily destructive) things. Target gets an RR every other round to attempt to get rid of the Demon.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.3: Target has an extreme dislike for any specific thing the caster chooses. Target has a 50% chance (modified by three times Self Discipline stat bonus) of overcoming the neurosis when given a choice (e.g., neurosis concerning horses would mean that every time the target tried to get on or near a horse the target would need to make a roll in order to do so).
SOUL DESTRUCTION.4: Target experiences chronic guilt over some action in his past. The GM should choose some significant event in the target’s past. The target will not perform the same or similar actions again and must take steps to alleviate the guilt (acting to rectify the past wrong or, if that is impossible, similar wrongs).
SOUL DESTRUCTION.5: Target will trust no one absolutely. When in a life threatening/ dangerous situation, there is a 50% chance (modified by three times Self Discipline stat bonus) that the target will not trust the protection of others and will act unilaterally for self-preservation.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.6: As Possession I, except Demon is Type II and the possessed only gets an RR once every minute.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.7: Target flees in total panic from caster. Fleeing equates to movement away at maximum pace for 1 round per 5 failure of the target’s RR.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.8: Target’s “soul” and the caster’s “soul” are interchanged; the caster can operate at half of his normal activity (double all AP costs as with concentration) while in the body of the target. The target (in the caster’s body) is inactive. The caster can cancel the spell at any time (takes one round). The target can cancel the spell if he makes a successful RR (he gets one every 10 minutes). If either body is killed, both “souls” are destroyed.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.9: This spell torments a spirit, typically a conjured being like an elemental or demon. These spirits may be targeted even if in an incorporeal form or if possessing another’s body. The GM may wish to include some undead among potential targets. The pain caused by this spell reduces the target to 2 AP per round and the target takes 1 hit per 1 failure on the RR as well. These hits do not return at the end of the spell duration; that aspect of the spell is “permanent”.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.10: As Possession I, except Demon is Type III and the possessed target only gets an RR once every 10 minutes.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.11: Part of the target’s “soul” is taken and placed in an organic object on the caster’s person. The body of the target will act as the caster directs (caster must concentrate).The spell ends when: the caster cancels it or the object is destroyed or the body is more than 100' from caster or the object leaves the caster’s person. If the caster is not concentrating the target may act freely, though at -30 to all activities. While being commanded, the target is aware of all the actions performed, but is helpless to stop them.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.12: Part of the target’s soul is transferred to a random object somewhere within 100 miles; the target is at -30 to all activities until the spell is dispelled or the target touches the object (which returns the missing piece of soul). The target will always know the direction of the lost “soul”.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.13: As Possession I, except Demon is Type IV and the possessed target only gets an RR once every hour.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.14: As Word of Panic, except affects everyone within 20’ except the caster.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.15: [RR Mod.: -10] Target must make an RR against Fear (use the highest level foe or GM’s judgment for other perils as level of Fear) at -25 in any personally dangerous situation.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.16: [RR Mod.: +10] As Spirit Burn, except if target fails RR it must retreat to its own plane of existence, if applicable, or it will be transported instantly to its “home” location on this plane and is reduced to zero hits.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.17: As any single spell on this list of no more than 10th level, but with a range of 300'.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.18: As Possession I, except Demon is Type V and the possessed target only gets an RR once every day.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.19: Target is put into a state of deep sleep and will neither awaken nor age. The target will only die if killed (does not need food, water, etc.). This sleep will continue until dispelled or until a single, non-magical event (specified by the caster at the time of casting) is accomplished. Note that the caster must specify the non-magical condition (i.e., it is not optional).
SOUL DESTRUCTION.20: As Subjugation, except the “soul” is only released if the caster cancels the spell or the object is destroyed. The target is always aware of the direction of the object holding the stolen “soul”.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.25: As Transferal, except target only gets his additional RRs once per month and every time he fails his chance to successfully resist decreases by 1 and the caster may operate normally in the target’s body.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.30: [RR Mod: -20] Target’s “soul” is torn from the target’s body (or other physical location if the soul is otherwise housed); it remains in whatever place “souls” go for 30 days per 10 failure. The soul can be returned early only through Lifegiving or Reuniting. Target is unconscious until soul is restored; even subconscious activity (i.e., healing, etc.) suffers a -75 penalty.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.35: As Possession I, except Demon is Type VI and the possessed target only gets an RR once every week.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.40: [RR Mod: -20] As Long Absolution, except “soul” can only be brought back through Lifegiving.
SOUL DESTRUCTION.50: [RR Mod: -20] As Absolution Pure, except “soul” is utterly destroyed.

STARSENSE.1: Caster is aware of the presence of all sentient/thinking beings within range.
STARSENSE.2: Gives the direction and distance to any specific object or place that the caster is familiar with or has had described in detail, if it is within range. The caster must have the dimensions of the object exact within 10% of actual size and know at least two other attributes that make the item unique (e.g., color, texture, weight, etc.) within range of the spell. Note that sometimes the caster must know more than two other attributes to make the item unique.
STARSENSE.3: The caster can see on a clear night (when the stars or moonlight is visible) as if it were day, with no visibility penalties. The range of the caster's vision is that of normal daylight vision. The caster must be outdoors for this spell to function.
STARSENSE.4: As Location I, except range is 300'.
STARSENSE.5: Caster stores a mental pattern of target for later use with other spells. The target must first be located by Presence, Presence True, or Awareness.
STARSENSE.6: Caster gets direction and distance to any unshielded mind for which caster has a Mind Stored reference pattern.
STARSENSE.7: As Location I, except range is 500'.
STARSENSE.8: Caster learns race, profession, sex, age, and level of the target. The target must have been located by Presence, Presence True, or Awareness.
STARSENSE.9: Caster learns the direction to any unshielded mind for which caster has a Mind Stored reference pattern.
STARSENSE.10: Outdoors on a clear night (under starlight or moonlight), the caster attunes himself to the "music of the spheres" and can hear the faintest of sounds by merely focusing on a given locale (which must also be exposed to starlight or moonlight, i.e., not inside a building). The caster's range of hearing is up to the horizon.
STARSENSE.11: The caster can transfer a copy of any one Mind Stored person to another caster from the Mentalism realm (i.e., both casters now have the person stored). The target of this spell must also know the Mind Store spell.
STARSENSE.12: As Presence, plus a general knowledge of the actions of each being (e.g., being is casting a spell, but not what spell is being cast).
STARSENSE.13: As Stareyes, except caster can see even in a pitch dark night (no stars visible and no moonlight) as if it were day. The darkness must be naturally occurring (not from any magical effects).
STARSENSE.14: As Location I, except the range is 1 mile.
STARSENSE.15: As Mind Finding I, except the range is unlimited if both the caster and the target are outdoors when the stars are visible.
STARSENSE.16: As Mind Finding I, except the range is 1 mile per level.
STARSENSE.17: As Stareyes, except the caster can see in magically created darkness as if it were day.
STARSENSE.18: As Direction, except the range is 5 miles per level.
STARSENSE.19: As Starhearing, except the caster is also able to attune himself to the "music of the spheres" on dark nights when there is neither starlight nor moonlight.
STARSENSE.20: As Location I, except the range is 20 miles.
STARSENSE.25: As Direction, except the range is unlimited.
STARSENSE.30: As Mind Finding I, except range is 5 miles per level.
STARSENSE.35: As Location I, except the range is unlimited if both the caster and the target are outdoors while the stars are visible. If either the caster or the target (or both) are not outdoors, the range is 1 mile per level.
STARSENSE.40: As Mind Finding I, except range is unlimited.
STARSENSE.50: As Starlocation, except if the caster can see the stars and the target is out of range (which can only happen if the target is not outdoors under the stars), the caster may ask the stars to watch for the target. After the target has next been visible to the stars, the caster will learn the last location where the stars saw the target. The caster will not obtain this information until they next see the stars (which could occur instantly if the caster and target are both under the stars at the same time).

VISION BORROWING.1: Caster may borrow the visual sense of any non-intelligent animal within range, thus sharing the visual perceptions of the animal. The animal must be within sight or located with a Presence spell or with Mind Store followed by Mind Finding (for the initial contact only).
VISION BORROWING.2: As Animal Sight I, except the auditory sense is borrowed.
VISION BORROWING.3: As Animal Sight I, except any and all senses may be borrowed. Only senses possessed by the caster will be comprehensible without the use of Comprehend Sense.
VISION BORROWING.4: As Animal Sight I, except any being's visual sense may be borrowed.
VISION BORROWING.5: As Animal Hearing I, except any being's auditory sense may be borrowed.
VISION BORROWING.6: As Animal Sight I, except the range is 300'.
VISION BORROWING.7: The caster may view a person, item, or location, seeing what is happening at that very moment at the scried site. The caster must be able to name or describe the person or location uniquely. The caster must concentrate upon a medium, and the target will appear in that medium. If the medium is mobile (e.g., crystal ball, mirror), the range to the target is limited to 100' per level. If it is immobile (e.g., a pool), the range is limited to 1000' per level. The caster may only use their normal vision, no other senses are provided and magical enhancements (e.g., Nightsight) will not operate. Only the caster will see the images (unless Scrying Share is also cast); others will see nothing.
VISION BORROWING.8: As Animal Sense I, except the range is 300'.
VISION BORROWING.9: If cast before a "sense borrowing" spell, this enables the caster to understand the perceptive data received from a sense he himself does not possess. For example, a human caster would need this spell to understand the information from sharing a bat's sonar sense.
VISION BORROWING.10: As Sight Merge I, except the range is 300'.
VISION BORROWING.11: As Animal Sight I, except the range is 500'.
VISION BORROWING.12: As Animal Sense I, except any and all senses may be borrowed from any being.
VISION BORROWING.13: As Animal Sense I, except the range is 500'.
VISION BORROWING.14: As Scrying I, except the range limitation is 1 mile per level for a mobile medium and 10 miles per level for an immobile medium.
VISION BORROWING.15: As Sight Merge I, except the range is 500'.
VISION BORROWING.16: As Animal Sight I, except the range is 1 mile per level.
VISION BORROWING.17: By casting this on targets (up to 1 target per level) prior to casting a Scrying spell, the targets will be able to see what the scryer sees while the Scrying spell is active and the targets remain concentrating. The same limitations listed for the caster in Scrying I also apply to all who share the scrying. Note that the size of the medium may limit the number of targets that can view the medium at once.
VISION BORROWING.18: As Sensory Merge I, except the range is 300'.
VISION BORROWING.19: As Animal Sense I, except the range is 1 mile per level.
VISION BORROWING.20: As Sight Merge I, except the range is 1 mile per level.
VISION BORROWING.25: As Sensory Merge I, except the range is 1 mile per level.
VISION BORROWING.30: As Scrying I, except the range limitation is 10 miles per level for a mobile medium and 100 miles per level for an immobile medium.
VISION BORROWING.35: As Animal Sense I, except the range is unlimited.
VISION BORROWING.40: As Sight Merge I, except the range is unlimited.
VISION BORROWING.50: As Sensory Merge I, except the range is unlimited.

FUTURE VISIONS.1: Caster gains a vision of what will probably happen in the next minute if the caster takes a specified action.
FUTURE VISIONS.2: Caster can detect whether an unfulfilled fate, destiny, or wyrd lies upon a person, object, or place.
FUTURE VISIONS.3: As Intuitions I, except the caster gets to gaze 3 minutes into the future.
FUTURE VISIONS.4: The caster can attempt to avoid one attack, which can be a missile, melee attack, or spell. The missile, weapon, or enemy spellcaster must be within range and within the caster's field of vision when this spell is cast. The caster receives a +50 DB bonus against missile, melee, or directed spell attacks; their normal DB against area elemental attacks, or +10 to their RR against other types of spells.
FUTURE VISIONS.5: As Intuitions I, except the caster gets to gaze 5 minutes into the future.
FUTURE VISIONS.6: Caster has a dream relating to a topic decided upon just before retiring; limited to once per night. The caster must sleep for a normal sleep cycle (minimum of four hours) for this spell to work.
FUTURE VISIONS.7: Predicts most probable action of a being in the next round; specifics are not learned (e.g., attack in melee, cast a spell; but no detail on attack target or what spell).
FUTURE VISIONS.8: The caster is able (using a culturally specific method) to make a prediction concerning a person, place, or object. Making the prediction will take at least one minute per level of the spell. Only one prediction may be made in any 24-hour period by the caster (and a failed spell counts towards this limit). The prediction will be accurate 25% of the time plus 1% per level of the caster; otherwise, the results are random. The prediction may concern events up to 1 day per level of the caster into the future. The predictions will be general, ambiguous, and enigmatic. The interpretation of the predictions is left entirely to the caster.
FUTURE VISIONS.9: As Anticipations I, except if action is to cast a spell, the spell to be cast and target(s) are learned.
FUTURE VISIONS.10: As Intuitions I, except the caster gets to gaze 10 minutes into the future.
FUTURE VISIONS.11: As Dream I, except limit is 2 dreams/night on different topics.
FUTURE VISIONS.12: As Divinations I, except predicting events up to 1 month per level of the caster into the future.
FUTURE VISIONS.13: As Anticipations I, except the caster can predict the most probable actions of three beings in the next round or the most probable actions of one being over the next three rounds.
FUTURE VISIONS.14: The caster may analyze an unfulfilled destiny in terms of who made the prophecy and/or the source of the destiny, the strength of the destiny, and where appropriate the oracular riddle (or other pronouncement) which encapsulates the destiny. The spell does not indicate how a destiny may be fulfilled. Note that this spell will reveal if a given prophecy or divination is a hoax—the strength of the destiny will in such cases depend on the degree to which the victim of the hoax believes in the divination.
FUTURE VISIONS.15: As Intuitions I, except the caster gets to gaze 1 minute per level into the future.
FUTURE VISIONS.16: As Dream I, except limit is 3 dreams/night on different topics.
FUTURE VISIONS.17: As Divinations I, except predicting events up to 1 year per level of the caster into the future.
FUTURE VISIONS.18: As Anticipations III, except if any action is to cast a spell, the spell to be cast and target(s) are learned.
FUTURE VISIONS.19: As Anticipations I, except the caster can predict the most probable actions of five beings in the next round or the most probable actions of one being over the next five rounds.
FUTURE VISIONS.20: As Dream I, except limit is 5 dreams/night on different topics.
FUTURE VISIONS.25: As Anticipations I, except the caster can predict the most probable actions of every being within 100'.
FUTURE VISIONS.30: As Anticipations True, except if any action is to cast a spell, the spell to be cast and target(s) are learned.
FUTURE VISIONS.35: As Lord Dream, except the caster is not required to specify the topic of each dream until having received the prior dreams. Thus, they may choose to question specific details of each dream as the topic of the next. Caster remains sleeping until all five dreams are completed.
FUTURE VISIONS.40: As Spell Anticipations True, and the caster gains the benefit of Foresighted Defense against any anticipated attack or spell.
FUTURE VISIONS.50: As Divinations I, except predicting events up to 10 years per level of the caster into the future.

HOLY VISION.1: On a clear night, when stars and/or the moon(s) are visible, the caster gains perfect directional and distance sense. For the duration, he will always know where he is in relation to known landmarks.
HOLY VISION.2: Caster is able to read and write very simple phrases and words in a specific language, and possibly understand the context of very simple passages. The caster must have a sample text in the target language. For the duration of the spell, the caster has the equivalent of 2 ranks in the written form of the language.
HOLY VISION.3: Caster has a dream relating to a topic decided upon just before retiring; limited to once per night. The caster must sleep for a normal sleep cycle (minimum of four hours) for this spell to work.
HOLY VISION.4: Caster receives a vision of events that occurred up to 1 minute per level into the past. The caster must select the point in the past to be viewed (and the vision will be accurate within one minute). The vision must be associated with a person, place, or object touched at the time of casting. The vision includes sight and sound, and will last up to 1 round per level if the caster concentrates and remains inactive. Time passes at a rate of one round of real time per 10 rounds of vision.
HOLY VISION.5: As Literacy I, except the caster can read moderately simple writings and understand most of the details, but will have trouble with subtle concepts. For the duration of the spell, the caster has the equivalent of 4 ranks in the written form of the language.
HOLY VISION.6: As Dream I, except limit is 2 dreams/night on different topics.
HOLY VISION.7: This spell gives the caster the ability to scan the past by "feeling the temporal location for significant events." This translates to the caster knowing the approximate time-frames of significant events, without knowing the nature of those events. If the caster casts a Vision Behind spell within one minute of casting this spell, he will be able to see the specific events.
HOLY VISION.8: As Literacy I, except the caster has the reading level of an educated member of the nobility, and may write at an eleventh grade level. For the duration of the spell, the caster has the equivalent of 6 ranks in the written form of the language.
HOLY VISION.9: As Dream I, except limit is 3 dreams/night on different topics.
HOLY VISION.10: Caster receives a "yes" or "no" to a question on a single topic; usable but once a day. This answer normally comes from the caster's deity or some supernatural subordinate of that deity.
HOLY VISION.11: As Vision Behind I, except up to 10 minutes per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±5 minutes), and the vision can last up to one minute per level.
HOLY VISION.12: As Literacy I, except caster may read relatively complex material and recognize (if not fully understand) the nature of archaic or unusual dialects and concepts. For the duration of the spell, the caster has the equivalent of 8 ranks in the written form of the language.
HOLY VISION.13: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 hour per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±30 minutes), and the vision can last up to five minutes per level.
HOLY VISION.14: As Dream I, except limit is 4 dreams/night on different topics.
HOLY VISION.15: As Commune I, except caster may ask three questions.
HOLY VISION.16: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 day per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 hour), and the vision can last up to ten minutes per level.
HOLY VISION.17: As Dream I, except the target must sleep and will experience the dream rather than the caster. If the target is already sleeping when this spell is cast, any RR is at -20.
HOLY VISION.18: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 month per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 day), and the vision can last up to 1 hour per level.
HOLY VISION.19: The caster can enter the sleeping dreams (or nightmares) of one target chosen at the time of casting; this requires the caster to sleep (as in Dream I) and also the target must be asleep and must dream while the caster is sleeping (most targets will dream while sleeping unless actively prevented). The target must have been previously Mind Stored (see the Starsense spell list). Upon entry to a target's dreams, the caster may choose whether to merely passively observe or to interact with the dream and/or dreamer. If the target is experiencing a shared dream, the caster may also interact with others in the same dream.
HOLY VISION.20: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 year per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 week), and the vision can last up to 5 hours per level.
HOLY VISION.25: As Commune I, except caster can receive a more detailed answer (e.g., a name or short phrase) to a question involving only one concept.
HOLY VISION.30: As Dream I, except caster is able to manipulate his dream in a limited way to gain more information on a specific topic. For example, while he is in the dream he can ask a question (but there is no guarantee it will be answered).
HOLY VISION.35: By casting this spell just before retiring, the caster is alert to efforts by others to detect, store, observe, or manipulate his dreams. Any such spell or other attempt must make a RR versus this spell. If the RR succeeds, the spell proceeds normally; if it fails, the caster is aware of the attempt and may choose at any point to cancel it (including immediately).
HOLY VISION.40: As Enter Dream, except the range is 1 mile per level.
HOLY VISION.50: Caster receives detailed information on a single topic question. This information comes directly from the caster's deity.

FAR VOICE.1: Caster may mentally speak with another spell user of the Mentalism realm within range. They must be able to see each other or the caster must know the exact location of the target or the caster must use Focus Voice to locate the target.
FAR VOICE.2: The caster enters a trance-like state to prepare his mind to be the recipient of a Star Voice, Mind Voice, or Mind Tongue spell. While under the effects of this spell, an incoming spell of these three types will have its range increased by a factor of 10.
FAR VOICE.3: As Star Voice, except the target may be any one thinking being. The location must be known as for Star Voice.
FAR VOICE.4: The next Star Voice or Mind Voice spell (cast within one minute of this spell) will be able to focus in on a specific person as its target even if the caster cannot see the target. The target must have been previously Mind Stored (see the Starsense spell list).
FAR VOICE.5: As Star Voice, except the range is to the horizon if it is clear and at night, or otherwise 1000'.
FAR VOICE.6: As Mind Voice I, except the range is 300'.
FAR VOICE.7: As Prepare Voice I, except the range is increased by a factor of 20.
FAR VOICE.8: As Mind Voice I, except the range is 500'.
FAR VOICE.9: Caster can cause his voice to be heard at a point up to 100' away (in amplified tones). If the location is out of sight, the caster must have previously been there.
FAR VOICE.10: As Mind Voice I, except the range is 1000'.
FAR VOICE.11: As Prepare Voice I, except the range is increased by a factor of 50.
FAR VOICE.12: A mental message of up to 25 words can be stored and set to be delivered to a person entering the area of effect. The message is triggered at a specified time (within 24 hours), specified movements, specified sounds, touch, or a specified person entering the area (that person must have been Mind Stored by the caster; see the Starsense spell list). Triggering events must occur within the spell's area of effect.
FAR VOICE.13: As Long Voice I, except the point can be up to 300' away.
FAR VOICE.14: As Mind Voice I, except the range is 1 mile.
FAR VOICE.15: As Star Voice, except the range is 5 miles per level if the spell is cast on a clear night, or 1 mile per level under other conditions.
FAR VOICE.16: As Prepare Voice I, except the range is increased by a factor of 100.
FAR VOICE.17: As Long Voice I, except the point can be up to 500' away.
FAR VOICE.18: As Mind Voice I, except the range is 5 miles.
FAR VOICE.19: As Prepare Voice I, except the range is increased by a factor of 500.
FAR VOICE.20: As Long Voice I, except the point can be up to 100' per level away.
FAR VOICE.25: As Mind Voice I, except the range is 1 mile per level.
FAR VOICE.30: As Long Voice I, except the point can be up to 1 mile per level away.
FAR VOICE.35: As Long Voice I, except the range is 1000' per level and the caster may specify as many points as desired within range (e.g., the caster could specify that everyone within range will hear his voice).
FAR VOICE.40: As Mind Voice I, except if the target is another spell user of the Mentalism realm, the range is unlimited; otherwise, the range is 5 miles per level of the caster.
FAR VOICE.50: As Proclamation, except the range is 1 mile per level and the voice will be heard by everyone within range who meet any criteria specified by the caster (e.g., the caster could speak to "every soldier of my kingdom who remains loyal" or to "the person who has stolen my hat" or simply to "everyone").

STARLORE.1: The caster studies and memorizes the relation of the target to the influences. This provides no immediate information but permits the use of the other spells on this list to provide information regarding the target even when the target is not in range; this applies to any spell on this list which specifies a "target" or "person" with the exception of Determine Origin. Caster may have as many targets memorized in this way as their Memory stat (not stat bonus).
STARLORE.2: Caster learns which influence is the predominant aspect of the target's personality (e.g., a knowledge-focused scholar might be under the influence of the constellation of the owl).
STARLORE.3: Caster learns which influence has been the most significant source of hardship, failure, or difficulty for the target in the past (e.g., a person betrayed by their spouse might be suffering under the planet Venus).
STARLORE.4: Caster learns which influence has been the most significant source of aid, benefit, or help for the target in the past.
STARLORE.5: Caster learns which influence is most relevant to an item's purpose (e.g., a weapon might be associated with the deity or planet associated with war). If the purpose has changed, this might become apparent (e.g., a sword beaten into a plowshare might be represented as Mars turning towards Jupiter).
STARLORE.6: Given a query concerning a decision, action, event, etc., the caster can potentially assess which influence(s) will be the most important factors in determining the outcome, whether they will be positive or negative factors, and which influence(s) will be enhanced or reduced by the likely outcome. The prediction will relate to events up to 10 minutes per level into the future. However, the number of influences learned is limited to one per 30 the spell succeeded by (rounding up), e.g., if the casting roll is 1-30, the spell will only report one influence as an important factor or outcome, if it is 31-60 it will report two, if 61-90 it will report three (if that many are relevant), etc. Only one Horary spell may be cast by the caster within any given 24-hour period, and failed spells count towards that limit.
STARLORE.7: Caster learns the place (within 1 mile) and time (within one minute) of the target's birth. Any spell that conceals or hides information will distort the result (e.g., Misfeel Kind will either result in no answer or give a location consistent with the false race).
STARLORE.8: Caster learns which influence is currently the greatest obstacle or hardship for the target (e.g., a person in trouble with the law might be shadowed by Saturn, the planet considered the lawgiver).
STARLORE.9: Caster learns which influence is currently the most beneficial for the target. This does not necessarily indicate the target's actions or intent (although it could), only that they are benefitting from the influence.
STARLORE.10: As Horary I, except the time frame which can be assessed is 1 hour per level into the future.
STARLORE.11: Caster learns which influence will next have a major impact on a given place (e.g., if there will soon be an autumn festival, the harvest moon may be rising over it).
STARLORE.12: Given a decision, action, event, etc., the caster can determine which influence will be most auspicious for the target to act in accordance with, and which will be most inauspicious, in the near future. In addition to the value of this information, the next three actions (including maneuvers, attacks, and spells cast) taken by the target relevant to the topic and in line with the auspicious influence will gain a +10 bonus, while those aligned with the inauspicious influence will be at -10. For example, if the auspicious influence is the god of diplomacy and the inauspicious influence is the god of war, three attempts to negotiate or improve the circumstances for negotiation will be at +10, but attempts to attack or threaten will be at -10. The caster may have only one Auspex spell in effect at once, and it may not be on the same topic as any Horary spell cast within the same day. This spell may not be cancelled or dispelled; it merely determines fate, it does not change it. However, any unused modifiers after 24 hours will expire.
STARLORE.13: As Horary I, except the time frame which can be assessed is 1 day per level into the future.
STARLORE.14: As Auspex I, except it affects one target per level of the caster (and three actions per target). All targets must be working together for a shared purpose (at least nominally) related to the topic of the Auspex.
STARLORE.15: As Auspex I, except the modifiers are +20 or -20.
STARLORE.16: As Horary I, except the time frame which can be assessed is 1 week per level into the future.
STARLORE.17: Caster gains insight into the relationship of the target to a specified influence. For example, by choosing the planet Mars as the influence, the caster might learn the target decided to become a soldier because their family was killed by an enemy army, that they served for many years, and that they then retired and have tried since then to keep their distance from conflict. The caster would not learn the target took up pottery, married, and loves dogs, as these facts would be irrelevant to the influence specified.
STARLORE.18: As Greater Auspex I, except the modifiers are +20 or -20.
STARLORE.19: As Horary I, except the time frame which can be assessed is 1 month per level into the future.
STARLORE.20: As Auspex I, except the modifiers are +30 or -30.
STARLORE.25: Caster studies the relationship of a particular influence to the target and obtains a piece of advice regarding how best to overcome an obstacle related to that influence or to achieve a goal related to that influence. This advice should be most likely correct (bad luck and bad choices may still manage to negate any advantage) but the reasons may be unclear. For example, the advice might be to act at a precise moment (which happens to be when the king will be in the right place and the right mood) or to carry a particular weapon or item (which happens to be the only thing the foe is vulnerable to, or the gift that will elicit the desired outcome). In addition, the target gains a bonus of +30 on the next three actions related to acting upon the advice, or -30 on the next three actions that demonstrate an intention to disregard the advice. Only one such course may be plotted regarding a particular obstacle or goal, until the necessary action has been taken or irretrievably rejected. The modifiers are not cumulative with those from any Auspex.
STARLORE.30: As Horary I, except the time frame which can be assessed is 1 year per level into the future.
STARLORE.35: As Greater Auspex I, except the modifiers are +30 or -30.
STARLORE.40: As Plot Course, except it affects one target per level of the caster (and three actions per target). All targets must be working together for a shared purpose (at least nominally). The advice may be directed at the group (e.g., reinforce the line at this location) or at a key individual or subgroup within the group (e.g., send a scout or negotiator to a particular place).
STARLORE.50: As Horary True and Greater Auspex III regarding one overall endeavor, except one influence will be determined per 20 success (rather than 30 as usual), plus Plot Group Course regarding one predicted negative influence.

FAR VISIONS.1: Caster can see 10' per level in any water (including murky water) as if through air in daylight. Some residual light must exist for this spell to work.
FAR VISIONS.2: As Watersight, except caster can see in normal darkness such as a clear night outdoors, so long as there is some light.
FAR VISIONS.3: As Watersight, except caster can see in fog, mist, any other precipitation, or any gas.
FAR VISIONS.4: Caster can see through wood (up to a maximum thickness of 1"/level).
FAR VISIONS.5: Caster's point of hearing may be moved independently up to 10' per level away (moves at 10'/md); the caster must be physically able to go there (e.g., the caster could not send this point of hearing through walls or closed doors). Note that this means that the caster does not have hearing at his own location.
FAR VISIONS.6: Caster can pick a point (up to 10' away), and be able to see and/or hear from that point. The point is fixed but can be rotated. There can be intervening barriers such as walls between the caster and the point.
FAR VISIONS.7: As Long Ear, except caster sees from the moving point (it can rotate).
FAR VISIONS.8: Caster can see all invisible beings or objects as if they were not invisible. Note that the invisible object is not "detected;" it simply isn't invisible to the caster.
FAR VISIONS.9: As Woodsight, except caster can see through any non-magical stone.
FAR VISIONS.10: As Woodsight, except caster can see through any non-magical iron or steel.
FAR VISIONS.11: Caster can see "through" all visual illusions, phantasms, mirages, facades, and glamours.
FAR VISIONS.12: As Observe I, except the range can be up to 10' per level.
FAR VISIONS.13: As Long Ear, except up to 100' per level away, the sense can be moved up to 100' per round, and the caster may move any and all senses.
FAR VISIONS.14: As Woodsight, except the caster can see through any non-magical metal.
FAR VISIONS.15: As Nightsight, except caster can see through magically created darkness (such as that resulting from Dark or Utterdark spells) or total ordinary darkness (i.e., no residual light required).
FAR VISIONS.16: As Observe I, except two points up to 100' away may be observed simultaneously.
FAR VISIONS.17: As Observe I, except up to 100' per level away.
FAR VISIONS.18: As Woodsight, except the caster can see through any non-magical wall of any thickness.
FAR VISIONS.19: As Observe III, except caster does not have to concentrate until the spell is triggered by some movement or some sound which could be perceived from the observation point; concentration is required after the spell is so triggered or the spell will end. If the caster is ever more than 100' per level from the selected point, the spell will end.
FAR VISIONS.20: As Long Sense, except the range is 1 mile per level, and the sense can be moved up to 1000' per round.
FAR VISIONS.25: As Observe III, except the duration is 1 minute per level and concentration is not required (the caster need only glance and listen once every three rounds).
FAR VISIONS.30: As Woodsight, except the caster can see through all inanimate material. Highly magical materials might receive a RR (at the GM's discretion).
FAR VISIONS.35: As Long Eye, except the caster also benefits from one of the Sight spells (e.g., Woodsight) other than Sight True at the remote point.
FAR VISIONS.40: As Long Sense, except the caster may move his senses with no limitations on range, and the sense can be moved up to 1 mile per round.
FAR VISIONS.50: As Long Sense True, plus the caster benefits from Sight True at the remote point.

VISION GUARD.1: Detects if a being, item, or place in the area of effect is currently being scried upon. The caster may concentrate on a different 5' radius each round.
VISION GUARD.2: As Detect Scrying, except detects if an attempt is being made to divine the future of a being, item, or place in the area of effect.
VISION GUARD.3: Any scrying directed toward the subject is clouded. The scryer will perceive their vision as if through a fog, gaining only 50% of the knowledge that would otherwise be obtained.
