This protection lasts until the duration runs out, the spell is cancelled or dispelled, or the defense is pierced by a scryer (whichever happens first).
VISION GUARD.4: Caster conceals one curse or destiny which lies upon the subject, rendering the curse or destiny undetectable by Detect Curse or Detect Destiny. The curse or destiny is still fully active, merely hidden from detection.
VISION GUARD.5: By using a decoy subject very similar to the subject, within 10' per level of the caster at the time of casting this spell, the caster ensures that Scrying attempts targeting the subject will instead observe the decoy. Anyone scrying the subject may make a Perception maneuver to detect the deception (modified by the quality of the decoy). If no decoy is available, this spell will fail.
VISION GUARD.6: All deeds performed by the target while this spell is active are "shadowed" to divination spells. All related visions gained through divination effect are shrouded in shadows. For example, a Death's Memory cast on the scene of a murder might reveal a shadowy figure performing the deeds (but no details about the identity of the figure).
VISION GUARD.7: For the duration, if the target resists any information-gathering or mind-reading spells, he may portray falsehoods as truths. If the caster of such spells is aware by other means that the target must be deceiving him, or if False Truth ends while the mind-reading spell is still in effect, the deception will become apparent.
VISION GUARD.8: The target may mislead the caster of any Anticipate or Anticipations spell. Incorrect information is received, and no benefit will be obtained (e.g., Anticipate Missile will not provide any defensive benefit).
VISION GUARD.9: The caster may set a false vision upon the chosen subject for "would-be" scryers to discover. The false vision must be fairly simple and may not portray scenes or events longer than the duration of this spell. This spell can be defeated by piercing (see note) or repeated scrying (i.e., outlasting this spell), or noting that something unlikely is occurring, or that events in the scrying repeat exactly.
VISION GUARD.10: As Cloud Scrying, except caster can cloud any form of divinatory magic upon the subject (including spells from the Astrologer's Starlore base list).
VISION GUARD.11: Once this spell is learned, the caster is automatically aware of any scrying attempt directed at them.
VISION GUARD.12: Once this spell is learned, the caster is automatically aware of any divination attempt directed at them.
VISION GUARD.13: The subject of this spell will be detected or not detected by any combination of Detect spells as specified by the caster at the time of casting. For example, the caster might decide that an item will be detected as gold, a trap, and evil (e.g., by the Detect Substance, Detect Traps, and Detect Evil spells).
VISION GUARD.14: As Shadow Past, except absolutely no information about the target will be revealed. For example, a Death's Memory cast on the scene of a murder might show the victim collapsing with a knife in his chest (but no sign of the assassin).
VISION GUARD.15: Any attempt to divine information about the protected subject will receive a false reading, with the elements of the reading specified by the caster at the time of casting.
VISION GUARD.16: Target becomes undetectable by Presence spells or related abilities.
VISION GUARD.17: Caster learns the location and identity of a scryer whose activities have been detected by Detect Scrying or Feel Scrying.
VISION GUARD.18: As Scrying Analysis, except detects a diviner detected by Detect Divination or Feel Divination.
VISION GUARD.19: Caster may attach a false history to an item, which may include its place of origins, the race of its creator(s), its purpose, and one significant event. Any spells obtaining such information will obtain the false information.
VISION GUARD.20: As Shadow Past, except all deeds performed by the target while this spell is active will appear as if someone else is performing them. The false actor is chosen by the caster at the time of casting and the effectiveness of the falsification will depend on how well the caster can visualize the intended "fall guy." Merely observing someone is not as good as any of the following spells: Study Patsy, Impersonation Study, or Change Lore. In the absence of those spells, Illusion Crafting skill (modified by the caster's familiarity with the target) will determine the quality.
VISION GUARD.25: Target's memories are hidden from Inner Thoughts, Mind Scan, Mind Probe, etc. The caster may hide memories at a rate of one scene per round (with a maximum number of rounds equal to the caster's level). The hidden memories are still available to the target.
VISION GUARD.30: As Conceal Memories, except the caster may replace real memories with false memories at a rate of one memory per round. The target has access to both the true and the false memories.
VISION GUARD.35: As False Item History, except the caster may also specify whether or not the item has any magical powers, what those powers are, and the source of that power. No actual powers are granted or removed, but attempts to attune the item to powers that do not match the false power are at -20. Successful attunement will reveal real powers (if any are present).
VISION GUARD.40: Caster invents a history and biography for the target in as much detail as desired, including name, race, profession, age, place of origin, religion, magical realm, and significant events in their past. Spells revealing any such information will reveal only the false information. The target is aware of both the real and false information.
VISION GUARD.50: The subject of this spell is protected from all divinatory magic for the duration of this spell, which is immune to being pierced. Any divinatory magic directed to the subject will simply fail, and divinatory magic attempted on any other subject will fail to take the protected subject into account. The protected subject may not use any divinatory magic upon themself or on any other subject; they are truly outside the weave of fate.

WAY OF THE VOICE.1: Caster is able to communicate basic ideas in a specific language (e.g., hungry, thirsty, bathroom, peace, etc.); equivalent to skill rank 2.
WAY OF THE VOICE.2: Target is calmed and cannot take any aggressive (offensive) action, while the caster speaks to the target (requiring concentration). After the caster ceases to speak to the target, the effect will continue as many rounds as the caster has already spoken. For example, if the caster speaks to a target for 3 rounds, the target will be calmed for those 3 rounds plus the following 3 rounds. Target must be able to hear and understand the caster. The caster may concentrate on this spell and a Speech or Common Speech spell at the same time with a single concentration action.
WAY OF THE VOICE.3: Target must answer a single concept question (presuming that the target can understand the question).
WAY OF THE VOICE.4: As Voice of Calming, except the target will become afraid of one person (such as the caster), object, or place chosen by the caster at the time of casting, and will flee in fear from the source of that fear at maximum pace for the duration of the spell. Note that unless the target is restrained (even in a minor way), they will attempt to run after one round.
WAY OF THE VOICE.5: As Tongues I, except caster can communicate more complex concepts, although there is a good chance of misinterpretations; equivalent to skill rank 4.
WAY OF THE VOICE.6: Caster receives a special +10 bonus to all non-magical attempts to persuade and/or influence people.
WAY OF THE VOICE.7: As Voice of Calming, except target has its Action Points per round reduced by 3 (i.e., normally, the target will have 1 AP each round).
WAY OF THE VOICE.8: As Voice of Calming, except target will obey any actions suggested by the caster. However, he will not perform any act that is completely alien to him or is self-destructive.
WAY OF THE VOICE.9: As Tongues I, except caster is reasonably fluent in the language. Caster's accent is imperfect, but there is only a slight chance of misinterpretation; equivalent to skill rank 6.
WAY OF THE VOICE.10: As Voice of Calming, except target will believe that the reasoning and ideas put forward by the caster are correct and valid, and will be unable to doubt these beliefs for the duration of the spell. After the spell has ended, the target will continue to believe these ideas until either persuaded otherwise or presented with irrefutable evidence to the contrary.
WAY OF THE VOICE.11: As Voice of Calming, except affects all within range who can hear and understand the caster.
WAY OF THE VOICE.12: As Orate I, except the bonus is +20.
WAY OF THE VOICE.13: While the caster concentrates, target becomes reasonably fluent in a specific language. Target's accent is imperfect, but there is only a slight chance of misinterpretation; equivalent to skill rank 6.
WAY OF THE VOICE.14: As Voice of Fear, except affects all within range who can hear and understand the caster.
WAY OF THE VOICE.15: As Voice of Holding, except affects all within range who can hear and understand the caster.
WAY OF THE VOICE.16: As Voice of Command, except affects all within range who can hear and understand the caster.
WAY OF THE VOICE.17: As Tongues I, except caster speaks the specified language like a native (equivalent to skill rank 8) and the duration is 10 minutes/level.
WAY OF THE VOICE.18: As Speech III, except target speaks the specified language like a native and the caster does not need to concentrate (duration is 1 min/level). Skill is equivalent to skill rank 8.
WAY OF THE VOICE.19: As Voice of Beguilement, except affects all within range who can hear and understand the caster.
WAY OF THE VOICE.20: The target will consider the caster to be a staunch ally and friend, and will obey any commands directly issued by the caster which are not truly alien or self-destructive, and where no commands have been issued will act in what the target believes to be the caster's best interests. The caster must speak alone and without interruption with the target for at least one minute per level of the target, within 50' of the target, and the target must hear and understand the caster. The allegiance will be terminated if the target is presented with irrefutable evidence that the caster has betrayed them or if the caster orders the target to perform a truly alien act.
WAY OF THE VOICE.25: All who can hear the caster will hear him in their native language, and the caster may concentrate on understanding a different language each round. The caster may only understand a single language per round through use of this spell.
WAY OF THE VOICE.30: As Orate I, except the bonus is +50.
WAY OF THE VOICE.35: As Calming Oration, except those affected may take no action whatsoever.
WAY OF THE VOICE.40: All within range who can hear and understand the caster are freed from any negative mental influence as long as they can hear the caster continuing to speak. Negative mental effects may make a RR to resist this spell.
WAY OF THE VOICE.50: As Voice of Dominion, except caster must speak with the target for 10 minutes per level of the target, and the duration is permanent unless terminated early as described in Voice of Dominion.

MIND VISIONS.1: Caster is aware of the presence of all sentient/thinking beings within range. The caster may opt to use this spell to become aware of animal presences within this range (unlike the normal Presence ability), but this requires the expenditure of 1 PP in the casting of the spell.
MIND VISIONS.2: Caster stores a mental pattern of target for later use with other spells. The target must first be located by any Presence spell (e.g., Seer's Presence) or Awareness.
MIND VISIONS.3: Caster learns one of the following concerning a target: race, profession, or level. The target must have been located by any Presence spell or Awareness.
MIND VISIONS.4: Caster gets direction and distance to any unshielded mind for which caster has a Mind Stored reference pattern.
MIND VISIONS.5: Caster receives surface thoughts from target.
MIND VISIONS.6: Target must answer single-concept questions truthfully. Questions are asked and answered mentally. One question may be asked per round.
MIND VISIONS.7: As Seer's Analysis, except caster learns race, profession, sex, age, and level of the target.
MIND VISIONS.8: As Seer's Presence, plus a general knowledge of the actions of each being (e.g., being is casting a spell, but not what spell is being cast).
MIND VISIONS.9: The caster knows when anyone within the radius is lying.
MIND VISIONS.10: As Seer's Presence, except within a 50' radius at a range of 100' per level. The caster can concentrate on one such area each round.
MIND VISIONS.11: As Thoughts, except caster also learns reasoning and thought patterns behind surface thoughts.
MIND VISIONS.12: As Awareness, except that very detailed knowledge of actions is given.
MIND VISIONS.13: As Mind Store, except the range is 100' per level.
MIND VISIONS.14: As Mind Typing, except the range is 100' per level.
MIND VISIONS.15: As Mind Finding I, except range is 1 mile per level.
MIND VISIONS.16: As Inner Thoughts, except affects a single target and caster can also scan target's conscious memories; at a rate of 1 scene/round.
MIND VISIONS.17: As Truth I, except within a 50' radius.
MIND VISIONS.18: As Truth I, except when this spell is cast before any Vision Behind spell, it will detect anyone lying within the vision.
MIND VISIONS.19: As Mind Finding I, except range is 5 miles per level.
MIND VISIONS.20: As Mind Scan, except caster can probe target's subconscious memories (i.e., all experiences).
MIND VISIONS.25: Caster can remove one thought or memory from the target's mind each round.
MIND VISIONS.30: This can be cast as Truth V with a duration of one minute per level or as Long Truth with a range of 100' per level.
MIND VISIONS.35: Caster is aware which individuals in the radius are having thoughts of a particular type. The type may be as specific or general as desired (e.g., thoughts about murdering the king with a magical dagger, or thoughts about any sort of weather), but the caster does not learn any details of those thoughts, only whether or not each individual is having thoughts that meet the specified description.
MIND VISIONS.40: As Truth V, except the caster is also aware of other types of magical and non-magical deception in addition to lies. For example, the caster is aware of illusions, glamours, mind tricks, disguises, forgeries, and counterfeits. The caster is aware of the general category of deception (e.g., the caster realizes there is an illusion) but not the details.
MIND VISIONS.50: As Mind Finding I, except range is unlimited.

STARTLIGHTS.1: Beam of light (like a flashlight) springs from the caster's palm; it has a 50' effective range. If the caster's hand is closed into a fist, the light will "turn off". If the caster's fist is reopened before the end of the duration, the light will turn on again.
STARTLIGHTS.2: Causes a bright aura about the caster, providing a more powerful appearance and subtracting 5 from all attacks on the caster.
STARTLIGHTS.3: Lights either one area with a 20' radius or two areas with a 10' radius each (i.e., a total radius of 20'). This spell may be cast onto a target as explained in Spell Law section 10.17.
STARTLIGHTS.4: [RR Mod: -10] Causes a 10'R sphere of intense light, all within are stunned (-50) for 1 round/10 failure.
STARTLIGHTS.5: A bolt of intense, charged light is shot from the palm of the caster; results are determined on the Lightning Bolt attack table, as a Miniscule attack.
STARTLIGHTS.6: As Self Aura I, except subtracts 10 from all attacks.
STARTLIGHTS.7: A ball of light one foot in diameter is shot from the palm of the caster: it will travel to the limit of Long range, explode (as a flare), burn with a bright light (as a flare), drift slowly to earth, and go out. An area equal to the range is lit if the flare can rise to its full range; drops 10'/round. It can be fired at a target as a Small Fire Bolt.
STARTLIGHTS.8: Nullifies all magically created darkness in a 10'R, and lights that area as full daylight.
STARTLIGHTS.9: As Self Aura I, except subtracts 15 from all attacks.
STARTLIGHTS.10: Ray of light of any color springs from caster's palm; can be up to 5 miles long.
STARTLIGHTS.11: As Lights II, except up to 6 areas can be lit with a total radius of 60'.
STARTLIGHTS.12: A bolt of intense coherent light (color chosen by caster at the time of casting, but cannot be white) is shot from the caster's palm. The attack is resolved as a Medium Fire Bolt attack, with the following special rules: If the bolt hits a reflective surface (such as a mirror or a highly polished breastplate), the bolt will be harmlessly scattered; however the reflective surface will be burned/tarnished and lose its reflectivity until repaired or polished. If the bolt hits a surface which has the same color as the bolt (e.g., a green bolt hits the target's green robes), the attack is reduced by one size (to Small).
STARTLIGHTS.13: As Lights II, except caster can delay the spell up to 24 hours; it can be triggered by one of the following (decided by caster): elapsed time, specific movements, specific sounds, touch, etc.
STARTLIGHTS.14: As Self Aura I, except subtracts 20 from all attacks.
STARTLIGHTS.15: Creates a field of twinkling stars which provides dim illumination (-20) but which is very difficult to notice from outside the area of effect.
STARTLIGHTS.16: As Beacon V, except the ray can be up to 10 miles long.
STARTLIGHTS.17: As Lights II, except up to 20 areas can be lit with a total radius of 200'.
STARTLIGHTS.18: As Utterlight I, except up to five areas can be created with a total radius of 50'.
STARTLIGHTS.19: A bolt of intense coherent light (color chosen by caster at the time of casting, but cannot be white) is shot from the caster's palm. The attack is resolved as a Medium Fire Bolt attack, with the following special rules: If the bolt hits a reflective surface (such as a mirror or a highly polished breastplate), the bolt will be harmlessly scattered; however the reflective surface will be burned/tarnished and lose its reflectivity until repaired or polished. If the bolt hits a surface which has the same color as the bolt (e.g., a green bolt hits the target's green robes), the attack is reduced by one size (to Small).
STARTLIGHTS.20: As Self Aura I, except subtracts 25 from all attacks.
STARTLIGHTS.25: Focuses starlight or moonlight as a lens, must be focused initially on a fixed point. The lens can be moved at a rate of 1'/round, after the first round. It will burn through a 1' diameter at a rate of: 1' wood/round, 4" stone/round, or 1" metal/round. This spell cannot be used effectively in combat (as foes can easily move out of the way). However, if used on an immobile foe, see Starhand for damage resolution.
STARTLIGHTS.30: As Starfires, except the initial focus is 6" from open palm of caster (caster's arm is immune unless he fumbles) and it can be moved 10'/round. If used in melee, it strikes on the Fire Bolt table (with concussion hits doubled) using the caster's Directed Spell: Elemental Bolts skill; concentration is not required when focus is fixed 6" from palm. If the attack is fumbled (01-02 UM), the caster takes an automatic C Heat Critical.
STARTLIGHTS.35: Light shines down from the sky (which must be visible to the caster), illuminating the area of effect as brightly as daylight.
STARTLIGHTS.40: A bolt of intense coherent light (color chosen by caster at the time of casting, but cannot be white) is shot from the sky (which must be visible to the caster). The attack is resolved as a Medium Fire Bolt attack, with the following special rules: If the bolt hits a reflective surface (such as a mirror or a highly polished breastplate), the bolt will be harmlessly scattered; however the reflective surface will be burned/tarnished and lose its reflectivity until repaired or polished. If the bolt hits a surface which has the same color as the bolt (e.g., a green bolt hits the target's green robes), the attack is reduced by one size (to Small).
STARTLIGHTS.50: As Starfires or Starhand, except star/moonlight is not required.

PAST VISIONS.1: Caster gains a general idea of the place of origin of an item.
PAST VISIONS.2: Detects a curse on an item or person.
PAST VISIONS.3: Caster receives a vision of events that occurred up to 1 minute per level into the past. The caster must select the point in the past to be viewed (and the vision will be accurate within one minute). The vision must be associated with a person, place, or object touched at the time of casting. The vision includes sight and sound, and will last up to 1 round per level if the caster concentrates and remains inactive. Time passes at a rate of one round of real time per 10 rounds of vision.
PAST VISIONS.4: Caster learns the origins of an item's power.
PAST VISIONS.5: This spell gives the caster the ability to scan the past by "feeling the temporal location for significant events." This translates to the caster knowing the approximate time-frames of significant events, without knowing the nature of those events. If the caster casts a Vision Behind spell within one minute of casting this spell, he will be able to see the specific events.
PAST VISIONS.6: Caster gets a vision of a significant event in the item's past.
PAST VISIONS.7: As Vision Behind I, except up to 10 minutes per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±5 minutes), and the vision can last up to one minute per level.
PAST VISIONS.8: When cast before a Vision Behind spell, the caster may perceive the past using one (and only one) additional sense (i.e., smell, taste, feel).
PAST VISIONS.9: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 hour per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±30 minutes), and the vision can last up to five minutes per level.
PAST VISIONS.10: Caster learns the significant details about an item's construction and purpose (not specific powers).
PAST VISIONS.11: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 day per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 hour), and the vision can last up to ten minutes per level.
PAST VISIONS.12: As Item Vision, except gives a vision of a significant event in the past which occurred at the caster's current location.
PAST VISIONS.13: Caster may cast this spell while in a Vision Behind; it saves an image of a person, location, or object that can later be used by another Vision Behind spell to key in on the saved image.
PAST VISIONS.14: Caster learns the origin of a curse, the source of its power, its effects, its required cure, and its effectiveness (i.e., level).
PAST VISIONS.15: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 month per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 day), and the vision can last up to 1 hour per level.
PAST VISIONS.16: The caster gains complete information on the item's construction, purpose, magical abilities, and any non-magical bonuses.
PAST VISIONS.17: As Vision Behind I, except up to 1 year per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 week), and the vision can last up to 5 hours per level.
PAST VISIONS.18: Caster gets a vision of a significant event in the person's past.
PAST VISIONS.19: Casting this spell prior to a Vision Behind spell will cause it to appear in a suitable reflecting medium (e.g., pool, crystal ball, mirror). Persons other than the caster will only see the visual aspects of the vision. Each person other than the caster will continue to share the vision until they stop concentrating, the caster stops concentrating, or the trance ends.
PAST VISIONS.20: Casting this spell before Vision Behind will cause that spell to key in on the event most closely matching a description specified by the caster. The more accurate and specific the description, the more accurate this spell will be.
PAST VISIONS.25: As Vision Behind I, except up to 10 years per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 month), and the vision can last up to 10 hours per level.
PAST VISIONS.30: As Vision Behind I, except up to 100 years per level into the past (with an accuracy of ±1 year), and the vision can last up to 1 day per level.
PAST VISIONS.35: Caster may revisit any of their own past experiences. The memory is accurately enhanced, allowing the caster to note details that were missed at the time and recall vividly details that had been forgotten or misremembered.
PAST VISIONS.40: If cast before any Vision Behind, time during the vision passes at a rate of one minute of real time per hour of the vision.
PAST VISIONS.50: As Vision Behind I, except any point in the past (with an accuracy of ±10 years), and the vision can last up to 1 day per level. Time passes at a rate of 1 minute of real time per hour of the vision.

DEMONIC BINDING.1: Each round, the caster may learn one of the following about a single demon: level, plane of origin, one talent, one flaw, one spell list, one skill bonus. Skill bonuses are learned from largest on down to (eventually) smallest, talents and flaws from most DP involved to least (ignoring negative nature of flaw “cost”), and otherwise in random order within the chosen category.
DEMONIC BINDING.2: Allows caster to bring out the demonic nature of an item into which a demon has been embedded. This will have cosmetic effects, transforming the appearance of the item to reflect the nature of the embedded demon. It will also give the attuned bearer of the item a bonus equal to that of the level of the embedded demon (not the level of the item) to Creature Lore: Demon maneuvers and SCRs casting spells dealing with demons.
DEMONIC BINDING.3: Cast once per day, this spell allows the caster to give an intelligent item the power of touch telepathy or the power of speech. Cast twice per day (double time and PP requirement), it can provide the power of ranged telepathy (with a range equal to its level in feet).
DEMONIC BINDING.4: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded demon’s talents up to a limit of 6 DP value.
DEMONIC BINDING.5: Allows caster to embed a Type I demon into an object as described in Section 5.3.
DEMONIC BINDING.6: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded demon’s Open spell lists. These spells may be cast using the wielder's PP or the item's PP (e.g., from Manifest Power).
DEMONIC BINDING.7: Allows caster to provide access to three of an embedded demon’s skills for purposes of the item’s own use or the direct use of the item.
DEMONIC BINDING.8: There are few things as good at killing a demon as another demon. This spell allows the caster to turn a weapon containing an embedded demon into one which gains +10 OB when fighting Extra Planar Creatures, is Slaying II against one Variety of demon and Slaying I against all demons of the same Type as that Variety. The embedded demon must be at least Type II for this enchantment.
DEMONIC BINDING.9: Allows caster to provide access to an embedded demon’s normal PP total, for use in casting spells from its lists.
DEMONIC BINDING.10: Allows caster to embed a Type II or lesser demon into an object as described in Section 5.3.
DEMONIC BINDING.11: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded demon’s Closed spell lists. These spells may be cast using the wielder's PP or the item's PP (e.g., from Manifest Power).
DEMONIC BINDING.12: As Manifest Talent I, but limit is 20 DP.
DEMONIC BINDING.13: This spell allows the caster to turn a weapon containing an embedded demon into one which gains +15 OB when fighting Extra Planar Creatures, is Slaying III against one Variety of demon and Slaying II against all demons of the same Type as that Variety and Slaying I against other Extra Planar Creatures. The embedded demon must be at least Type III for this enchantment.
DEMONIC BINDING.14: Allows caster to make one of an embedded demon’s stat bonuses available to the wielder or to make one of the embedded demon’s physical stat bonuses (Ag, Co, Qu, St) available for the item’s use.
DEMONIC BINDING.15: Allows caster to embed a Type III or lesser demon into an object as described in Section 5.3.
DEMONIC BINDING.16: Allows caster to provide access to three of an embedded demon’s skills for all purposes.
DEMONIC BINDING.17: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded demon’s spell lists which is neither an Open nor a Closed list (Base or Evil). These spells may be cast using the wielder's PP or the item's PP (e.g., from Manifest Power).
DEMONIC BINDING.18: As Manifest Talent I, but limit is 40 DP.
DEMONIC BINDING.19: This spell allows the caster to turn a weapon containing an embedded demon into one which gains +20 OB when fighting Extra Planar Creatures, is Slaying IV against one Variety of demon and Slaying III against all demons of the same Type as that Variety and Slaying II against other Extra Planar Creatures. The embedded demon must be at least Type IV for this enchantment.
DEMONIC BINDING.20: Allows caster to embed a Type IV or lesser demon into an object as described in Section 5.3.
DEMONIC BINDING.25: Allows caster to provide access to general traits of an embedded demon, such as its level for purposes of the bearer’s RRs, a full set of senses (without talents) in item form, etc.
DEMONIC BINDING.30: As Manifest Talent I, but limit is 75 DP.
DEMONIC BINDING.35: Allows caster to embed a Type V or lesser demon into an object as described in Section 5.3.
DEMONIC BINDING.40: This spell allows the caster to turn a weapon containing an embedded demon into one which gains +25 OB when fighting Extra Planar Creatures, is Slaying IV against one Type of demon and Slaying III against other Extra Planar Creatures. The embedded demon must be at least Type V for this enchantment.
DEMONIC BINDING.50: Allows caster to embed a Type VI or lesser demon into an object as described in Section 5.3.
DEMONIC BINDING.60: As Manifest Talent I, but there is no limit on the talent’s DP cost.
DEMONIC BINDING.75: Allows caster to empower an item containing an embedded demon of at least Type V to grant the power to travel between the mortal and demonic spheres, as well as between one demon plane and another. If the embedded demon is only Type V, it can only offer access to the demonic planes of its own general type (e.g., a Demon of the Pales would grant transport to and from the various Pales), while a more powerful demon allows access all the demon planes. The item’s bearer will be acclimatized to the ambient conditions of the plane travelled to. The transfer between planes can be used no more often than once per day and requires a full minute of concentration to achieve.
DEMONIC BINDING.90: Allows caster to embed any demon into an object as described in Section 5.3. The embedding of demons beyond Type VI is generally a task best left to gods or god-like beings, but strange things can happen.

ORGANIC SKILLS.1: Allows caster to work with non-magical paper to create an enchanted item. All required tools and material must be present. Alternatively, this spell can be used to work on non-magical paper without enchanting it, in which case the caster can do the work in half the normal time. In either case, the caster gains a +30 bonus to his relevant Crafting maneuver(s).
ORGANIC SKILLS.2: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with non-magical fabric.
ORGANIC SKILLS.3: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with non-magical leather or hide.
ORGANIC SKILLS.4: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with non-magical wood.
ORGANIC SKILLS.5: Allows caster to make a sheet of paper or parchment (vellum, etc.) which will hold a rune as described in the Open Essence spell list Rune Mastery (or the Sanctifier spell list Sacred Runes).
ORGANIC SKILLS.6: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any non-magical organic materials.
ORGANIC SKILLS.7: Allows the caster to make a “wand” which may have spells embedded in it.
ORGANIC SKILLS.8: Allows the caster to create a piece of rune paper that will allow the rune to be used twice before it vanishes. The first use of the rune will cause it to fade a bit, so it is easy to tell if the rune has one or two uses left, but not so much as to make it difficult to read.
ORGANIC SKILLS.9: Allows the caster to make an item with a non-”constant” embedded spell that does not require attunement, but is instead activated by a given “trigger” (e.g., the holder speaking a certain word, a certain species comes within range of the embedded spell, a certain part of the item is twisted clockwise, or the item is touched to someone with a bleeding wound). Note that because the action is automatic, the user has no ability to perform target-selection or the like. The conditions set for the trigger must include any necessary target selection or other choices that would normally fall on the caster of the embedded spell (e.g., the item casts the spell on the first person to touch it) This spell provides the activation method, but does not embed the spell to be triggered, which must be done normally. Note that single-use items (see Single Use Items in section 5.3) may be created with triggers without the need for this spell.
ORGANIC SKILLS.10: Allows the caster to make a “rod” which may have spells embedded in it.
ORGANIC SKILLS.11: Allows a caster to create an item which casts any embedded spells at a level greater than the level of the embedded spell. The spell will be cast at the lower of the level of the item itself or the level of caster providing the embedded spell.
ORGANIC SKILLS.12: When cast immediately before a Make Rune Paper spell, this allows any non-living organic material to be made capable of holding a rune (e.g., a rune could then be inscribed on a wooden chair or a hide shield). The object must be at least 3" by 3" in size.
ORGANIC SKILLS.13: Allows the caster to create an organic magical item that is reduced from its normal size. For example a “rod” could be made wand-sized. To make a “staff” wand-sized would require that this spell be cast twice each day during item creation: once to convert the “staff” to rodsized and then a second reduction to move from rod-sized to wand-sized.
ORGANIC SKILLS.14: Allows the caster to make a “staff” which may have spells embedded in it.
ORGANIC SKILLS.15: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any paper (e.g., including magical scrolls).
ORGANIC SKILLS.16: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any fabric (e.g., including magical cloth).
ORGANIC SKILLS.17: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any leather or hide (e.g., including magical leather or hide).
ORGANIC SKILLS.18: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any wood (e.g., dask or springwood).
ORGANIC SKILLS.19: Allows the caster to make a “half-bole” which may have spells embedded in it.
ORGANIC SKILLS.20: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any organic materials (e.g. dragon scale).
ORGANIC SKILLS.25: Allows the caster to make a “bole” which may have spells embedded in it.
ORGANIC SKILLS.30: Allows the caster to enchant an item that will transform any living organic being into a “non-dangerous” animal form (e.g., swan, sheep, rabbit) when worn. This requires something from an animal of this type (typically a feather or bit of hair). The creature into which the wearer transforms must be selected at the time of the item’s enchantment, as must whether the wearer’s worn and carried possessions other than the transformation item (which always transforms with the wearer) merge into wearer’s altered form or fall to the ground when the wearer transforms. Transformed gear cannot be used unless it has a magical effect when simply carried, but the transformation item may normally be taken off while in beast form at any time. This effect can be made “at will” (allowing the wearing of the item in human form or the ability to transform into more than one creature using a single item) by doubling the time and PP spent on this spell.
ORGANIC SKILLS.35: When cast immediately before a Make Rune Paper spell, this allows a living organic being to be made capable of holding a rune. The rune will take the appearance of a tattoo, brand, or painted/dyed skin or fur. This spell ends when the creature dies.
ORGANIC SKILLS.40: As Lesser Transformation, except that the wearer transforms into a dangerous animal (e.g., tiger, cobra, hippo).
ORGANIC SKILLS.50: As Lesser Transformation, except that the wearer transforms into a magical living creature (e.g., gryphon, unicorn, wyvern). This excludes all races, undead, demons, great drakes, elementals, and artificial creatures. While the wearer of the transformation item gains all innate abilities of the being into which he transforms, no skill is automatically granted for magical abilities (i.e., flight with wings would “come naturally”, but a breath weapon would need to be learned in order to develop OB).
ORGANIC SKILLS.60: As Work Mundane Paper, except caster may work with any living plant to create an enchanted plant, and the +30 bonus applies to applicable maneuvers when working with the plant.
ORGANIC SKILLS.75: As Work Plant, except caster may work with any normal beast to create an enchanted beast.
ORGANIC SKILLS.90: As Work Plant, except caster may work with any organic living being to place enchantments upon it.

GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.1: Allows caster to enchant an item that will always provide the attuned bearer with a last second sense of peril when he would otherwise be caught flatfooted, leading him to merely be surprised instead.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.2: Allows caster to enchant an item to detect the presence of one thing, be it a particular race, metal, stone, etc., such as Orcs, gold, or emeralds. When the thing is present within its detection radius, the item will glow, chime, or otherwise emit some set signal. Base detection radius is 5', but this spell may be cast at an effectively higher level in order to increase the radius by 5' per increased level (e.g., Detection could be cast as a 5th level spell, costing 5 PP per casting, and requiring a base 5 days for enchantment, to increase the detection radius to 20'). By doubling the time and PP spent on this spell, detection can be of a broader category such as demons, precious metals, or gems.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.3: Allows caster to enchant an item that has two different forms. Both of the forms must be created as separate items, either at the same time or separately, and then combined into a single object with multiple forms through this spell. The Multiform enchantment itself must be added to the item which will take the most days to enchant, which must be completed last in order to absorb the other forms, but does not need to be added to both forms. Enchantments on the separate forms must be done for each individually and appropriate Work spells used on all objects to be combined even if some forms have no enchantments of their own. An individual “form” may be multiple objects, so one can make a sword that can become two swords, but this would require Work spells for each of the three swords and any abilities to be added at this time would need to be cast on each sword independently, even if the powers were the same. Abilities of each item are independent.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.4: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it provides a +1 bonus to Initiative.This bonus may be increased by casting this spell multiple times, with the result counting as a single ability (e.g., a +3 bonus requires casting Initiative Bonus three times a day, and produces a 12th level ability). This bonus normally applies only when using the item (useful mainly for weapons). By doubling the time and PP spent on this enchantment, the bonus may apply to all actions.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.5: The caster gains complete information on the item’s magical abilities and any non-magical bonuses. Attunement may still be required to make use of the item.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.6: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it provides a +5 bonus to one unspecialized skill or skill specialization or provides a +5 bonus to one type of RR (one realm, Physical, or Fear) or adds 2 ranks to an unspecialized skill or one skill specialization for uses of that skill that use the number of skill ranks only (e.g., +2 ranks of Running skill for purposes of passive Dodging but granting no skill bonus for Running maneuvers or partial or full Dodging). Although bonus items may grant bonuses to Combat Training skills (e.g., gloves which grant a bonus to Ranged Weapons), these bonuses are not cumulative with any bonuses from weapons.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.7: As Multiform II, except that the item can assume three different forms.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.8: Allows caster to enchant one container so that the contents will suffer no ill effects from any exterior force so long as the container is intact. For example, a chest enchanted with this spell could tumble down a staircase and glassware within would not only not be broken, it would not even have become disorganized.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.9: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it turns 50% of Absolute Failure results by the bearer in a given skill category into ordinary failures.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.10: As General I, except bonus is +10 for skills and RRs, while 4 ranks may be added for skill rank purposes.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.11: Allows caster to enchant an item that provides a +1 increase to the stat bonus of one stat specified at the time of casting.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.12: As Multiform II, except that the item can assume four different forms.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.13: Allows caster to enchant one container so that the contents will have half their normal weight. This ability may be given to an item more than once by casting this spell multiple times per day during the enchantment. For example, a backpack which had been enchanted with Enhance Portability twice and contained 60 pounds of loot would weigh as if it was carrying only one-quarter that amount (15 pounds).
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.14: Allows caster to enchant one container so that the attuned user can always take out the item he is looking for immediately (it is a 1 AP action to retrieve any item from the container).
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.15: As General I, except bonus is +15 for skills and RRs, while 6 ranks may be added for skill rank purposes.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.16: As Multiform II, except that the item can assume five different forms.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.17: Allows caster to enchant one container so that the interior dimensions are twice those of the exterior dimensions. This allows a 2' x 2' x 3' chest to hold 4' x 4' x 6' of contents. This ability may be given to an item more than once, doubling each interior dimension each time. This spell is applicable to “containers” of people, so can produce a deceptively spacious hovel, tent, etc.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.18: Allows caster to enchant an item such that the maximum cost for its use is reduced by one AP. The minimum cost remains the same, but penalties are calculated based on the altered maximum. For example a sword with Reduced Time I would only require 3 AP for a full melee attack and would attack at -25 (rather than the usual -50) if only 2 AP were used to attack with it.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.19: As Stat Bonus I, except an increase of +2.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.20: As Multiform II, except that the item can assume up to as many different forms as the caster’s level divided by three (round down).
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.25: As Stat Bonus I, except an increase of +3.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.30: As General I, except bonus is +20 for skills and RRs, while 8 ranks may be added for skill rank purposes.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.35: As Stat Bonus I, except an increase of +4.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.40: As Reduced Time I, except that reduction is by two AP.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.50: As Stat Bonus I, except an increase of +5.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.60: As General I, except bonus is +25 for skills and RRs, while 10 ranks may be added for skill rank purposes.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.75: As General I, except bonus is +30 for skills and RRs, while 12 ranks may be added for skill rank purposes.
GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.90: As General I, except bonus is +35 for skills and RRs, while 14 ranks may be added for skill rank purposes.

EMPOWERING PLACES.1: Caster learns of any permanent enchantments or any influences such as resident spirits or other supernatural features of the location. This does not reveal spells that do not have a lasting magical effect or any supernatural features not tied to the location (it would not indicate a possessed individual or demon-powered sword that happened to be on the site, unless it were a strong enough influence to interfere with enchanting the site, though this spell would reveal if a ghost resided there, though that might not interfere with a desired enchantment).
EMPOWERING PLACES.2: Removes contrary influences from a location. This is required prior to any enchantment of a location using this list. If there are no extraordinary influences (such as revealed by Location Analysis), this should be automatically successful. Normal psychic residue is cleared up without a problem; a conflicting magical effect would be entitled to an RR. If a location is enchanted in a contrary way, this spell can be used as a counter-enchantment. In that case, it becomes a Type “A” spell and must be cast once/day for as many days as the level of the existing enchantment. At that point, the existing enchantment gets an RR. If it succeeds, the effort was wasted. If it fails, the old enchantment is broken and the caster can proceed to enchant the location. Channeling enchantments on a place may have a bonus of up to +50, if the enchanted location is in some way inherently sacred to the faith of those who enchanted it.
EMPOWERING PLACES.3: The area of effect for Work Location spells is given in feet. If the location is a defined space with borders, this indicates the maximum length of any side of an enclosing cube. If the location has no defined borders, this is a diameter (not radius) around the central point. The place enchanted must have a conceptual unity. Destroying the unifying concept (burning down the building, paving over the garden, etc.) will destroy the enchantment. This spell allows the caster to enchant a location in conjunction with other spells on this list.
EMPOWERING PLACES.4: Allows caster to enchant a location so that those within the area recover 1 power point every 4 hours spent within the location (in addition to any normal recovery) or allows the caster to enchant a location so that it has power to cast an Emplaced or Embedded spell of 1st level.
EMPOWERING PLACES.5: Allows caster to enchant a location so that anyone entering the location must make an RR or be affected by a mood (from the Mood Impressions list) so long as he remains in the enchanted location.
EMPOWERING PLACES.6: Allows caster to enchant a location so that anyone entering the place will have a spell cast upon him (no more often than once per day). This spell may be included in the enchantment through either an Emplace Spell or an Embed spell, plus (in either case) a Magical Aura spell of sufficient power.
EMPOWERING PLACES.7: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.8: Allows caster to enchant a location with up to a 10th level spell from the Skill Impressions list or a Talent Embedding spell of no more than 10th level. All within the location gain the benefit of this effect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.9: As Magical Aura I, except recovery rate is 1 power point every 2 hours or the Emplaced or Embedded spell may be of up to 3rd level.
EMPOWERING PLACES.10: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.11: Allows caster to enchant a location so that anyone in the location must make an RR every hour or be affected by a mood (from the Mood Impressions list) so long as he remains in the enchanted location.
EMPOWERING PLACES.12: Allows caster to enchant a location so that a spirit within the location will be constrained to remain within that location. The spirit must be within the location when the caster completes the enchantment (he can all but finish the enchantment process and complete it upon the spirit being brought into the location in a single 4 AP spell-casting action). Spirit does not get an RR, except to recognize that the location is a trap. Spirit need not be free at the time of confinement (e.g., it could be trapped in an object that is placed in the location, which would also prevent the object from being removed from the location so long as the enchantment lasts and the spirit remains within).
EMPOWERING PLACES.13: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.14: As Magical Aura I, except recovery rate is 1 power point per hour or the Emplaced or Embedded spell may be of up to 5th level.
EMPOWERING PLACES.15: As Lesser Enchanted Locale, except that up to a 20th level spell may be used.
EMPOWERING PLACES.16: As Welcoming Spell, except that the spell does not affect a target upon the target entering the location, but upon performing some triggering action or having some triggering quality (e.g., starting a fire or being an Orc or having a bleeding wound). Spell may only be triggered once per day per individual.
EMPOWERING PLACES.17: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.18: Allows caster to enchant a location so that anyone who would otherwise observe it must make an RR or suffer a mental “blind spot” so that he does not notice the location is there. This does not make the location invisible; it prevents those failing the RR from acknowledging that the place is there, though they will go around it without being aware that they are making such an effort. If someone is attacked from the location, he immediately ceases to be subject to the effect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.19: As Magical Aura I, except recovery rate is 2 power points per hour or the Emplaced or Embedded spell may be of up to 7th level.
EMPOWERING PLACES.20: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.25: Allows caster to enchant a location so that any spirit entering the location must make an RR. If it fails, it will be confined to the location so long as the enchantment lasts.
EMPOWERING PLACES.30: As Lesser Enchanted Locale, except that there is no level limit on the spell included in the enchantment.
EMPOWERING PLACES.35: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.40: As Magical Aura I, except recovery rate is 3 power points per hour or the Emplaced or Embedded spell may be of up to 12th level.
EMPOWERING PLACES.50: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.
EMPOWERING PLACES.60: As Magical Aura I, except recovery rate is 4 power points per hour or the Emplaced or Embedded spell may be of up to 20th level.
EMPOWERING PLACES.75: Allows caster to enchant a location through the use of Spirit Binding, Demon Binding, or Elemental Binding spell lists, creating a location-sized entitypowered enchantment. The entity will be able to make its abilities manifest anywhere within the location.
EMPOWERING PLACES.90: As Work Location II, except for size of location it can affect.

INORGANIC SKILLS.1: Gives nature and origin of natural metal, and when and how worked metal was obtained and worked.
INORGANIC SKILLS.2: Gives nature and origin of natural stone, and when and how worked stone was obtained and worked.
INORGANIC SKILLS.3: Allows caster to work with non-magical non-precious stone to create an enchanted item. All required tools and material must be present. Alternatively, this spell can be used to work on non-magical non-precious stone without enchanting it, in which case the caster can do the work in half the normal time. In either case, the caster gains a +30 bonus to his relevant Crafting maneuver(s).
INORGANIC SKILLS.4: Allows caster a +30 bonus to any maneuvers to produce an alloy. This spell is advised (but not required) when creating an item which is made from the components of an alloy rather than beginning with alloyed metal, as a Metalcraft maneuver will be required to create the alloy.
INORGANIC SKILLS.5: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +0 (e.g., iron or inferior bronze).
INORGANIC SKILLS.6: Allows caster to create a charged item of inorganic materials (the name of the spell being something of a misnomer, as one could create a staff of glass if one chose), when used in conjunction with the appropriate Make spell (see Organic Skills list).
INORGANIC SKILLS.7: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +5 (e.g., low steel or superior bronze).
INORGANIC SKILLS.8: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical precious stone.
INORGANIC SKILLS.9: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +10 (e.g., high steel).
INORGANIC SKILLS.10: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any non-precious stone.
INORGANIC SKILLS.11: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +5 (including magical materials, e.g., zataak).
INORGANIC SKILLS.12: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +15 (e.g., white alloy).
INORGANIC SKILLS.13: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical non-metallic inorganic materials (e.g., glass).
INORGANIC SKILLS.14: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +10.
INORGANIC SKILLS.15: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +20 (e.g., black alloy).
INORGANIC SKILLS.16: Allows the caster to create an inorganic magical item that is reduced from its normal size. For example a “rod” could be made wand-sized. To make a “staff” wandsized would require that this spell be cast twice each day during item creation: once to convert the “staff” to rod-sized and then a second reduction to move from rod-sized to wand-sized.
INORGANIC SKILLS.17: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any precious stone.
INORGANIC SKILLS.18: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any non-magical metals.
INORGANIC SKILLS.19: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +15 (e.g., starfall).
INORGANIC SKILLS.20: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any non-metallic inorganic materials (e.g., laen).
INORGANIC SKILLS.25: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +20.
INORGANIC SKILLS.30: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it turns the usual protection of items by the bearer’s aura somewhat into reverse, offering some of the strength of its aura to protect the bearer. This allows the bearer to make all RRs against magic as if he were of at least 20th level. If the bearer is actually of 20th or higher level, he receives no benefit.
INORGANIC SKILLS.35: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +25 (e.g., adamant steel).
INORGANIC SKILLS.40: As Mutual Aura I, except minimum level is 30th.
INORGANIC SKILLS.50: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +30 (e.g., eog).
INORGANIC SKILLS.60: As Mutual Aura I, except minimum level is 50th.
INORGANIC SKILLS.75: As Work Mundane Stone, except caster may work with any metals.
INORGANIC SKILLS.90: Allows caster to create an item that is nigh-indestructible. This item will never fail a breakage check and gains a second RR against any spell that would destroy or break it. If this power is given twice, the item will become almost impossible to destroy, requiring some special method be employed, which must be specified at the time of casting.

DEEP IMPRESSIONS.1: Allows caster to create a potion granting an enchantment that can apply to an imbiber for a duration of 15 minutes. The enchantment to be included in the potion may be any suitable spell(s) from this spell list, Mood Impressions (generally Infuse Mood), Power Impressions, or Skill Impressions. In addition to these spells, Work Mundane Liquid is also required.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.2: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it grants a bonus to a stat of +0. If the wielder of the item has a lower stat bonus (i.e., a negative bonus), then it is raised to +0.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.3: As Enchanting Elixir I, except the effect of the potion will last for an hour.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.4: Allows caster to enchant an item such that the item can keep a spell requiring Concentration going on its own (though it cannot make adjustments to the spell effect unless intelligent). If the spell is a constant one, this can be maintained indefinitely. For individual castings of the spell, the item can maintain concentration for 1 round per item level. This can only allow the item to concentrate on spells provided by the item.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.5: Allows caster to create an item such that a spell may be stored within it. The spell may be of no more than 5th level, and it is stored by casting the spell normally, except that it is targeted “for storage” and goes into the item. Later, the wielder may cast the spell as if casting from an item, except that the spell is cast at its normal casting level and is cast as an instantaneous spell.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.6: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it will negate 10% of spell failure effects (negation means that the wielder need not roll on the spell failure table, but the spell will still fail quietly and PP expended will be lost).
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.7: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it grants a bonus to a stat of up to +5. If the wielder of the item has a lower stat bonus, then it is raised to the bonus granted. The bonus requires an individual with the bonus to be granted to serve as the “template.” If this template is not the caster himself, then the Template Link spell from the Power Impression spell list must be cast at the start of the enchantment process.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.8: Allows caster to create an item with Spell Storage such that the spell(s) stored may be of up to level 10. Both Spell Storage and Deepen Storage must be cast upon the item.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.9: As Enchanting Elixir I, except the effect of the potion will last for a day (24 hours).
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.10: As Spell Storage I, except that item can store up to two spells at once.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.11: As Deepen Storage I, except the spell(s) stored may be of up to level 15.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.12: As Spell Discipline I, except 20% of spell failure effects are negated.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.13: As Fixed Bonus II, except maximum bonus is +10.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.14: As Spell Storage I, except that item can store up to three spells at once.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.15: As Deepen Storage I, except the spell(s) stored may be of up to level 20.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.16: Allows caster to create an item such that an attuned wielder can use the item for its basic function (picking locks with a lock pick, fighting with a sword, etc.) at a distance of up to 2' per level of the item. The wielder must concentrate to do so, and the item will operate with the wielder’s normal skill (unless the item itself possesses the necessary skill, in which case that may used instead). This allows the item to levitate and move about through a form of telekinesis, at up to the wielder’s normal walking speed. The wielder maintains any normal benefits from wielding the item while using it in this manner.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.17: As Spell Storage I, except that item can store up to four spells at once.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.18: As Spell Discipline I, except 30% of spell failure effects are negated.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.19: As Spell Storage I, except that item can store up to five spells at once.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.20: As Fixed Bonus II, except maximum bonus is +15.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.25: As Spell Storage I, except that item can store up to seven spells at once.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.30: As Spell Discipline I, except 40% of spell failure effects are negated.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.35: As Fixed Bonus II, except there is no limit on the bonus that may be granted, other than the need to find a template with the desired bonus.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.40: Allows caster to create an item that can continue to operate without the wielder’s assistance, but within reach. This is usually used to create a weapon that will defend its wielder when the wielder is incapable of self-defense. It will even guard its wielder’s corpse. It can distinguish attack from aid, in this case, even if not intelligent otherwise. The item will operate with the wielder’s normal skill (unless the item itself possesses the necessary skill, in which case that may used instead). This can also be used to create, for example, a shield that will float in the air near the wielder, defending him without the need for a hand to hold the shield.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.50: As Deepen Storage I, except the spell(s) stored may be of any level.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.60: Allows caster to create an item that can operate semi-autonomously, working like Remote Operation, but without the need to concentrate and with a range of up to 10' per item level. Item is given an order (“Kill all orcs in the area” or “Mend this torn shirt”, depending on the item type), which it will follow, then return to the wielder when it is done or its time is up. The item can operate in this fashion for no more than one minute per level of the wielder, needing a “charge” from the wielder’s aura to empower its operations. If the item is intelligent, it can be given a more complex mission or allowed more judgment, and it can use all of its abilities in the pursuit of that mission.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.75: Allows caster to enchant an item with Spell Storage such that so long as it has an “open slot” for storing a spell within, the wielder can concentrate to use the item to attempt to catch an incoming spell and store it within the item, both preventing the spell from having effect in the present and allowing the wielder to use the spell himself later. The incoming spell is allowed an RR against the item’s magic, and if it succeeds, it will go off normally instead.
DEEP IMPRESSIONS.90: As Spell Discipline I, except 90% of spell failure effects are negated.

SACRED STRUCTURES.1: Caster learns the purpose for which a structure was designed and built (not necessarily the current use), who built it in general terms (race/culture), when it was built, and its current condition.
SACRED STRUCTURES.2: Allows caster to provide the artificial aspects of a consecrated area with a general feel and cosmetic enhancements suitable to the deity to which it is dedicated. Generally metals gleam, surfaces stay dusted and polished, light streams majestically through stained glass windows, etc., though this may vary based on the religion in question. The temple of the spider-god would have an abundance of cobwebs due to a Splendor spell. The place will evoke awe or dread or whatever feeling is most appropriate (the temple of a god of peace might evoke calm, that of a goddess of love might stir passions, etc.).
SACRED STRUCTURES.3: Allows caster to enchant a single structure so as to make it sacred ground. This must be a structure created for, or rededicated to, a religious purpose.
SACRED STRUCTURES.4: Allows caster to provide an area of sacred ground with protection from a specific natural threat appropriate to the deity to which it is dedicated. For example, a temple of Poseidon might be protected from earthquakes. A second Grace spell might protect that same temple from tsunamis.
SACRED STRUCTURES.5: Allows caster to provide an alarm to an area of sacred ground that will sound when any hostile supernatural being enters the area. This will usually sound the alarm by ringing bells, sounding horns, or otherwise employing the site’s sound-producing equipment. It can, however, take other forms, like lighting candles or changing the color of a sacred flame.
SACRED STRUCTURES.6: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that prevents a given spell from crossing. This spell need not actually be cast during enchantment, as during embedding a spell. Variants differing only in roman numeral or the appearance of the word “True” or “Lord” are considered the same spell. The spell may make an RR against the level of the site to overcome the barrier. If the spell is active on someone crossing the barrier, it will be subject to dispelling (again with an RR against the level of the site allowed).
SACRED STRUCTURES.7: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that prevents entry by either a specific creature Variety or the followers of a particular god. An RR against the level of the site is allowed, but if the individual fails the RR, he cannot try again to enter until a number of days passes equal to the amount by which the RR failed.
SACRED STRUCTURES.8: Allows caster to enchant a walled area so as to make it sacred ground. This area must be completely enclosed in a permanent wall or fence and dedicated to a religious purpose. This allows covering church or monastery grounds or consecrating an area like a cemetery.
SACRED STRUCTURES.9: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that crafting (but not enchantment) appropriate to the faith has work time cut in half.
SACRED STRUCTURES.10: Allows caster to undo the enchantments which render a structure or walled area sacred ground. This requires casting every day for as many working days as this spell’s level (10) plus the level of the area to be affected. This process must be completed before any sacred ground may be rededicated as sacred ground to another faith. If a place is “naturally” sacred rather than being made so by the work of a Sanctifier, then double the level of the area when determining the time required.
SACRED STRUCTURES.11: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Spell Barrier, but blocks all spells from a single spell list (e.g., Light Law). Spells that appear on this list are not blocked if cast from a different list.
SACRED STRUCTURES.12: As Supernatural Alarm, except that the alarm will sound upon the entry of any hostile intruder.
SACRED STRUCTURES.13: Allows caster to enchant a body of water on sacred ground (a pool, pond, font, fountain, bath, spring, etc.) such that all of its water is holy water so long as it remains on the holy site. If removed from the sacred grounds, it will become normal water, but may be used in any way that the religion’s holy water is used while it remains within the boundaries of the sacred ground.
SACRED STRUCTURES.14: Allows the caster to enchant an altar that is part of an area of sacred ground such that anyone who prays there (to the god or gods to whom the site is dedicated) will receive the blessing of the site. In game terms, this is an attempt by the site to remove any curse, heal any mental illness, and exorcise any possessing spirit or mental invader which may be plaguing the praying individual. This may be attempted only once per particular instance of a condition (i.e., if the condition makes its RR against Channeling at the site’s level, more prayer will not work, but if a demonic spirit keeps possessing the same individual repeatedly, each possession may be prayed against once).
SACRED STRUCTURES.15: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Lesser Entry Barrier, but will bar either a creature Type or a single profession.
SACRED STRUCTURES.16: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that all Symbols on that sacred ground cast their spells at the higher of their normal level or the level of the sacred site.
SACRED STRUCTURES.17: Allows caster to create an area of sacred ground where one instrument or set of instruments (e.g., an organ, a set of bells, or drum) may be sounded in order to frighten hostile creatures. All hostiles within half a mile must make an immediate Fear RR if they can hear the sound (so loud instruments are preferred). This may be done once per day and uses the level of the sounder.
SACRED STRUCTURES.18: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Spell Barrier, but blocks a given type of spell (e.g., fire magic, teleportation, detections, scrying, influence, or curses).
SACRED STRUCTURES.19: Allows the caster to enchant a fire source on sacred ground such that when someone who uses Channeling spells from the power to which the site is dedicated gazes into the flames, they may look upon a location up to one mile away per PP they expend on the effort, the image lasting for 1-10 minutes.
SACRED STRUCTURES.20: Cast in conjunction with Spell Barrier, List Barrier, Type Barrier, Realm Barrier, or Universal Barrier, this spell causes the effect to cover the entire sacred grounds, so any attempt to cast such spells of the blocked types must make an RR against the level of the site or fail to take effect.
SACRED STRUCTURES.25: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Lesser Entry Barrier, but will bar a broad category from entering. This may be a creature Category, such as undead or extra planar creatures, but might also be a category like “men” or “weapon-bearers.”
SACRED STRUCTURES.30: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Spell Barrier, but blocks all spells from a given realm (including hybrid spells that include that realm).
SACRED STRUCTURES.35: Cast in conjunction with Spell Barrier, List Barrier, Type Barrier, Realm Barrier, or Universal Barrier, this spell causes the effect to only apply to spell effects attempting to cross into the sacred grounds, not to those leaving the sacred grounds.
SACRED STRUCTURES.40: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Spell Barrier, but blocks all spells.
SACRED STRUCTURES.50: Allows caster to create a barrier at the boundary of sacred ground that functions as a Lesser Entry Barrier, but will bar anyone other than followers of the faith to which the site is dedicated.
SACRED STRUCTURES.60: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that the OBs, SCRs, and morale of those on that ground are modified as follows: +20 to any Channeling realm member of the site’s faith, +10 to other members of the faith, -20 to any Channeling realm enemy of the site’s faith, and -10 to other enemies.
SACRED STRUCTURES.75: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that Symbols on that ground will recharge after one hour, rather than being limited to daily use.
SACRED STRUCTURES.90: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that a building, statue, or similar structure may be erected such that it defies physics (e.g., impossibly slender support, an interior larger than the exterior, or non-Euclidean internal geometries). This enchantment must be done as the impossible structure is being constructed.

WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.1: Caster learns the materials of which a target weapon is made, what bonuses it has to OB and breakage rolls, the approximate time and place of manufacture, and whether the weapon has any additional magical properties.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.2: Allows caster to enchant a weapon which negates 50% of fumbles made with the weapon.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.3: Allows caster to enchant a weapon which gains an additional +5 OB when wielded by a member of a specific race (e.g., human, Elf, or Orc).
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.4: Allows caster to enchant a melee weapon, thrown weapon, or ammunition (e.g., arrows) with a +5 OB bonus or with an additional +5 OB bonus against a specific Type of creature (see note above for costs for more or less restrictive bonuses).
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.5: Allows caster to enchant a weapon (or missile) that when thrown or launched, will return to the user after the attack via flight (with a speed a 100'/round). It will come to the user’s hand, if the user chooses to catch it; otherwise, it will settle at the user’s feet.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.6: Allows caster to enchant a weapon with an improved range. Any melee weapon that cannot normally be thrown will be given a thrown range increment of 10'. A normally thrown weapon will have its range increment increased by 5'. A missile weapon will have its range increment increased by 10'. A siege weapon will have its range increment increased by 50'.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.7: Allows caster to enchant a weapon so that whenever it delivers a critical, it will also deliver a second critical of two degrees of severity less than the primary critical (e.g., if the weapon does a C critical, it will also do an A critical of the additional type). The type of extra critical delivered is determined at the time of enchantment.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.8: As Weapon I, except the bonus is +10.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.9: As Returning Weapon, except that the weapon returns instantly via a teleport effect (one mile range limit).
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.10: Allows caster to enchant a weapon that can be used to cause most objects other than armor, weapons, and shields to make a breakage check or be smashed, cut through, or whatever effect is most appropriate for the weapon. Any weapon bonuses are applied as a penalty to this breakage check. One item may be “cleaved” each round.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.11: Allows caster to enchant a weapon with an improved range. Any melee weapon that cannot normally be thrown will be given a thrown range increment of 15'. A normally thrown weapon will have its range increment increased by 10'. A missile weapon will have its range increment increased by 25. A siege weapon will have its range increment increased by 100'.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.12: Allows caster to enchant a weapon such that every round it is used in combat against an opponent using a shield, that shield must make a breakage check.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.13: As Weapon I, except the bonus is +15.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.14: Allows caster to enchant a weapon so that whenever it delivers a critical, it will also deliver a second critical of one degree of severity less than the primary critical (e.g., if the weapon does a B critical, it will also do an A critical of the additional type). The type of extra critical delivered is determined at the time of enchantment.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.15: Allows caster to enchant a weapon that has a Slaying I effect (adds +5 to all criticals) when used against one kind of target. See notes for more or less restrictive options.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.16: Allows caster to enchant a weapon with a Vampiric Effect (see above).
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.17: Allows caster to enchant a weapon with an improved range. Any melee weapon that cannot normally be thrown will be given a thrown range increment of 20'. A normally thrown weapon will have its range increment increased by 15'. A missile weapon will have its range increment increased by 50'. A siege weapon will have its range increment increased by 200'.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.18: Allows caster to enchant a weapon such that every time it delivers a critical to an armored area, the armor must make a breakage check. If the critical already indicates possible breakage, roll both checks.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.19: Allows caster to enchant a weapon so that whenever it delivers a critical, it will also deliver a second critical of the same degree of severity as the primary critical (e.g., if the weapon does an A critical, it will also do an A critical of the additional type). The type of extra critical delivered is determined at the time of enchantment. af: 1
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.20: Allows caster to enchant a weapon that has a Slaying II effect (adds +10 to all criticals) when used against one kind of target.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.25: As Weapon I, except the bonus is +20.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.30: Allows caster to enchant a weapon which attacks as if it were one Size larger than actual. (E.g., a human-sized longsword could be enchanted to attack as a Big creature’s longsword, doing Large rather than Big attacks.)
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.35: Allows caster to enchant a melee weapon such that when the weapon is used in combat against an armed foe, the foe’s weapon(s) must make a breakage check each round.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.40: Allows caster to enchant a weapon that has a Slaying III effect (adds +15 to all criticals) when used against one kind of target.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.50: As Weapon I, except the bonus is +25.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.60: Allows caster to enchant a weapon that has a Slaying IV effect (adds +20 to all criticals) when used against one kind of target.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.75: As Weapon I, except the bonus is +30.
WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.90: Allows caster to enchant a weapon which attacks as if it were two Sizes larger than actual. (E.g., a human-sized longsword could be enchanted to attack as a Large creature’s longsword, doing Huge rather than Big attacks).

DISENCHANTMENTS.1: All magical abilities of target item cease to function while the caster concentrates. This does not remove the basic benefits of a magical item (e.g., it still gets an RR if targeted by a spell that allows for one).
DISENCHANTMENTS.2: One magical ability of target item ceases to function for the duration of this spell. The ability is determined at random unless the caster makes a Very Hard Spell Mastery maneuver in order to select which ability is negated.
DISENCHANTMENTS.3: All items on the target lose their magical abilities as in Item Negation I while caster Concentrates.
DISENCHANTMENTS.4: One charge from a charged or empowered item is expended, as if it had been used. A charged item cannot be reduced below zero charges; an empowered item may have its uses reduced to none for the current time span of its operations (e.g., an item that casts a spell three times daily may have the three uses for the current day dispersed, while an item that casts a spell once a week could have the current weekly use dispersed).
DISENCHANTMENTS.5: All items within the area of effect have their magical abilities negated as in Item Negation I.
DISENCHANTMENTS.6: As Item Negation I, except for a duration of 1 minute per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.7: As Capability Negation I, except the duration is one hour per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.8: As Charge Dispersion I, except three charges are dispersed.
DISENCHANTMENTS.9: All items on the target lose their magical abilities as in Item Negation I for 1 minute/level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.10: Target loses all of his attunements to items, whether those items are present or not. (He may attempt to reattune to a given item without having to develop his Attunement skill, but if he fails, he cannot try again until he has developed another rank of Attunement skill, as normal.)
DISENCHANTMENTS.11: As Item Negation I, except for a duration of 1 hour per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.12: As Capability Negation I, except the duration is one day per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.13: As Charge Dispersion I, except five charges are dispersed.
DISENCHANTMENTS.14: All items within the area of effect have their magical abilities negated as in Item Negation I, for 1 minute per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.15: All items on the target lose their magical abilities as in Item Negation I for 1 hour/level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.16: As Item Negation I, except for a duration of 1 day per level.
