DISENCHANTMENTS.17: This spell may be cast on the caster or on another animate or inanimate target. The target is then surrounded by a 10' radius within which any magical item must make an RR with a -25 penalty or cease to function magically while within the radius. This includes the target’s own items.
DISENCHANTMENTS.18: As Charge Dispersion I, except ten charges are dispersed.
DISENCHANTMENTS.19: All items within the area of effect have their magical abilities negated as in Item Negation I, for 1 hour per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.20: All items on the target lose their magical abilities as in Item Negation I for 1 day/level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.25: As Null Area I, except for duration and that the radius of effect is 20'.
DISENCHANTMENTS.30: As Charge Dispersion I, except a number of charges up to the caster’s level are dispersed.
DISENCHANTMENTS.35: An item with an entity bound into it (using the Demonic Binding, Elemental Binding, or Spirit Binding lists) has that entity freed from the item. The item loses all abilities based on the entity. The entity’s fate and reactions will depend upon its type. A sense of gratitude for its release is far from guaranteed.
DISENCHANTMENTS.40: All items within the area of effect have their magical abilities negated as in Item Negation I, for 1 day per level.
DISENCHANTMENTS.50: One power is permanently removed from the target item. The caster may make an Extremely Hard Spell Mastery maneuver in order to choose a known power to remove. Otherwise the power lost is determined at random. If this spell is cast upon an item with the doubled Unbreakable Work capability, it will not harm the item, but will reveal the method by which it might be destroyed (if the target fails its RR).
DISENCHANTMENTS.60: As Null Area I, except for duration and that the radius of effect is 30'.
DISENCHANTMENTS.75: As Limited Disenchantment, except removes all magical properties from the target item. The item is no longer magical, but retains any non-magical bonuses.
DISENCHANTMENTS.90: As Disenchantment, except affects all items on the target (each item makes a separate RR).

PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.1: Allows caster to enchant an item so as to link it to himself. He will then always be considered to be attuned to the item, although this does not prevent another from attuning to the item. This spell is required for any of the other enchantments on this list.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.2: Allows caster to create an item such that it can be summoned from up to 10' per level away (use higher of item or caller level) by himself or another attuned user. Item will fly to its summoner at 100'/round. If two attempt to summon it at the same time, it will go to whichever is higher level (or its creator if levels are equal).
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.3: Allows caster to create an item such that it will automatically attune itself and attach itself immovably when placed on a potential user correctly (e.g., a ring would be worn on a finger or a glass eye placed in an empty socket). This grants a +20 bonus to SCRs made using powers from the item, as well as joining the auras of item and wielder so completely that the wielder may use the item’s level for RRs if the item’s level is the higher one.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.4: Allows caster to enchant an item so that the bearer has a -10 to RRs against the caster’s spells or other abilities. This does not take effect until the bearer attunes to the item or uses it in some way (e.g., if the item is a weapon, using it in combat would activate this effect). This will be a hidden ability.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.5: Allows caster to enchant an item so as to render any of its magical effects non-effective when employed against himself. This generally can apply only to direct effects of the item’s powers, not any secondary effects from the item’s activity on other things. So, the caster could not be hurt by a Fire Ball from the item, but if he were standing next to a tank of gasoline which the Fire Ball caused to explode, he could be hurt by the secondary explosion. Likewise, the caster could not be influenced by a mind-control power of the item, but someone else could be made to attack him.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.6: As Item Calling I, except item will teleport when called from up to 100'/level away.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.7: Allows caster to create an item such that the caster can, by concentrating, sense things as if he were at the item’s location, so long as the item is borne by an attuned user. This is a hidden ability. Range is 10 miles per level of the item. Alternatively, the caster may enchant a pair of items as an unusual set, with one of the items allowing remotely spying on the location of the other as described above. In this case, the ability is hidden only in the item that will be the location sensed.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.8: As Vulnerability I, but the penalty is -20.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.9: Allows caster to enchant a pair of identical items such that what is done to one is done to the other as well. This does mean that there is twice the risk of breakage, but allows for remotely playing an instrument or writing on a chalk board or similar methods. This allows communication over unlimited distances, for there is no range restriction on this link.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.10: Allows caster to enchant an item such that so long as it endures, the caster will age at but one-tenth the normal rate. If another becomes attuned to the item, that person will age at one-fifth the normal rate.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.11: Allows caster to enchant an item such that the caster need not wear/wield the item in order to use its spell abilities. The range at which these abilities are available is 500' per level of the item.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.12: As Item Calling I, except item will teleport when called from up to 1 mile/level away.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.13: As Vulnerability I, but the penalty is -30.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.14: Allows caster to enchant an item such that he can influence another individual attuned to the item. If that individual is in the service of the caster, then his morale/loyalty receives a +50 bonus. Otherwise, the individual will have to make an RR against a 5th level mental influence (treat as a Fear RR) in order to act contrary to the caster’s interests. This will be a hidden ability.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.15: Allows caster to enchant an item so as to place some of his own levels within. The item then grants those levels, plus an additional level for every two levels so transferred, to its wielder. Thus, a caster of 20th level who placed six of his levels into such an item would become 14th level for all purposes, including RRs and the casting levels of his spells, but the item would grant nine levels to its wielder, so if the caster kept the item, he would be treated as (14 + 9) 23rd level. If the item is lost or destroyed, the levels are gone forever.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.16: Allows caster to enchant an item such that the wielder’s hits are multiplied by x1.5. This multiplication is done after applying all other modifiers. Thus, someone who normally would have 100 hits would have 150 instead.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.17: Allows caster to create a set of items such that some or all of the items, which must be ranged attack items (e.g., arrows or a wand of Shock Bolts) gain a homing ability towards the other items (which need not be ranged attack items) when they are active. This homing ability must be chosen at creation time and might be complete lack of range penalties or the ability of the attack to make corners like a Magician’s “Following” bolt spells or a straight +25 OB bonus. A target item might be always active or it might be triggered, as with a set of arrows where the first to hit will lead further arrows to the same target.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.18: As Vulnerability I, but the penalty is -40.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.19: Allows caster to enchant an item such that he can always cast a mental spell (one of subtype ‘m’) on the individual bearing the item regardless of range (at no range penalty if the individual is attuned to the item; at -30 if he is not). This will be a hidden ability. The caster may also enchant a pair of items as an unusual set, allowing one of the items to allow remotely casting mental spells on the location of the other as described above. In this case, the ability is hidden only in the “receiver” item.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.20: As Aura Augmentation I, except that the levels transferred to the item are doubled (e.g., transferring six caster levels would provide twelve levels from the item).
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.25: As Vulnerability I, but the penalty is -50.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.30: Allows caster to enchant an item such that so long as he retains possession of it, he will not age. If another gains possession of the item, the caster will age at one-hundredth the normal rate. Anyone other than the caster attuned to the item will age at one-twentieth the normal rate.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.35: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it possesses a limited copy of his own will and intelligence. It has psychic stat bonuses based on those of the caster, but with the bonus reduced by 1d10 for each stat, as well as his ethics, purposes, and much of his personality (unless spell failure dictates otherwise). It will possess half the ranks of its creator’s Lore and Science skills. The item will have touch telepathy.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.40: As Vulnerability I, but the penalty is -70.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.50: As Aura Augmentation I, except that the levels transferred to the item are tripled (e.g., transferring six caster levels would provide eighteen levels from the item).
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.60: As Vulnerability I, but the penalty is -100.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.75: Allows caster to enchant an item such that it possesses a copy of his own will and intelligence. It has the same psychic stat bonuses as the caster, as well as his ethics, purposes, and much of his personality (unless spell failure dictates otherwise). It will possess all of its creator’s Lore and Science skills. The item will have ranged telepathy.
PERSONAL EMPOWERMENT.90: Allows caster to enchant an item such that if the caster is killed, but the item survives, the caster’s spirit will restore itself in a new body, identical to the current one, in 1-100 years. This body will appear within 1-100 miles of the site where the caster died. The caster’s soul must not have been destroyed or captured, though his tie to the item will grant a +50 RR bonus against such effects.

DIVINE TOUCH.1: Caster learns origin, history, and powers of one item, insofar as these relate directly to the central concerns of caster’s power source (e.g., a Sanctifier of a sea god would learn about time an item spent on a ship or under the sea, but not the history of the item in the mountains; he would learn that the item gives a bonus to Survival: Ocean or that it Slays Mermaids, but would not learn the item’s OB or that it casts a Fire Bolt once per day).
DIVINE TOUCH.2: Allows caster to enchant an item which allows the bearer to speak and understand in spoken form the “holy language” of his faith as if the bearer had 5 ranks in the language. This will grant an intelligent item the power of speech (including use of all its existing language skills).
DIVINE TOUCH.3: Allows caster to enchant a weapon closely associated with his faith with a +5 bonus to the weapon’s OB. Ranged weapons which launch missiles (e.g., bows, crossbows) receive a +10' bonus to their range increment instead.
DIVINE TOUCH.4: Allows caster to enchant an item associated with his faith such that it grants a +5 bonus to one skill specialization, or one skill that cannot be specialized, which is associated with his faith. Alternatively, the item may grant a bonus of +2 to the number of ranks for purposes using the number of ranks rather than the skill bonus.
DIVINE TOUCH.5: Allows caster to embed a spell of up to second level, which must be closely associated with his faith, into an item associated with his faith. The spell may then be used once per day (as if an appropriate Embed and Daily spell had been used to enchant the item).
DIVINE TOUCH.6: Allows caster to enchant an item which allows the bearer to read and write the “holy language” of his faith as if the bearer had 5 ranks in the language.
DIVINE TOUCH.7: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +10 or a +20' range increment.
DIVINE TOUCH.8: As Sacred Skill I, except a +10 bonus or +4 ranks for purposes using the number of ranks.
DIVINE TOUCH.9: Allows caster to enchant an item associated with his faith so that it provides a +10 bonus to either RRs or DB against some hazard which his deity opposes or rules. It may also act to counter some penalty which the deity opposes or rules (e.g., a god of night could negate a penalty for darkness).
DIVINE TOUCH.10: As Sacred Spell II, except a spell up to fourth level.
DIVINE TOUCH.11: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +15 or a +30' range increment.
DIVINE TOUCH.12: As Sacred Skill I, except a +15 bonus or +6 ranks for purposes using the number of ranks.
DIVINE TOUCH.13: Allows caster to enchant an item which allows the bearer to speak, write, sign, and understand (i.e., to have two-way communication in all forms of the language) the “holy language” of his faith as if the bearer had 10 ranks in the language. This will grant an intelligent item the power of speech (including use of all its existing language skills), as well as whatever writing capabilities it can muster.
DIVINE TOUCH.14: As Sacred Protections II, except a bonus of +20.
DIVINE TOUCH.15: As Sacred Spell II, except a spell up to sixth level.
DIVINE TOUCH.16: Allows caster to enchant an item associated with his faith so that it allows its bearer to summon a specific kind of creature associated with his faith. These will appear the round after the summons is made and will provide such aid as they are able, within a span of up to eight hours if not required to fight (or an hour of battle). The total levels that may be summoned are equal to the number of days spent on this power (i.e., a minimum of 16, but the caster may increase the number of days to increase the levels summoned). If any of the summoned creatures dies, the ability to summon is reduced for a period of one year (i.e., it takes a year to replace any killed creature).
DIVINE TOUCH.17: As Sacred Protections II, except a bonus of +25.
DIVINE TOUCH.18: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +20 or a +40' range increment.
DIVINE TOUCH.19: As Sacred Skill I, except a +20 bonus or +8 ranks for purposes using the number of ranks.
DIVINE TOUCH.20: As Sacred Spell II, except a spell up to tenth level.
DIVINE TOUCH.25: As Sacred Skill I, except a +25 bonus or +10 ranks for purposes using the number of ranks.
DIVINE TOUCH.30: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +25 or a +50' range increment.
DIVINE TOUCH.35: As Sacred Skill I, except a +30 bonus or +12 ranks for purposes using the number of ranks.
DIVINE TOUCH.40: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +30 or a +60' range increment.
DIVINE TOUCH.50: As Sacred Skill I, except a +35 bonus or +14 ranks for purposes using the number of ranks.
DIVINE TOUCH.60: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +35 or a +70' range increment.
DIVINE TOUCH.75: As Sacred Spell II, except a spell of any level.
DIVINE TOUCH.90: As Sacred Weapon I, except the bonus is +40 or a +80' range increment.

MAGICAL WEAVES.1: Allows caster to enchant a cloth item that will change its appearance (color, pattern, texture) as desired by the (attuned) wearer.
MAGICAL WEAVES.2: Allows caster to enchant a piece of weaving up to 2' by 3' in size.
MAGICAL WEAVES.3: Allows caster to enchant a carpet (requires Work Weave) that can fly at a rate of up to 50' per round. Controller of the carpet must be on the carpet and attuned to it. Piloting the carpet may be done for up to four hours at a time. For every five minutes beyond that, an Endurance roll is required. After four hours of doing something else, piloting may be resumed without penalty. The carpet can support up to 100 pounds per square foot of carpet (seating space can also be a limiting factor).
MAGICAL WEAVES.4: Allows caster to enchant regular cloth or cloth armor to be more protective (requires Work Weave). This will allow regular cloth to offer the protection of AT 2 or cloth armor to provide AT 3.
MAGICAL WEAVES.5: Allows caster to enchant a tapestry (requires Work Weave) so that it will portray the current state of the place depicted. Note that this is done with animated stitching and always appears as a tapestry; it is not a photorealistic depiction. Discernable detail depends on the size of the tapestry and area depicted. The range at which the tapestry can update itself is 1 mile per square foot of tapestry. If taken beyond this range, it will portray the area as it was the moment the tapestry moved out of range. If brought back within range, it will resume depicting the current situation.
MAGICAL WEAVES.6: Allows caster to enchant a piece of weaving up to 3' by 5' in size.
MAGICAL WEAVES.7: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 100' per round.
MAGICAL WEAVES.8: As Armoring Cloth I, except regular cloth will provide AT 3, cloth armor AT 4.
MAGICAL WEAVES.9: Allows caster to enchant a carpet also enchanted with a Flying Carpet spell to be summoned. One attuned to the carpet can then concentrate and the carpet will come to him at full speed. If it is physically barred, it will circle, looking for an opening, but it cannot apply intelligence to this search based on this enchantment. Range of this summons is 200' per level of the carpet.
MAGICAL WEAVES.10: Allows caster to enhance a Visionary Tapestry with sound. Any sounds produced beyond the area portrayed will not be heard, even if they would be quite loud from any of the points pictured.
MAGICAL WEAVES.11: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 150' per round.
MAGICAL WEAVES.12: Allows caster to enchant a piece of weaving up to 4' by 6' in size.
MAGICAL WEAVES.13: As Armoring Cloth I, except regular cloth will provide AT 4, cloth armor AT 5.
MAGICAL WEAVES.14: Allows caster to enhance a Visionary Tapestry with the ability to show anything from the history it has portrayed, at the command of someone attuned to it. In order to search for events whose time is only vaguely known, the depiction can be sped up to as much as 20 times actual time (so that an hour’s events would fly through in but three minutes).
MAGICAL WEAVES.15: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 200' per round.
MAGICAL WEAVES.16: Allows caster to enchant a rope, carpet, rug, or curtain such that at a range of up to 5' per level of the item, an attuned user may mentally command the item (as an instantaneous action) to seize the nearest target. A rope can attack as a Medium Grapple, a carpet as a Big Grapple. OB is determined by item level, treated as ranks in attack, so a 16th level item would have a +68 OB. Treat escape from any successful grapple as a Very Hard maneuver.
MAGICAL WEAVES.17: Allows caster to enchant a piece of weaving up to 5' by 7' in size.
MAGICAL WEAVES.18: As Armoring Cloth I, except regular cloth will provide AT 5, cloth armor AT 7.
MAGICAL WEAVES.19: Allows caster to enchant a carpet or rug (requires Work Weave) such that any attempt to cross it is a Nigh Impossible maneuver (usually Running) unless one is attuned to it; add any penalties for pace modifiers as well. Footing is extremely slippery and the carpet may seem to move under one’s feet.
MAGICAL WEAVES.20: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 300' per round.
MAGICAL WEAVES.25: Allows caster to enchant a piece of weaving up to 6' by 8' in size.
MAGICAL WEAVES.30: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 400' per round.
MAGICAL WEAVES.35: Allows caster to enhance a Visionary Tapestry so that an attuned user may change the location portrayed. It can only be moved at a rate of 50' per round, starting from the current portrayed location or, if the previous view is now out of the tapestry’s range, from the location of the tapestry itself.
MAGICAL WEAVES.40: Allows caster to enchant a piece of weaving up to 6' by 10' in size.
MAGICAL WEAVES.50: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 600' per round.
MAGICAL WEAVES.60: As Armoring Cloth I, except regular cloth will provide AT 7, cloth armor AT 8.
MAGICAL WEAVES.75: Allows caster to enhance a Visionary Tapestry to look into other worlds. This is effective only with respect to worlds that have “parallel locations” with the plane containing the tapestry. Thus the utility of this power depends on the cosmology of the game setting. The view will be in the same place (relatively speakng) regardless of which plane is observed.
MAGICAL WEAVES.90: As Flying Carpet I, but carpet’s maximum speed is 1000' per round.

GOLEM MAKING.1: Each round, the caster may learn one of the following about a single golem: level, composition material, one talent, one flaw, one spell list, one skill bonus. Skill bonuses are learned from largest on down to (eventually) smallest, talents and flaws from most DP involved to least (ignoring negative nature of flaw “cost”), and otherwise in random order within the chosen category.
GOLEM MAKING.2: [RR Mod.: -20] Targeted golem loses 1 AP every round (i.e., normally leaving 3 AP).
GOLEM MAKING.3: Caster learns the approximate direction (but not distance) to the targeted golem’s master or command item, if the master or item is close enough to control the golem.
GOLEM MAKING.4: Allows caster to transfer mastery of a golem from himself to someone else. Both the golem and the new master must be within range of this spell.
GOLEM MAKING.5: Allows caster to animate a golem of up to 5th level, made of a non-magical, non-metallic material (e.g., a flesh golem).
GOLEM MAKING.6: As Golem I, except the golem may be of a metallic material.
GOLEM MAKING.7: As Golem I, except the golem may be of any material.
GOLEM MAKING.8: Allows caster to assign an on-going task to a golem under his control. The golem will continue to perform this task so long as it is able and it receives no contrary instruction from its master. This task may involve a single conditional element (e.g., “Destroy anyone who touches this treasure, unless he first speaks the words ‘Mexlar the Magnificent is the greatest golem maker in the world’.”).
GOLEM MAKING.9: As Golem I, except the golem may be up to 10th level (e.g., a tar golem).
GOLEM MAKING.10: As Golem II, except the golem may be of a metallic material.
GOLEM MAKING.11: As Golem II, except the golem may be of any material.
GOLEM MAKING.12: Allows caster to enchant an item, giving its bearer the ability to command a golem that he is creating or commands at the time of this enchantment. This is the only spell required for this enchantment (i.e., no Work or Consecration spell is required), though this ability may be incorporated into an item with other powers.
GOLEM MAKING.13: Allows caster to grow a golem figure in a mold from a “seed” of nonmetallic material.
GOLEM MAKING.14: Allows caster to embed a single skill which the golem can use. The completed golem will have one rank in the skill per level. Note that, unless the golem has been granted intelligence (e.g., by Blessed Thoughts), it will use its skills only in a rote and routine manner. A golem may recite memorized lore, for example, but will not be capable of analytical thinking no matter how many ranks it has in the skill.
GOLEM MAKING.15: As Golem I, except the golem may be up to 15th level (e.g., a clay golem).
GOLEM MAKING.16: As Golem III, except the golem may be of a metallic material.
GOLEM MAKING.17: As Golem III, except the golem may be of any material.
GOLEM MAKING.18: Allows caster to grow a golem figure in a mold from a “seed” of metallic material.
GOLEM MAKING.19: As Golem I, except the golem may be up to 20th level.
GOLEM MAKING.20: As Golem IV, except the golem may be of a metallic material (e.g., a brass or stone golem).
GOLEM MAKING.25: As Golem IV, except the golem may be of any material.
GOLEM MAKING.30: As Embed Skill I, except the golem will have two ranks in the skill per level.
GOLEM MAKING.35: As Golem I, except the golem may be up to 40th level, and may be made of any material (e.g., an iron or eog golem).
GOLEM MAKING.40: Allows caster to make a golem in his command loyal to some group, protecting and accepting commands from all rulers of a certain dynasty or nation, all members of a clergy (or just one position in the church, like the Archbishop of Tweedle), the eldest female in a family, or the like.
GOLEM MAKING.50: Allows caster to program a golem under his control to relentlessly search out and destroy one target type, against which its attacks become Slaying II. This may happen immediately, or it may be kept as a default state in case the golem otherwise goes out of control.
GOLEM MAKING.60: As Golem I, except the golem may be of any level.
GOLEM MAKING.75: As Golem True, except the golem may be of a metallic material.
GOLEM MAKING.90: As Golem True, except the golem may be of any material.

SPIRIT BINDING.1: Each round, the caster may learn one of the following about a single spirit: level, general type (undead, animal, rational, etc.), profession or archetype, one talent, one flaw, one spell list, one skill bonus. Skill bonuses are learned from largest on down to (eventually) smallest, talents and flaws from most DP involved to least (ignoring negative nature of flaw “cost”), and otherwise in random order within the chosen category.
SPIRIT BINDING.2: Allows caster to embed a plant spirit into an object as described in Section 5.3. In many settings, this will have very limited use, but in others plants with useful spirits may be more common and there may be more powerful plant and animal spirits than those residing within living plants and animals.
SPIRIT BINDING.3: Cast once per day, this spell allows the caster to give an intelligent item the power of touch telepathy or the power of speech. Cast twice per day (double time and PP requirement), it can provide the power of ranged telepathy (with a range equal to its level in feet).
SPIRIT BINDING.4: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded spirit’s talents up to a limit of 6 DP value.
SPIRIT BINDING.5: Allows caster to embed an animal spirit into an object as described in Section 5.3.
SPIRIT BINDING.6: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded spirit’s Open spell lists. These spells may be cast using the wielder's PP or the item's PP (e.g., from Manifest Power).
SPIRIT BINDING.7: Allows caster to provide access to three of an embedded spirit’s skills for purposes of the item’s own use or the direct use of the item.
SPIRIT BINDING.8: Allows caster to make an item with an embedded spirit such that the item will allow communication with the embedded spirit’s kindred. Even if such are non-speaking creatures, the wielder will be able to communicate as effectively as with speech. All interactions with such kindred creatures are at +20, with relevant Lore maneuvers gaining a +15 bonus, and relevant Science maneuvers gaining +10.
SPIRIT BINDING.9: Allows caster to provide access to an embedded spirit’s normal PP total, for use in casting spells from its lists.
SPIRIT BINDING.10: Allows caster to embed the spirit of someone belonging to a species classified as a “Race” into an object as described in Section 5.3.
SPIRIT BINDING.11: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded spirit’s Closed spell lists. These spells may be cast using the wielder's PP or the item's PP (e.g., from Manifest Power).
SPIRIT BINDING.12: As Manifest Talent I, but limit is 20 DP.
SPIRIT BINDING.13: Allows caster to enchant an item with an embedded spirit such that the spirit within can be mentally “handed” one of the wielder’s spells, allowing the item spirit to maintain and adjust a spell requiring concentration for the wielder.
SPIRIT BINDING.14: Allows caster to make one of an embedded spirit’s stat bonuses available to the wielder or to make one of the embedded spirit’s physical stat bonuses (Ag, Co, Qu, St) available for the item’s use.
SPIRIT BINDING.15: Allows caster to embed the spirit of any living creature that is not classified as a plant, animal, or race into an object as described in Section 5.3.
SPIRIT BINDING.16: Allows caster to provide access to three of an embedded spirit’s skills for all purposes.
SPIRIT BINDING.17: Allows caster to provide access to one of an embedded spirit’s spell lists which is neither an Open nor a Closed list (e.g., a Base or Evil list). These spells may be cast using the wielder's PP or the item's PP (e.g., from Manifest Power).
SPIRIT BINDING.18: As Manifest Talent I, but limit is 40 DP.
SPIRIT BINDING.19: Allows caster to enchant a gemstone (must be at least 10 carats) so that it can hold a spirit within for later embedding. This allows for the capture of spirits in the field, with a suitable permanent housing to be found later. The gem need merely be touched to a willing individual, and the individual’s spirit is transferred into the gem. It can later be removed by binding it into an item, if Lifegiving is applied to its original body, or if the gem is destroyed (in which case the spirit goes wherever such houseless spirits go).
SPIRIT BINDING.20: Allows caster to embed an undead spirit into an object as described in Section 5.3.
SPIRIT BINDING.25: Allows caster to provide access to general traits of an embedded demon, such as its level for purposes of the bearer’s RRs, a full set of senses (without talents) in item form, etc.
SPIRIT BINDING.30: As Manifest Talent I, but limit is 75 DP.
SPIRIT BINDING.35: Allows caster to embed any spirit that does not fall into the previously listed categories into an object as described in Section 5.3.
SPIRIT BINDING.40: Allows caster to enchant an item with an embedded spirit such that the wielder may choose to take on the mental or physical appearance (or both) of the spirit. Transformation is at will and takes 1 AP. Physical change gives the wielder the form of the spirit’s previous existance (but no powers not otherwise granted). Mental change makes the wielder and the item detect as a single mind with the characteristics of the spirit.
SPIRIT BINDING.50: Allows caster to enchant an item with an embedded spirit such that RRs against the wielder’s spells that summon, control, influence, or deceive have an RR penalty when the target is of the same kind as the embedded spirit. The penalty is equal to the embedded spirit’s level if the target belongs to the same Category as the spirit. The penalty is twice the embedded spirit’s level if the target is of the same Type, and it is triple the embedded spirit’s level if the target is of the same Variety. See Creature Law for details regarding creature Category, Type, and Variety.
SPIRIT BINDING.60: As Manifest Talent I, but there is no limit on the talent’s DP cost.
SPIRIT BINDING.75: Allows caster to enchant an item with an embedded spirit such that the wielder may journey incorporeally, as described in the spell Conveyance on the Delving Ways list, except that there is no time limit (though the body is still left vulnerable). This requires no spellcasting or SCR, just a round of relaxation and the decision to depart the body. The wielder may also journey to any suitable spirit realms, dream lands, etc. that exist in the setting and with which the embedded spirit would have some connection.
SPIRIT BINDING.90: Allows caster to create an item that can draw in and imprison unwilling spirits. The item may be used by a wielder or created with a trigger (such as looking into a mirror). Any creature with a spirit must make an RR against the effect or be drawn into the item (leaving behind the body, if applicable). An attuned user can communicate with trapped spirits and may release them at will. Each item will have a limited number of spaces available for trapped spirits (roll 2-20 randomly upon item creation) and any new spirits trapped beyond that limit result in the release of a previously trapped spirit on a first in, first out basis. Note that unless it has a body to return to somewhere, a released spirit is just another dead soul and will go where such souls go. Those which were already bodiless spirits (including undead) when trapped will return to their previous condition.

MECHANICAL MASTERY.1: Caster learns the general purpose of a target machine, as well as the approximate time and place of manufacture, the skills (and spell lists, if any) that were needed to make it, and its readiness (or lack thereof) for operation. The caster gains a +10 bonus for any subsequent maneuvers working with or on this machine.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.2: Allows caster to include a mechanical device in the body of a construct, which the construct is then able to use.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.3: Allows caster to enchant an item with Dim Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.4: Allows caster to enchant an intelligent item such that it can communicate by touch telepathy. If the time and PP spent are doubled to 8, the item may have the power of speech instead. If tripled (12), the item may communicate through ranged telepathy.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.5: Allows caster to enchant a construct, golem, or intelligent item such that it possesses an additional sense, one of the senses it has is extended in some way (e.g., extend sight into infrared), or in the case of a construct or item with a suitable location (e.g., a sword with an eye in the pommel) to make one sense record what it senses for later playback (requiring a Medium Mechanics: Operation maneuver). Only the last 24 hours will be available for playback.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.6: Allows caster to enchant an item with Low Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.7: Allows caster to instantly repair to full working order one single-purpose mechanical device (e.g., a clock or a dart thrower). While damage may be extensive, no more than 10% of material may be missing, or this spell will fail.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.8: Allows caster to enchant an item possessed of an artificial intelligence to cast spells. This spell may be cast multiple times per day to increase the effect of this enchantment. One spell provides the item with access to the Open lists of a single Realm of magic. Doubling up the spell (requiring 16 days and PP) will add access to the Closed lists of the same Realm. Tripling up the spell (24) will add access to all other lists available to a caster of that Realm (Base, Evil). Adding another casting of this spell each day (and adding another 8 days and PP) can be done to give access to an additional Realm, to create an item with Hybrid spellcasting abilities. This spell also provides the item with both the Power Development skill and the Adept's choice of spell lists up to the item's capacity to learn them (the Adept or an assistant must know the spell lists up to the level to be imparted to the item).
MECHANICAL MASTERY.9: Allows caster to enchant an item with Medium Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.10: Allows caster to enchant a mechanical device so as to cut the time to operate it in half for one specific operation. For example, this is typically used to reduce the time to raise a portcullis or to reduce the time to reset the firing mechanism on a crossbow or siege engine. This ability may be added multiple times (e.g., twice for one-quarter the usual operation time).
MECHANICAL MASTERY.11: Allows caster to increase the learning potential of an item which has artificial intelligence. Either the maximum number of skills which can be learned is increased by one category (i.e., from the limit for a Low Intelligence to the higher limit of Medium Intelligence), or maximum number of ranks in one skill is increased by one category. See Table 5-3i in section 5.3 for details.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.12: Allows caster to enchant a mechanical device such that upon use, it will reset itself into a ready state. This takes the normal amount of time, but the item’s parts move on their own. This allows traps to reset themselves, crossbows and siege engines to wind themselves (though reloading ammunition will still need to be accomplished manually without a mechanical reloading device and ammunition reservoir), and clockwork toys and timepieces to keep themselves wound.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.13: Allows caster to animate a construct, as described in Section 5.4.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.14: Allows caster to enchant a container such that it never runs empty. An initial supply must be in place when the item receives this enchantment. An appropriate Work spell for the contents (e.g., Work Mundane Wood for arrows, Work Poison for a poison reservoir) must be incorporated into the enchantment on the container. By default, this can only be done with mundane items and substances (regular arrows, but not magical arrows).If the GM allows magical reserves to be created, all spells required to enchant the item to be eternally supplied must be cast on the reservoir during each day of enchantment, duplicating any spells already cast for enchanting the reservoir itself (e.g., a wooden ammunition reserve for an automatic crossbow would need Work Mundane Wood twice, once for the wooden case itself, again for the magical bolts that it will generate).
MECHANICAL MASTERY.15: Allows caster to enchant an item with High Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.16: Allows caster to enchant a mechanism such that its operation is tied to a hand-shaped depression. When the hand of an authorized individual is placed in the depression, the mechanism will operate (or not operate, in the case of a trap), while the reverse is otherwise true. Shape-changing can fool this device or a very detailed forgery of a hand, down to body warmth and fingerprints. Any authorized person may authorize another, so long as an Easy attunement maneuver is made by both.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.17: Allows caster to create a large piece of architectural/engineering work with twice the normal strength. A bridge could support twice the normal weight, a fortress wall endure twice the destructive force, etc.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.18: Allows caster to create a clockwork device that will work forever without winding. While especially useful for clocks, various toys and gadgets may be powered in this way as well. Unlike Selfwinding, this ability does not require the item to run down and renew itself, but maintains constant function.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.19: As Hand-Key, except operation is tied to the sound of an authorized person’s voice, which must speak the correct words. This requires both mimicking an authorized voice and discovering the correct phrase to defeat.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.20: Allows caster to enchant an item with Superior Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.25: As Mend Mechanism, except it may apply to a complex machine with many working parts. For each ton of machinery, it requires one hour for repairs to become complete.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.30: Allows caster to enchant a vehicle so that it will operate itself. This might be a carriage that rolls along without a horse, a siege tower that advances on its own, a sailing ship that performs its functions without a crew, etc. This can substitute for up to fifty men or a dozen horses. This ability can be added multiple times if needed to replace a larger work force. The vehicle cannot direct itself and will require a pilot.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.35: Allows caster to enchant an item with Genius Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.40: Allows caster to enchant a construct such that it has an extra 2 AP each round. This will make the mechanisms somewhat less stable. Any Impact or Unbalancing critical suffered by the construct will count as Slaying I. This cannot be combined with an embedded intelligence of any kind, as the excessive speed would disorientate the embedded intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.50: Target machine immediately ceases its operations, freezing in its current position. This can be any single mechanism, a system of mechanisms working closely together (as in a series of pistons or the gears running different hands of a clock), or a more complex machine unified through enchantment (as a construct or one of the self-mobile vehicles created with this list). Something like a sailing ship, with many different simple machines working more or less independently, cannot be so shut down except when magically enhanced as a machine.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.60: Allows caster to convert a workshop to one with multiple self-operating tools and other simple devices that will work in accordance with the user’s needs. Where applicable, this constitutes the equivalent of a full set of assistants. In any case, all work will be done in two-thirds the normal time (this does not reduce the time required to enchant an item), with a +30 to all maneuvers. These are cumulative with the benefits of a Work spell.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.75: Allows caster to enchant an item with Transcendent Intelligence.
MECHANICAL MASTERY.90: As Automated Vehicle, except that the vehicle can steer itself. This requires that the course be set, which will require both a Navigation or Region Lore maneuver and a Mechanics: Operation maneuver. Difficulty for Navigation/ Region Lore should be the same as conventional travel, while the Mechanics maneuver starts at Very Hard and complex tasks, such as navigating a winding mountain road, will increase the difficulty.

CREATURE CULTIVATION.1: Caster learns the general origin, age, and level of a target creature. If the creature is of an artificial nature, the caster will also learn what spells were used to create the creature.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.2: Provides caster with the necessary information to later make a clone of the target.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.3: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 1st level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.4: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 2nd level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.5: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature that will be “loyal” to its creator. At a minimum, this will keep the most psychotic cultivated creatures from attacking their creator. Less mindlessly aggressive creatures will be actively friendly.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.6: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature which is a crude clone of the original template. This clone will pass as the original only from a distance or seen at a glance. Features are not fully formed or are slightly malformed.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.7: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 4th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.8: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 5th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.9: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 6th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.10: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 7th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.11: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature which is a clone of the original template. This clone will pass as the original based on visual inspection. It will also have the same voice as the original, but it will lack the mannerisms of the original and cannot pass as the original under observation by someone who knows the original, as it will not move, speak, or react in the same ways.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.12: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature that will be “loyal” and “obedient” to its creator. This allows even the most dimwitted of creatures to understand the creator’s commands, although it will not allow the creature to perform complex tasks beyond its normal intellectual grasp. The duration of obedience will vary greatly depending on the creature type. A Vile will need to be told not to attack someone every round it is in that individual’s presence. A Battlepede will continue following a command forever.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.13: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 10th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.14: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 11th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.15: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 12th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.16: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 13th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.17: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 14th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.18: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 15th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.19: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 16th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.20: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature which is a clone of the original template. This clone will have not only the appearance, but the mannerisms of the original. It does not have the knowledge or skills of the original and may be caught out due to a lack of appropriate knowledge, but it otherwise replicates the original.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.25: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 20th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.30: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 25th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.35: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 30th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.40: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 35th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.50: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature which is a clone of the original template. This clone will have the appearance, mannerisms, and knowledge of the original. Note that knowledge will only be up to date for the most recent Clone Template available to the creator at the time of its completion. The clone has access to all of the template’s skills and abilities (depending on setting, Channeling spell abilities may be excluded).
CREATURE CULTIVATION.60: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of up to 50th level.
CREATURE CULTIVATION.75: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature which is a true clone of the original template. This clone will have the appearance, mannerisms, knowledge, and personality of the original. It is essentially a perfect copy (as of the most recent Clone Template), although it can be made to have the current template mind duplicated in a younger version of the template body and injuries in the original can be removed (e.g., the original’s eye lost in a stick-sharpening accident is whole in the clone).
CREATURE CULTIVATION.90: Allows caster to grow a cultivated creature of any level.

SACRED LAND.1: Caster learns if a given location is sacred ground and, if so, to which religion it is dedicated. Caster also learns if the area is enchanted in any other way, whether the magic is “natural” or the work of spellcasting, and the general nature and purpose of the enchantment. Caster also learns if the area is suitable for dedication to his own religion and any specific problems barring such use.
SACRED LAND.2: Allows caster to provide the natural aspects of a consecrated area with a general feel and cosmetic enhancements suitable to the deity to which it is dedicated. Generally dewdrops sparkle, flowers bloom unusually large and bright, streams babble musically, etc., though this may vary based on the religion in question. The sacred pool of the death god would be bare and still. The place will evoke awe or dread or whatever feeling is most appropriate (the grove of a god of peace might evoke calm, that of a goddess of love might stir passions, etc.).
SACRED LAND.3: Allows caster to enchant a small area so as to make it sacred ground. This must be an outdoor area or natural feature dedicated to a religious purpose. This could be a standing stone, a natural spring, a tree, a small cave, etc.
SACRED LAND.4: Allows caster to enchant an immobile living thing (usually a tree) on sacred ground such that it can contain a Symbol. This counts as an enchantment of the sacred site. The Symbol spell must be cast by a member of the faith to which the site is dedicated. The living thing must be at least twenty years old and weigh at least fifty pounds.
SACRED LAND.5: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that the growth of desired species is promoted and suitable animals are drawn to the area. Harvests from this area will be 50% greater than normal.
SACRED LAND.6: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground where anyone not of the faith to which the area is dedicated will have difficulty being stealthy. Leaves will crackle, floors creak, twigs snap, birds be disturbed, etc. leading to a -50 penalty to all such Stalking attempts.
SACRED LAND.7: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that it promotes the flow of magical energies to and from members of the faith to which it is dedicated. All such individuals within the site gain a +25 bonus to all Channeling maneuvers. Enemies of the faith are hindered, suffering a -25 penalty to any Channeling maneuvers. (This does not affect Channeling spellcasting, just use of the Channeling skill.)
SACRED LAND.8: Allows caster to enchant a medium- sized area so as to make it sacred ground. This must be an outdoor area or natural feature dedicated to a religious purpose. This could be a stone circle, a pond, a grove, a large cave, etc.
SACRED LAND.9: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that members of the faith to which the site is dedicated will recover from injury or fatigue at three times the normal rate, while others not hostile to the faith will recover at twice the normal rate.
SACRED LAND.10: Allows caster to undo the enchantments which render an outdoor area or natural feature sacred ground. This requires daily castings for as many days as this spell’s level (10) plus the level of the area to be affected. This process must be completed before any sacred ground may be rededicated as sacred ground to another faith. If a place is “naturally” sacred rather than being made so by the work of a Sanctifier, then double the level of the area when determining the time required.
SACRED LAND.11: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that Channeling spells cast by those dedicated to the deity to which the area is sacred have a +5 bonus to their SCRs and a -10 modification to any spell failure roll resulting from the failure of such a spell. Hybrid casters that channel the power of the same deity may apply this bonus to their base list spells, but not to their spells from their non-Channeling realm.
SACRED LAND.12: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that it is conducive to ritual magic conducted by members of the faith to which it is dedicated. If all participants in a magical ritual are members of the faith, then the site is considered to be an auspicious location worth at least a +5 bonus (any superior bonus the site would normally give is used instead when such applies to the given ritual).
SACRED LAND.13: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that the need for sleep is reduced by 25% for all those not hostile to the faith to which it is dedicated (i.e., 3 hours of sleep count as 4). Channelers of the faith who make the area their permanent residence will only need 50% normal sleep. Those hostile to the faith or under penalty from the god of the faith will need an extra 25% sleep (i.e., 5 hours of sleep count as 4).
SACRED LAND.14: As Blessed Casting I, but the modifiers are +10 to SCRs and -20 to spell failure rolls.
SACRED LAND.15: Allows caster to enchant a large area so as to make it sacred ground. This must be an outdoor area or natural feature dedicated to a religious purpose. This could be a mountain, a lake, a wood, a cavern complex, etc.
SACRED LAND.16: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that any living thing with a multiyear lifespan will age at one-tenth speed while within the area, so long as it has reached maturity.
SACRED LAND.17: As Blessed Casting I, but the modifiers are +15 to SCRs and -30 to spell failure rolls.
SACRED LAND.18: As Lesser Auspicious Location, except that the minimum bonus for rituals is +10.
SACRED LAND.19: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that natural creatures within the area are non-hostile (+50 to all Animal Handling attempts), sleep is nightmare-free and resting (ignore any negative sleeping conditions, including flaws, while here), and accidents are less dangerous, providing a reduction in any critical due to accident by three severities (e.g, D becomes A, C or less is ignored) and providing a +50 bonus to breakage rolls due to accident (not deliberate breakage). Dropped bread will land buttered-side up.
SACRED LAND.20: As Blessed Casting I, but the modifiers are +20 to SCRs and -40 to spell failure rolls.
SACRED LAND.25: As Lesser Auspicious Location, except that the minimum bonus for rituals is +15.
SACRED LAND.30: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that it becomes a suitable growing site for magical herbs. This will not allow the herbs to thrive outside of their normal biome, but it will allow the cultivation of any magical herbs that do grow in the location’s general conditions.
SACRED LAND.35: As Blessed Casting I, but the modifiers are +25 to SCRs and -50 to spell failure rolls.
SACRED LAND.40: As Lesser Auspicious Location, except that the minimum bonus for rituals is +20.
SACRED LAND.50: As Blessed Casting I, but the modifiers are +30 to SCRs and -60 to spell failure rolls.
SACRED LAND.60: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that it has a physical connection to the site’s patron’s home plane or region. On certain holy days (depending on religion, but usually no fewer than four and no more than thirteen days in a year), this connection opens. This spell is named after one prominent manifestation of such a connection, a rainbow bridge up which the faithful may walk up into the “heavenly realm”, but the appearance can vary greatly. It might be a set of steps down into the earth in a pit that opens suddenly, or it might be that a door or waterfall always present allows transportation at the chosen times. Members of the site’s religion may pass through the connection into the divine realm (or some intermediate location chosen for mortals and immortals to mingle), receive such advice, blessing, judgment, or other treatment as the higher powers choose to give, and then return again to the mortal realm. No being from the other side can pass through, nor can any who are not of the site’s religion. In an emergency, it can be used as an escape route to evacuate the sacred site, with transportation back to mortal realm provided by divine power rather than a return through the “rainbow bridge.”
SACRED LAND.75: As Lesser Auspicious Location, except that the minimum bonus for rituals is +25, and only the primary caster need be a member of the faith.
SACRED LAND.90: Allows caster to enchant an area of sacred ground such that an immanent sense of the caster’s god permeates the area. This produces enhanced effects similar to Aura of Sanctity or Splendor, provides a +25 bonus to all divinatory spells cast using the god’s power, and requires anyone attempting to act in opposition to the will of the god to make a Fear RR (against the level of the site).

CRAFTS MASTERY.1: Allows caster to work with non-magical, non-toxic liquids to create an enchanted item (normally a potion). All required tools and material must be present. Alternatively, this spell can be used to work on a non-magical liquid without enchanting it, in which case the caster can do the work in half the normal time. In either case, the caster gains a +30 bonus to his relevant Crafting maneuver(s).
CRAFTS MASTERY.2: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical fabric.
CRAFTS MASTERY.3: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical leather or hide.
CRAFTS MASTERY.4: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical wood.
CRAFTS MASTERY.5: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical non-precious stone.
CRAFTS MASTERY.6: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical, precious metals with a bonus of no better than +0 (e.g., gold).
CRAFTS MASTERY.7: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any non-magical organic materials (e.g., horn or bone).
CRAFTS MASTERY.8: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical, non-precious metals with a bonus of no better than +0 (e.g., iron or inferior bronze).
CRAFTS MASTERY.9: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical precious stone.
CRAFTS MASTERY.10: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +5 (e.g., low steel or superior bronze).
CRAFTS MASTERY.11: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any non-precious stone.
CRAFTS MASTERY.12: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +10 (e.g., high steel).
CRAFTS MASTERY.13: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +5 to create an enchanted item (e.g. zataak).
CRAFTS MASTERY.14: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +15 (e.g., white alloy).
CRAFTS MASTERY.15: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical non-metallic inorganic materials (e.g., glass).
CRAFTS MASTERY.16: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +10 to create an enchanted item.
CRAFTS MASTERY.17: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any fabric (including magical fabrics).
CRAFTS MASTERY.18: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with non-magical metals with a bonus of no better than +20 (e.g., black alloy).
CRAFTS MASTERY.19: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any precious stone.
CRAFTS MASTERY.20: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any organic materials (e.g., dragon scale).
CRAFTS MASTERY.25: Allows caster to use his skill bonus for this list as his skill bonus for any one Crafting skill.
CRAFTS MASTERY.30: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any non-magical metals.
CRAFTS MASTERY.35: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any non-metallic inorganic materials (e.g., laen).
CRAFTS MASTERY.40: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +20 (e.g., starfall or metal of the sun).
CRAFTS MASTERY.50: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +25 (e.g., adamant steel).
CRAFTS MASTERY.60: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any metals with a bonus of no better than +30 (e.g., eog).
CRAFTS MASTERY.75: As Work Mundane Liquid, except allows caster to work with any metals.
CRAFTS MASTERY.90: Allows caster to create an item that is nigh-indestructible. This item will never fail a breakage check and gains a second RR against any spell that would destroy or break it. If this power is given twice, the item will become almost impossible to destroy, requiring some special method be employed, which must be specified at the time of casting.

STANDING CHANNELS.1: Caster learns the location of the Focus for a given Standing Channel if it is within 10' per level of the caster. Caster must be aware of a specific Standing Channel in order to cast this spell.
STANDING CHANNELS.2: An object is prepared to become the Focus for a Standing Channel. This spell must be cast on the item as a regular enchantment prior to creating the Standing Channel. However, no Make or other additional spells must be cast in order to make the item into a Focus.
STANDING CHANNELS.3: Cast on the prepared Focus before the casting of a Standing Channel, this spell allows the Focus to be located up to 10' from the focal point of the Standing Channel.
STANDING CHANNELS.4: Once this spell is cast, the caster has one minute to cast a Standing Channel spell which will have a special -10 RR modifier applied to the spell placed into the Standing Channel. This is cumulative with any RR modifier which that spell normally has.
STANDING CHANNELS.5: When this spell is cast, a 1st level Channeling spell cast by the caster or a cooperating member of the same religion will be made permanent as a Standing Channel as explained above. The spell to be placed into the Standing Channel must be cast within one minute of casting this spell and the caster of that spell must be within 50' of the caster of this spell.
STANDING CHANNELS.6: Once this spell is cast, the caster has one minute to cast a Standing Channel spell which will be capable of having a spell which is not a Channeling spell placed within it (e.g., a Sorcerer Base spell or an Open Mentalism spell could be placed into the exotic Standing Channel).
STANDING CHANNELS.7: Cast on the prepared Focus before the casting of a Standing Channel, this spell allows the Focus to be located up to 50' from the focal point of the Standing Channel.
STANDING CHANNELS.8: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 2nd level.
STANDING CHANNELS.9: As Create Focus, except that it allows caster to enchant a Focus that may be used to turn the Standing Channel on and off. Control may take one of two forms. The Focus may be programmed to make the change according to its condition. For example, the Focus could be a switch that is thrown to change the state of the Standing Channel, or it could be a bucket that must be filled with water in order to turn off the Standing Channel, turning it back on when the water level lowers below a certain point (or the bucket is simply emptied). The other option is to require that the Focus be touched by the individual attuned to it, in which case a thought will suffice for changing the state of the Standing Channel. Difficulty of attunement is Easy for the caster, Medium for other Channelers of his faith, Hard for non-Channelers of his faith, Very Hard for those not of his faith, and Absurd for those hostile to his faith. This spell can even be used to make a Standing Channel that allows a Permanent spell to be turned on and off, such as an Icewall that can be made to appear and disappear by manipulating the Focus.
STANDING CHANNELS.10: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 3rd level.
STANDING CHANNELS.11: Cast on the prepared Focus before the casting of a Standing Channel, this spell allows the Focus to be located up to 100' from the focal point of the Standing Channel.
STANDING CHANNELS.12: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 4th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.13: Allows caster to enchant a Focus such that it will make the Standing Channel harder to dispel by allowing it a second RR against any attempt to dispel it. This requires that Create Focus or Controlling Focus be simultaneously or previously used to enchant the focus, but otherwise requires no additional spells to function.
STANDING CHANNELS.14: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 5th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.15: Cast on the prepared Focus before the casting of a Standing Channel, this spell allows the Focus to be located up to 200' from the focal point of the Standing Channel.
STANDING CHANNELS.16: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 6th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.17: As Augment Channel I, except that the modifier is -20.
STANDING CHANNELS.18: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 7th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.19: Cast on the prepared Focus before the casting of a Standing Channel, this spell allows the Focus to be located up to 300' from the focal point of the Standing Channel.
STANDING CHANNELS.20: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 8th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.25: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 10th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.30: As Hardened Channel I, except two extra RRs are given.
STANDING CHANNELS.35: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 15th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.40: As Augment Channel I, except that the modifier is -30.
STANDING CHANNELS.50: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be up to 20th level.
STANDING CHANNELS.60: As Hardened Channel I, except three extra RRs are given.
STANDING CHANNELS.75: Cast on the prepared Focus before the casting of a Standing Channel, this spell allows the Focus to be located up to 50'/level from the focal point of the Standing Channel.
STANDING CHANNELS.90: As Standing Channel I, except spell may be of any level.

OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.1: Allows caster to create an item with a single embedded ability that allows the user to freely choose among the spells embedded in that ability (e.g., a Daily II ability with two embedded first level spells would allow casting either of the spells twice in a day or both of them once, although two separate Embed I spells would still be required).
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.2: Allows the caster to use the spells on this list to embed Hybrid Base list spells.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.3: Allows caster to embed a 1st level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.4: Allows caster to use an Embed # spell to embed a Channeling or Mentalism spell list up to the level of the Embed spell’s #. Each spell to be included must be cast into the item during the enchantment, but only a single Embed spell suitable for the highest level spell from the list is required. The resulting item will permit lower level spells from the embedded list to be cast at the level of the highest level spell embedded as part of the same embedding.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.5: Allows caster to charge a wand containing one or more Channeling, Mentalism, or Hybrid spells.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.6: Allows caster to embed a 2nd level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.7: Allows caster to give an item the ability to cast a 1st level Channeling or Mentalism spell embedded in the item (using an Embed spell) once per day. Daily spells have considerable flexibility; for details see Daily/Constant Items in Section 5.3.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.8: Allows caster to embed a 3rd level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.9: As Daily I, except a 2nd level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.10: Allows caster to charge a rod containing one or more Channeling, Mentalism, or Hybrid spells.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.11: As Daily I, except a 3rd level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.12: Allows caster to embed a 4th level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.13: As Daily I, except a 4th level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.14: Allows caster to embed a 5th level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.15: Allows caster to charge a staff containing one or more Channeling, Mentalism, or Hybrid spells.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.16: As Daily I, except a 5th level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.17: Allows caster to embed a 7th level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.18: Allows caster to embed a Channeling or Mentalism spell of up to 3rd level (in conjunction with an Embed spell) that functions constantly (or this spell may be cast twice to activate the embedded spell “at will” or when triggered, see item enchantment rules for details).
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.19: Allows caster to charge a half-bole containing one or more Channeling, Mentalism, or Hybrid spells.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.20: Allows caster to embed a 10th level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.25: As Daily I, except a 10th level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.30: Allows caster to charge a bole containing one or more Channeling, Mentalism, or Hybrid spells.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.35: Allows caster to embed a 20th level or lower level Channeling or Mentalism spell in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.40: As Constant III, except a Channeling or Mentalism spell of up to 10th level.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.50: As Daily I, except a 20th level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.60: Allows caster to embed a Channeling or Mentalism spell of any level in an item.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.75: As Daily I, except a 40th level Channeling or Mentalism spell.
OTHER REALM EMBEDDING.90: As Constant III, except a Channeling or Mentalism spell of up to 20th level.

MOOD IMPRESSIONS.1: Reveals any mood on an item or experienced by a being, including the type of mood and its area of influence. This includes natural moods where applicable (individuals are usually not in a particular mood, but may be).
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.2: Allows caster to apply an Infuse Mood spell effect to any entity bound into the item (or any magical intelligence of the item itself), rather than to the bearer of the item.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.3: Allows caster to cause the effect from an Infuse Mood spell to have a lingering effect, such that the mood will continue to affect a target of the effect after that target has left the area of effect for 1 minute per point by which he failed his RR.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.4: Allows caster to modify the effect of an Infuse Mood spell so that the mood is not present all the time. Some trigger is set to bring on the mood and a second trigger may cancel the mood or it may be allowed to time out (1 hour per level of the Infuse Mood spell is the longest a conditional mood may last, although this counts from the last time the trigger occurred, so someone frequently triggering the mood may keep it going indefinitely).
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.5: Allows caster to impress a specific mood into an item, which will then normally apply to anyone bearing the object (although certain spells on this list may alter this). Any attempt to act contrary to the mood will require an RR modified as for Fear (i.e., using SD). If unsuccessful, the individual influenced by the mood will not act contrary to the mood, but in accord with the mood. This RR is made against the level of the Infuse Mood spell, and it is not necessary if circumstances force the action (e.g., someone in a Friendly Mood would have to make an RR to initiate combat, but not to fight if attacked). In any case, actions taken which are in tune with the mood gain a +5 modifier, while any action taken counter to the mood suffers a -5 modifier.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.6: Modifies an Infuse Mood spell so that it affects not only the bearer of the item, but anyone within 10' of the item.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.7: Modifies an Infuse Mood spell so that it affects everyone within 5' of the item, except for the bearer.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.8: Allows the caster to enchant an item such that it has a fear effect that may be triggered once per day. The item will produce a magically-terrifying noise, requiring a Mentalism RR against the item’s level. Treat the result of failure of this RR as if it were a failed Fear RR. Normally, it will have an effect in a 50' radius. On missiles or thrown weapons, it will have an effect in a 10' radius all along the weapon’s path of flight. The wielder is immune to this effect.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.9: As Projected Mood I, except radius is 10'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.10: As Shared Mood I, except radius is 20'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.11: As Infuse Mood I, except modifier is +10 for acting in tune with the mood and -10 against the mood.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.12: As Projected Mood I, except radius is 15'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.13: Modifies an Infuse Mood spell so that the mood will only apply to some specified type of being. This can be any natural category: a species, a larger biological group (e.g., mammals or felines), males, females, Essence users, etc. It cannot be an artificial category like a nationality or members of a secret society.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.14: Allows caster to enchant an item such that the attuned wielder can cause it to have a 20' radius fear effect like that described for Frightfulness. This need not have an associated noise.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.15: As Shared Mood I, except radius is 30'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.16: As Projected Mood I, except radius is 20'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.17: As Infuse Mood I, except modifier is +15 for acting in tune with the mood and -15 against the mood.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.18: Allows caster to enchant an item so that it will inspire desire in one who falls under its enchantment to possess and keep the item. The item will seem highly desirable to those under its influence and they will act accordingly. Two castings of this spell per day of enchantment create a compulsion to use the item. Three castings create temptations to take the item by stealth or force even among those who normally would not seek to do so in the circumstances. RR is against Mentalism, with the effect starting at 1st level and increasing 1 level each time one uses the item or spends a week in its proximity, up to the item’s own level. Normally, this will affect the bearer of the item only or someone who actually touches it. A Shared Mood will allow this effect to influence anyone in the radius who sees the item. RRs need be made generally only initially, upon perceived need for the item, attempts to be rid of the item, or other occasions calling attention to the item. Once failed, an RR to shrug off the effect temporarily may be made once/ week.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.19: As Shared Mood I, except radius is 40'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.20: Allows the caster to create an item that will cause someone to feel a lasting emotion (e.g., love, hate, fear, disgust, or pity) for the next person seen after failing an RR against this effect. This can be triggered only once per person and cannot be triggered from more than 20' away. This effect is usually put into a potion, requiring only a Work Mundane Liquid spell in addition to this one. The emotion will last for 1 week for every 5 by which the RR was failed.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.25: As Infuse Mood I, except modifier is +20 for acting in tune with the mood and -20 against the mood.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.30: As Emotional Manipulation, but the effect is permanent. It is subject to normal emotional changes, but it will hold at least for one full year.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.35: As Infuse Mood I, except modifier is +25 for acting in tune with the mood and -25 against the mood.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.40: As Projected Mood I, except radius is 50'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.50: As Shared Mood I, except radius is 100'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.60: As Aura of Dread, except that the fear effect covers a 100' radius per level of the attuned wielder and it affects that wielder’s foes only.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.75: As Projected Mood I, except radius is 100'.
MOOD IMPRESSIONS.90: As Infuse Mood I, except modifier is +30 for acting in tune with the mood and -30 against the mood.

ESSENCE EMBEDDING.1: Allows caster to create an item with a single embedded ability that allows the user to freely choose among the spells embedded in that ability (e.g., a Daily II ability with two embedded first level spells would allow casting either of the spells twice in a day or both of them once, although two separate Embed I spells would still be required).
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.2: Allows caster to use an Embed # spell to embed an Essence spell list up to the level of the Embed spell’s #. Each spell to be included must be cast into the item during the enchantment, but only a single Embed spell suitable for the highest level spell from the list is required. The resulting item will permit lower level spells from the embedded list to be cast at the level of the highest level spell embedded as part of the same embedding.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.3: Allows caster to embed a 1st level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.4: Allows caster to charge a wand containing one or more Essence spells.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.5: Allows caster to embed a 2nd level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.6: Allows caster to give an item the ability to cast a 1st level Essence spell embedded in the item (using an Embed spell) once per day. Daily spells have considerable flexibility; for details see Daily/Constant Items in Section 5.3.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.7: Allows caster to embed a 3rd level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.8: Allows caster to charge a rod containing one or more Essence spells.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.9: Allows caster to embed a 4th level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.10: As Daily I, except a 3rd level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.11: Allows caster to embed a 5th level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.12: Allows caster to charge a staff containing one or more Essence spells.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.13: Allows caster to embed a 6th level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.14: As Daily I, except a 5th level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.15: Allows caster to embed a 7th level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.16: Allows caster to charge a half-bole containing one or more Essence spells.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.17: Allows caster to embed an Essence spell of up to 3rd level (in conjunction with an Embed spell) that functions constantly (or this spell may be cast twice to permit activation of the embedded spell “at will” or when triggered, see item enchantment rules for details).
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.18: As Daily I, except a 7th level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.19: Allows caster to embed a 10th level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.20: Allows caster to charge a bole containing one or more Essence spells.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.25: As Daily I, except a 10th level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.30: Allows caster to embed a 20th level or lower level Essence spell in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.35: As Constant III, except an Essence spell of up to 10th level.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.40: As Daily I, except a 20th level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.50: Allows caster to embed an Essence spell of any level in an item.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.60: As Daily I, except a 30th level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.75: As Daily I, except a 50th level Essence spell.
ESSENCE EMBEDDING.90: As Constant III, except an Essence spell of any level.

FLUID SKILLS.1: Allows caster to work with non-magical, non-toxic liquids to create an enchanted item (normally a potion). All required tools and material must be present. Alternatively, this spell can be used to work on a non-magical liquid without enchanting it, in which case the caster can do the work in half the normal time. In either case, the caster gains a +30 bonus to his relevant Crafting maneuver(s).
FLUID SKILLS.2: Caster learns the nature and origin of a natural liquid or gas, and when and how a worked liquid or gas was obtained and worked.
FLUID SKILLS.3: Allows caster to make one dose of a potion with up to 3 levels of spells embedded in it (no Embed spell is required), for example one 3rd level spell or three 1st level spells. The spells take effect at the level of the highest level spell embedded. Normally the spells will affect the imbiber, but the creator of the potion may choose when the potion is made to allow them to target others instead.
FLUID SKILLS.4: Allows caster to work with a poison of up to 5th level of potency to create an enchanted poison (usually done simply to prevent the poison from losing potency until used, although one could use a Potion spell to create a poison that also delivered a spell effect). All required tools and material must be present. Alternatively, this spell can be used to work on a poison without enchanting it, in which case the caster can do the work in half the normal time.
